Title: ICBC contributes to a $208.5 million syndicated loan in February 2016
Description: On February 17, 2016, ICBC, Indonesia Eximbank, and Permata signed a $208.5 million syndicated loan agreement with PT J Resources Nusantara (JRN), PT Sago Prima Pratama (SPP),  PT J Resources Bolaang Mongondow (JRBM), PT Gorontalo Sejahtera Mining (GSM) and PT Arafura Surya Alam (ASA) -- as onshore borrowers -- and J Resources Netherland B.V. (JBV), J Resources Gold (UK) Limited (JRGL) and Specific Resources Sdn Bdn (SRSB) as offshore borrowers.  The term of this syndicated loan facility was sixty (60) months as of the utilization date of the syndicated loan. As of December 31, 2016, total loan drawdowns (disbursements) under the loan agreement amounted to $198,500,000.
Funding_Agencies: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 10 million grant to support the Government of Burundi’s Strategic Framework for the Fight Against Poverty
Description: In 2007, the Burundian President received an RMB 10 million grant from the Chinese Government to support the Government of Burundi’s implementation of its Strategic Framework for the Fight Against Poverty. The goal of this framework is to reduce poverty in both urban and rural areas while also focusing on restoring social security and the national economy. The proceeds from this grant were used to obtain construction and transportation materials for use in Bujumbura. These materials were delivered in two batches: one on June 20, 2007 and one on August 14, 2007.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 60 million grant to Yemen —via a January 2019 ETCA—for unspecified development and humanitarian projects
Description: On January 30, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Yemen, Kang Yong, and Najib, Yemen’s Minister of Planning and International Cooperation signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) on behalf of both governments at the Saudi capital, Riyadh. The Chinese Government agreed to provide Yemen with a RMB 60 million grant in order to carry out humanitarian and development projects. Both representatives agreed to determine the specific projects under the ETCA “later on”; however they are currently unknown. Yemen’s Minister of Planning expressed Yemen’s appreciation for the People’s Republic of China’s support throughout the war. The Chinese government expressed its willingness to participate in Yemen’s post-war reconstruction while signing the agreement.

Title: Chinese Embassy's Women Group Donates fair proceeds to the Mercy of Hussein's Mother Charity
Description: On October 5, 2019, the Women's Group at the Chinese Embassy to Jordan participated in the 55th annual Mercy of Hussein's Mother charity fair. Throughout the event, they sold Chinese handicrafts and donated all proceeds to the Mother Hussein organization, which supports orphans, disabled children, and poor families. The event was held at Al-Hussein Youth City in Amman. The Women's Group also participated in this event in 2018, 2017, 2016, and 2015.

Title: China Eximbank provides RMB 310 million government concessional loan for Mpila Social Housing Construction Project (200 Units)
Description: On March 29, 2013, China Eximbank and the Republic of Congo signed an RMB 310 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Mpila Social Housing Construction Project (200 Units). This loan reportedly carried a 20-year maturity and a 5-year grace period.   The project involved the construction of 200 housing units in the Mpila neighborhood within the capital city of Brazzaville. Beijing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. (BCEG) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began in August 2013 and was completed on June 30, 2015.  There are some indications that the China Eximbank loan for the Mpila Social Housing Construction Project (200 Units) may have financially underperformed vis-a-vis the original expectations of the lender. In 2020, China Eximbank and the Republic of Congo signed a debt suspension agreement as part of the G-20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI). Under the terms of the agreement, the lender agreed to suspend principal and interest payments due between May 1, 2020 and December 31, 2020 under multiple buyer’s credit loan (BCL) agreements and multiple government concessional loan (GCL) agreements (as captured via Project ID#95566 and ID#95571).  Debt service payments under many of these loan agreements were again deferred in 2021 (as captured via Project ID#95573, 95572, 95570, and 95568). The IMF assessed the Republic of Congo to be in debt distress in 2021, 2022, and 2023.

Title: Chinese Government signs an exchange of letters on a project to the people's livelihood in Djibouti
Description: On May 7, 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Djibouti signed an exchange of letters on a project regarding cooperation on people's livelihood and societal development in Djibouti. Further details are unknown.

Title: Chinese MOFCOM provides assistance for Ethiopia with ETB 4 million worth of agricultural equipment and materials
Description: On August 16, 2019, a handover ceremony was held for China's donation of ETB 4 million worth of 136 items of agricultural equipment and materials to Ethiopia. The Chinese Agency for International Assistance (CHINAAID) provided the Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture with agricultural technology and assistance in hopes of improving Ethiopia's agricultural development capabilities, which will hopefully reduce their hunger and poverty levels.  During the ceremony, representatives of both governments signed a "Certificate of Handover of Agricultural Equipment and Materials for Ethiopia in the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia." The exact materials donated is unclear, however according to CGTN the donated materials included tractors, sowing and soil-tilling machines, rice and wheat thresher machines, cottonseed removing machine and generators.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates 10 million kyats to NGO to support orphans in Myanmar
Description: According to a report from the Chinese Embassy, on January 30, 2019, Chinese Ambassador's wife Wang Xuehong donated 10 million kyats on behalf of the embassy to Myanmar's Loving and Caring for Orphans Association. The donation will be used to help orphans in the country.

Title: China Eximbank provides $113.4 million preferential buyer’s credit for National Road No. 214 (NR 214) and 6th Cambodia-China Friendship Mekong-Stung Treng Bridge Project
Description: On February 2, 2012, China Eximbank and the Government of Cambodia signed a $113,441,875 preferential buyer’s credit( PBC) agreement for the National Road No. 214 (NR 214) and 6th Cambodia-China Friendship Mekong-Stung Treng Bridge Project. The PBC carried the following terms: 20-year maturity, 7-year grace period, and 2% interest rate. The proceeds of the PBC were to be used by the borrower to partially finance an EPC (commercial) contract between Shanghai Construction Group (SCG), which was signed on August 20, 2011.  The purpose of this project was to (a) construct a 1,731-meter bridge (the 6th Cambodia-China Friendship Bridge or Stung Treng Bridge) over the Mekong River at the Junction of NR7 & NR9 in Stung Treng, and (b) construct a 143.412 km National Road No. 214 (NR 214) that stretches from PK458 of NR 7 in Stung Treng Province to PK130 of NR 62 in Preah Vihear Province.  SCG was the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. The project was supervised by Guangzhou Wanan Construction Supervision Company. The expected duration of the construction period was 45 months.  Road construction started on May 8, 2012, and bridge construction began on April 15, 2012. The planned completion date for both the bridge and the road was November 15, 2015. On August 19, 2014, the bridge was completed and opened to traffic ahead of schedule. An official project completion ceremony for both the bride and the road was held on April 1, 2015.

Title: Chinese Government funds Grand'Anse Praslin Community Center Construction Project
Description: On May 15, 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Seychelles attended an opening ceremony for the Grand'Anse Praslin Community Center. The Chinese Embassy in Seychelles financed this project and Qingdao Construction was responsible for its implementation. The monetary value of this donation and the construction start date are unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides $500,000 USD cash grant, food, and blankets after CNMC industrial accident
Description: In 2005, the Chinese Government donated $500,000 USD and material assistance (including food and blankets) to the Government of Zambia after a fatal accident took place at a CNMC-owned BGRIMM explosives plant in the town of Kitwe. The explosion killed 51 and injured 2 others.

Title: Chinese Government cancels $66.4 million of the Government of Sudan’s outstanding repayment obligations
Description: On August 15, 2001, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sudan’s Ministry of International Cooperation signed a debt exemption protocol.  This agreement reportedly cancelled the equivalent of $66.4 million of the Government of Sudan’s outstanding debt obligations to China.

Title: Chinese embassy donates sewing machines to poor women in Kaédi area
Description: On October 25, 2017, the Chinese embassy donated sewing machines to poor women in Kaédi area._x000D_ _x000D_ The value of the donation is unknown.

Title: China donates sewing machines and other equipment to Al-Faisal Education Health and Social Compound in Lebanon in 2019
Description: According to a report from the Chinese Embassy in Lebanon, on March 27, 2019, the Chinese Government donated sewing machines and other equipment to the Al-Faisal Education Health and Social Compound in Lebanon. The equipment will help improve the center's training capabilities, the sewing skills of female trainees, the lives of local people, and create employment opportunities. The center is located in Lashaya City and provides free medical, foreign language and vocational skills training for local residents. The sewing machines donated by China will be used in the center's sewing skills training for local women, which will help improve the lives of female students or start their own businesses.

Title: China donates 3 trucks and 1 motor grader to Cambodian King's Working Group
Description: On February 2nd, 2011, the Chinese government donated agricultural machinery, including 3 trucks and 1 motor grader, to Cambodian King's working group for humanitarian activities. The handover ceremony was held at the Royal Palace , and attended by Chinese ambassador to Cambodia Pan Guangxue, Cambodian King Norodom Sihamoni, Commercial Counsellor Jin and  Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Royal Palace Affairs Gong Sangao._x000D_ _x000D_ The donated goods were provided to Cambodian King's Working Group, or Krom 'Samdech Euv' [literally mean the Father King] of King Sihanouk. Krom Samdech Euv is a poverty eradication programme. Since 1993, China has provided material assistance to the working group; supplies that had been donated include small batches of construction machinery, drilling rigs and agricultural supplies. The donation aims to assist the working group in its humanitarian activities in helping Cambodian poor people in the vast rural areas through digging ponds, building roads, constructing houses and so on.

Title: Chinese Government provides SCR 52.4 million grant for Phase 3 of Corgate Housing Project (Linked to Project ID#73585 and ID#73584)
Description: On February 26, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Seychelles signed an exchange of letters related to Phase 3 of the Corgate Housing Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of funding and it committed approximately SCR 52.4 million in total. The purpose of the Corgate Housing Project was to completely rebuild 157 outdated housing units (that were torn down) and further increase the capacity of the Corgate Housing estate to a total of 191 units (through the construction of of four blocks of 32 affordable housing units with three bedrooms each). _x000D_ _x000D_ Phase 1 (captured in Project ID#73584) involved the construction of 13 housing units and it was completed in 2008. Phase 2 (captured in Project ID#73585) involved the construction of 20 housing units and it was nearly complete as of 2015. Phase 3 (captured in Project ID#55616). involved the construction of construction of four blocks of 32 affordable housing units (with three bedrooms each) in the Corgate community within Mont Fleuri District. Phase 3 construction began on June 30, 2017, but an official groundbreaking ceremony did not take place until July 13, 2017.  _x000D_ _x000D_ China Architecture Northeast Design Institute and Shenyang Engineering Supervision Consulting were the contractors responsible for project design. Huashan International Engineering (also known as Top International Engineering Corporation) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. During a site visit in April 2018, the Seychellois Housing Minister said 16 units should have been completed by June 2018 and all the demolition was scheduled to end in December 2019. Then, on July 7, 2018, the project passed an on-site MOFCOM inspection. MOFCOM conducted another on-site inspection on September 23, 2019. Phase 3 was ultimately completed and handed over to the Government of Seychelles on August 6, 2020.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 76.7 million interest-free loan — via ETCA — for Social Housing Project (Linked to Project ID#30570)
Description: In 2016, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 70 million ($10.3 million) grant for the Government of Cape Verde for Phase 1 of the São Vicente Social Housing Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) is the source of funding. The grant proceeds were drawn from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ECTA) signed by the parties.   The project involves the construction of 88 affordable housing units in the neighborhood of Portelinha within the Ribeira de Craquinha suburb on the island of São Vicente. Each housing unit will have four floors, with two 2-bedroom apartments/condominiums on each floor. Each apartment/condominium will have two bedrooms, a bathroom, living room, a kitchen and a storage room. The project also involves the construction of social facilities — namely, green spaces, children's playground and parking. Zheng Tai Group Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for project implementation and China Urban Construction Design and Research Institute Co., Ltd is the contract responsible for project design. On January 29, 2019, a project implementation agreement was signed. Then, on December 9, 2019, a groundbreaking ceremony took place. The project was officially completed and handed over the local authorities on January 19, 2022. This project was originally expected to reach completion in 2021

Title: Chinese Government donates tents, electricity generators, medical equipment, and bedding materials worth RMB 20 million
Description: In 2006, the Chinese Government donated humanitarian relief to Lebanon in the midst of a conflict with Israel. The aid package was worth RMB 20 million ($2.5 million) and it consisted of 150 tents, electricity generators, medical equipment, and bedding. The equipment arrived in Beirut on August 11, 2006.   Then, on September 18, 2006, Chinese Premier Wen Jiabao announced that his government would provide an additional RMB 20 million of material assistance to Lebanon. However, it is unclear whether or when this pledged donation was fulfilled.

Title: China donates supplies to the Eastern Province of Rwanda
Description: On November 24, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda, Rao Hongwei, donated supplies including cement, sewing machines, desks, and bags, etc. to the Rwamagana region in Eastern Province, Rwanda. This donation is aimed to improve the livelihood of the poor, women, and children. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese embassy and other organizations donates a vehicle and assorted items to the Clar Hope Foundation in 2021
Description: On October 12th, 2021, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia, Ren Yisheng, donated a huge consignment of assorted materials along with a 15 – seater mini-bus to the Liberian First Lady’s Clar Hope Foundation. He named the items as several cartoons of noodles, clothes, academic materials, 200 pieces of tablet computers and kits-of-love-bags for children among others.  The All-China Women Federation, China Disabled Persons Federation and the China Charity Foundation and other institutions contributed to this donation.

Title: Chinese Embassy provides donation for 8 livelihood projects in Guyana
Description: On September 28, 2020, a handover ceremony was held for a donation of an unspecified amount of funds from the Chinese Embassy to the President of Guyana (Source ID #157173). According to the Chinese Embassy, this aid is intended to fund 8 "small livelihood projects" in Guyana. The breakdown of these projects and their values is unknown.

Title: Myanmar Chinese Chamber of Commerce donates relief supplies for fire victims in Yangon jointly with Chinese Embassy (linked to #38438)
Description: In December 2005, the Chinese Embassy in Myanmar as well as the Myanmar Chinese Chamber of Commerce donated a bulk of relief materials to fire victims left homeless through a recent major fire in Yangon. The relief materials included clothing, daily necessities and medicines.   While the total value of the supplies was said to be worth 15 million kyat, the value of the donation performed by the Chinese firms in unknown.

Title: China Eximbank provides $90 million seller's credit to CWE for Upper West Regional Electrification Project
Description: On October 22, 2010, the Government of Ghana and China International Water and Electric Corporation (CWE) signed an $90 million supplier credit agreement for the Upper West Regional Electrification Project. This credit has a 14.5 year year maturity. Its final maturity date is April 30, 2025. The loan’s (principal) amount outstanding was GHS 211,230,000 ($37,719,642) as of December 31, 2020 and GHS 154,600,000 ($29,730,769) as of December 31, 2021.  In order to finance its supplier credit agreement with the Government of Ghana, CWE secured an export seller’s credit from China Eximbank.   The purpose of this project was to extend electricity to 400 communities in the Upper West Region. It was expected, upon completion, to benefit about 300,000 people across the nine districts within the Upper West Region, creating 30 permanent jobs and 200 temporary jobs to serve as an ingredient needed for the socio-economic development of the beneficiary communities.   CWE was the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. It signed an EPC contract on March 8, 2011. Construction began in October 2011, and an official groundbreaking ceremony was held on or around November 18, 2011. This project was eventually completed, but its exact date of completion is unknown.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates relief supplies for fire victims in Yangon jointly with Chinese firms (linked to #39308)
Description: In December 2005, the Chinese Embassy in Myanmar as well as the Myanmar Chinese Chamber of Commerce donated a bulk of relief materials to fire victims left homeless through a recent major fire in Yangon. The relief materials included clothing, daily necessities and medicines.   While the total value of the supplies was said to be worth 15 million kyat, the value of the donation by the Embassy is unknown. The project is linked to #39308.

Title: Bank of China leads a $450 million syndicated loan to Food Investment SpA for the acquisition of Australis Seafoods
Description: On June 5, 2019, Food Investment SpA — a special purpose vehicle and subsidiary of the Legend Holdings Corporation-owned Joyvio Agriculture Development Co. (or ‘Joyvio Group’) — signed a $450 million syndicated loan agreement with a group of banks for the acquisition of up to 100% of Australis Seafoods S.A. (a major participant in the Chilean salmon industry). Members of the loan syndicate included the Macau Branch of Bank Of China Limited (mandated lead arranger, bookrunner, offshore security agent, and original lender), Beijing Haidian Sub-Branch of Bank of China Limited (lead signed registrar, book runner, PRC security agent, and original lender), Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone Branch of China Minsheng Banking Corp., Ltd. (mandated lead arranger and original lender), and Tai Fung Bank Limited (lead arranger and original creditor). Then, on October 18, 2019, Australis Seafoods S.A. issued a corporate guarantee in support of the loan that was issued to Food Investment SpA. Joyvio Group, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Legend Holdings, executed the acquisition of an 94.47% equity stake Australis Seafoods S.A.  for $880 million in January 2019. Joyvio Group claimed that the acquisition will guarantee consistent supply of salmon, optimizing its supply chain and allowing it to effectively serve its customers as the demand for salmon increases.

Title: Chinese Ministry of Commerce covers expenses for five Angolan officials to participate in hybrid rice technology training in China
Description: On June 1, 2011, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce announced it would be covering expenses for five Angolan officials from the Angolan Ministry of Agriculture to participate in a Hybrid Rice Technology Training Course for Portuguese-speaking Countries. The training was held in Hunan Province, China, from 1 June to 20 September 2011. Expenses including international round trip between Angola and China, accommodation, and food in China were covered._x000D_ _x000D_ The exact cost of these expenses is unclear.

Title: Chinese Government donates rice machines, tractors, and bulldozers worth $5 million (Linked to Project ID#49129)
Description: On December 17, 2015, the Chinese Government officially delivered $5 million worth of agricultural machinery — including rice machines, tractors, and bulldozers — to the Government of Fiji. This donation provided supplemental support for Phase 1 of the Rice Revitalization Project (captured via Project ID#49129).  The Chinese Government also sent mechanical experts to train Fijians on the use and maintenance of the machinery. The purpose of Phase 1 of the Rice Revitalization Project was to increase rice production in the Dreketi irrigated areas within Muanicula province on the island of Vanua Levu. It also supported the Koronivia Rice Research Center (also known as Koronivia Research Station) in Nasinu.

Title: China Development Bank pledges to loan $500 million USD for setting up the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank
Description: According to the International Food Policy Research Institute (p. 13), in March 2009, the chairman of China Development Bank (CDB) visited Tanzania and signed a framework cooperation agreement with the head of the Bank of Tanzania regarding the establishment of the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB). CDB conducted a pre-feasibility study shortly thereafter. On October 27, 2009, the Tanzanian and Chinese governments announced plans to set up the bank. Their plans included CDB setting aside $500 million USD of capital to support local farmers utilize the bank. The loan terms are unknown. However, the Chinese side were hesitant since the politicians running Tanzanian government banks have a reputation for not repaying loans.   The bank opened in May 2012, but funding for the bank appears to have come from entirely from the Tanzanian government, not China. According to Africanfarming.net, Tanzania provided $48 million USD every year for 8 years. It does not appear as though the Chinese government followed through on its initial pledge to support the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank.

Title: China grants food aid assistance of Central African Republic
Description: On July 17, 2017, the Chinese ambassador signed over a food aid agreement to the Central African Republic's Ministry of Economic Planning and International Cooperation. The agreement marked the handover of a batch of food aid to the Central African Republic. The value of the aid is unclear.

Title: Chinese Government donated 10 tons of rice and 2 truckloads of canned goods to the typhoon victims in the Philippines in 2018
Description: On September 28, 2018, the Consulate of the People's Republic of China in Laoag City donated 10 tons of premium rice and two truckloads of canned goods to the victims of Typhoon "Ompong" in Ilocos Norte in the Philippines. The Vice Governor, along with provincial board members Domingo Ambrocio and Donald Nicolas, received the donation. The 10 tons of premium rice were valued at P480,000.00 and various grocery items such as sardines, corned beef, and meat loaf were valued at P297,000.00, and were to be distributed during the "Paspas Takder" relief operations.

Title: Chinese Government funds Modern Agricultural Center Reconstruction Project (Linked to Project #56272, #56148)
Description: In 2005, China and Dominica started the China-Dominica Agriculture Technical Cooperation Project (#56148). This project includes the construction of an agricultural demonstration center with necessary facilities. The former demonstration center was located in Hillsborough between 2005 and 2011, which was completely destroyed by flood in 2011 (#56272). Then the new Modern Agricultural Centre (also referred as 'China-Dominica Horticulture Demonstrative Center') was reconstructed at One Mile, Portsmouth in partnership with the Chinese Agricultural Mission.The project cost approximately 2.1 million USD and was launched during AgriFest on May 17, 2014 in One Mile Portsmouth. The facilities serve purposes including the training of farmers and include a propagation area for different type of plants, according to a government statement. The exact amount of financing from the Chinese government is unknown.

Title: China provides 20 million RMB in agricultural assistance to Mongolia
Description: On January 12, 2007 Chinese and Mongolian officials signed an agricultural assistance agreement, with China providing tractors and other irrigation facilities worth 20 million RMB (2.56 million U.S dollars) to Mongolia. Chinese Ambassador Gao Shumao signed the agreement with Mongolia's Agriculture Minister Dendev Terbishdagva.

Title: China grants Barbados funds for agricultural projects via November 2019 ETCA (linked to #72076, #54831, #72077, #72081, and #72079)
Description: On November 29, 2019, the Charge d’Affaires for the Chinese Embassy in Barbados signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with the Barbadian Minister of Education, Technological and Vocational Training for two of China's agricultural projects in Barbados. The amount of funding provided through this agreement is unknown, though a December 2019 article from the Barbados Advocate reports a "recent" increase in funding for the two projects from BDS $14.5 million to BDS $29 million. The grant funds will be used for two agricultural projects in Barbados that cost a total of BDS $45 million:    1)The first is the Hope Agricultural Training Institute, detailed in Project ID #54831, located at at Hope Plantation in St. Lucy, where students from multiple schools can learn up to date techniques in crop production, animal husbandry, and farm management.   2) The second is the University of the West Indies (UWI) Centre for Food Security and Entrepreneurship, detailed in Project ID #72081, which intends to facilitate innovation in agri-business and food production through the establishment of an environmentally-friendly agricultural park.   Additionally, there are three other ETCAs funding these two agricultural projects (#72077, #72079, and #72076). It is unclear exactly what the funding breakdown is between these two sub-projects.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 37.6 million grant -- via March 2004 ETCA -- for Rice Milling Machine Installation Project (Linked to Project ID#85373 and #49941)
Description: On March 24, 2004, the Chinese Government and the Government of Myanmar signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an RMB 50 million grant for multiple projects (captured via Project ID#85373). These projects included the renovation of Yangon National Cultural Theatre at a cost of RMB 12.4 million (as captured via Project ID#49941) and the Rice Milling Machine Installation Project at the cost of an estimated RMB 37.6 million (as captured via Project ID#64998).  The purpose of the project was to renovate a small rice mill manufacturing plant that is located in Malun Village, Upper Minhla Township, Thayet District, and Magway Region.    Sinomach was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project commenced on December 10, 2011 and it was completed ahead of schedule on May 10, 2012.  A project handover certificate was issued on May 10, 2012.

Title: Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences (CATAS) provides agricultural training to Rwanda
Description: Around December 9, 2018, the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences (CATAS) in partnership with the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) provided training on modern farming technologies to district agronomists, Farmer Field School (FFS) facilitators, and other agriculture field staff. The 2-week training course on cultivation and processing technologies of tropical crops, including cassava cultivation and processing, bananas, mushrooms, maize, rice and related processing technologies, took place at Rubona Research Station of the Rwanda Agriculture Board in Huye District, Rwanda. On December 23, 2018, a closing ceremony was held for the training. During the closing, the Director-General of RAB said they recently signed a memorandum of understanding with China for sharing experiences, knowledge and technologies so as to improve agricultural yields, enhancing value addition and other technologies needed in handling post-harvest losses. The goal of the exchange is to reduce post-harvest loss from 16% to 5% by 2024.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 10th Agricultural Technical Assistance Mission to Cote d'Ivoire (Linked to Project ID#66174, #66171, #66160, #70502)
Description: In late December 2017, Chinese and Ivorian officials signed an agreement to initiate the 10th Chinese Agricultural Technical Assistance Mission (MATAC or Mission d'Assistance Technique Agricole Chinoise) from 2018 to 2020 in Guiguidou, a rice reclamation area spanning 432 hectares near Divo in Lôh-Djiboua region. 8 experts were dispatched to carry out training workshops and research. At least four new high-yield and high-quality rice varieties were cultivated. The 10th Agricultural Technical Assistance Mission to Cote d'Ivoire also donated agricultural machinery in 2019 (as captured via Project ID#66171).   In 1995, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire launched the Guiguidou farmland water conservancy project, and in May 1997, an agricultural rice technology cooperation project was launched in which Chinese experts work in Guiguidou with Ivorian farmers to promote agriculture — especially rice farming. The MATAC teams from Liaoning International have worked with the Government Cote d'Ivoire's Agency for Rice Development and National Agency for Rural Development in 2-year-long phases (as captured via Project ID#66175, #66160, #70502). Between 1997 and 2013, 7 technical assistance missions were carried out. Each team had a mechanization expert, an agronomy expert, an interpreter, and an accountant and they lived in a ‘city’ in Guiguidou made up of dormitories, offices, experimental laboratories, and a machine repair garage.

Title: Chinese Government donates food aid worth RMB 100 million
Description: In September 2017, the Chinese government provided 17,000 tons of wheat in food aid worth 100 million yuan. The aid was given in response to an estimated 7.88 million people in Ethiopia in need of food assistance. The food was distributed to Oromia, Amhara, Farr, Harald, and Southern States in Ethiopia. _x000D_ _x000D_ The UNOCHA Financial Tracking System reported a flow of 15 million USD from China to Ethiopia for bilateral food support, which is probably referring to the same flow (Flow ID: 165586).

Title: Grant from Yunnan Provincial government for an animal food production factory in Oudomxay.
Description: Yunnan Provincial government of China provided a grant for an animal food production factory in Oudomxay in Laos.

Title: Chinese Government provides grant for Affiniam Dam Rehabilitation Project
Description: On July 21, 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Senegal signed letters of exchange related to the Affiniam Dam Rehabilitation Project. This project was funded from the grant proceeds in an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) the Chinese Government and the Government of Senegal signed on November 18, 2016.    This project involved the rehabilitation of Affiniam Dam, which is located about 20 kilometers northwest of Ziguinchor. China Railway N°8 Engineering Company (CREC8) was the contractor responsible for implementation. A  groundbreaking ceremony for the project was organized on November 20, 2019 and it was originally anticipated that the project implementation period would be 7 months. However, the project was completed and handed over on September 18, 2020. According to Senegalese media - Teranga News, the project was completed at an estimated cost of 52,605,001 Yuan.   The Chinese project title is 阿菲尼亚姆水坝修缮项目. The French project title is la réhabilitation du barrage d’Affiniam. The Affiniam Anti-Salt Dam was completed in 1988 with financial support of China. It is estimated to have cost about FCFA 10 billion (approximately $21 million). Its construction allowed for the protection of about 12,000 hectares of potential rice-growing lands from salt intrusion.

Title: Chinese government provides AUD 0.7 million for Kiritimati Copra Mill project
Description: In the government of Kiribati's 2022 Development Budget, presented on November 30th, 2021 it was stated that China will provide AUD 0.7 million for the Kiritimati Copra mill project. Copra is dried white coconut meat from which coconut oil can be extracted. Copra is milled to extract coconut oil, which is one of Kiribati's largest exports. Building a copra mill on Kiritimati was identified as a goal in the Asian Development Bank's 2008-2011 Kiribati Development Plan. Kiritimati, also known as Christmas Island, is part of the Line Islands chain and the second most populous island in Kiribati after Tarawa.

Title: China grants $1 million USD to WFP for food security in Pakistan
Description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID #165560), on 23 August 2017, the Chinese government donated $1 million USD to the World Food Programme (WFP) making it the first United Nations entity in Pakistan to receive bilateral funds from the China. The financing was specifically sourced from the China South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund. The money supported an operation called Transition: Toward Resilience and Food-Secure Pakistan which aims to feed displaced populations after years of deteriorating socio-economic and environmental conditions. _x000D_ _x000D_ According to a December 2017 WFP press release, this $1 million USD donation targeted 158,000 residents of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA). It bought 60 mt of iodized salt, 110 mt of LNS or Mamta, 305 mt of yellow split peas, and 291 mt of vegetable oil. _x000D_

Title: Chinese Embassy in Côte d’Ivoire donates agricultural machinery to the Prime Minister
Description: From December 6 to 9, 2018, at the invitation of the Chairman of Ivory Coast Region and Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research Marbury, Ambassador Tang Weibin attended the second Nihidaley Economic and Trade Cultural Festival in the region as a special guest. At the official ceremony of the Nihidaley Economic, Trade and Cultural Festival on December 8, Ambassador Tang donated a batch of agricultural machinery to Prime Minister Coulibaly and Minister Marbury on behalf of the embassy. The value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese government grants $500,000 through the WFP to Niger for food security in 2010
Description: In July 2010, the Chinese government donated USD 500,000 to the government of Niger through the World Food Programme (WFP). The grant was meant to help improve the nutritional status and reinforce livelihoods of vulnerable populations in Niger.

Title: China grants $500,000 for provision of Humanitarian Air Services
Description: On January 22, 2010, China granted $500,000 for the provision of Humanitarian Air Services in response to the earthquake in Haiti.  The purpose of the grant is to provide aircraft support to enable the humanitarian community to implement emergency relief activities into areas inaccessible by surface means and to transport humanitarian workers and relief cargo such as medical supplies, shelter, high energy foods, and ICT equipment. It will also provide capacity for timely assessments and evacuations. The UN World Food Program helped with project implementation.   The total amount committed and disbursed to the project was $18,823,513, with funding from China and multiple other countries and organizations. Co-financiers included the UN Central Emergency Response Fund, the European Community Humanitarian Aid Office (now Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations), the UN World Food Program, Canada's Foreign Affairs, Trade, and Development Agency (now Global Affairs Canada), and the governments of Switzerland, Spain, the United States, Denmark, Japan, Sweden, and the UK.

Title: China pledges new agricultural training event for Barbados
Description: On August 22, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Barbados and the Barbadian Minister of Agriculture and Food Security met at the Barbadian Ministry headquarters at Graeme Hall, Christ Church and discussed a new visit to China for a delegation from the Barbadian agricultural sector. The Barbadian Permanent Secretary of the Ministry was also present. According to the Barbadian Government Information Service, the delegation would be provided training on modern agricultural techniques and technologies. Details on the implementation and cost of this program are unknown. As of October 2021, there are no evidence such delegation has taken place.

Title: Chinese Government donates 802 tons of rice to help internally displaced persons in Central African Republic
Description: On July 17, 2017, the Chinese Embassy held an emergency assistance ceremony for the provision of 802 tons of rice to the Central African Republic. The estimated monetary value of this donation is $336,799.90. The purpose of the donation was to provide emergency assistance to displaced people and alleviate the food shortage, products of the Central African Republic's civil war.

Title: Chinese Government provides grant for Phase 2 of Juncao Mushroom Technical Cooperation Project (Linked to Project ID#49135)
Description: In December 2017, the Juncao Mushroom Technical Cooperation Project entered into its second phase. Through this phase, experts provided technical demonstration, training, and promotion to farmers in Fiji. More than 900 Fijian farmers will attend the training courses. This phase was also funded by the Chinese Government, though the grant commitment (transaction) amount unknown. The project was meant to kickstart mushroom production in Fiji and supply feed to livestock husbandry in the dry season. It was expected to assist Fiji in developing the Juncao industry and raise Fijian farmers' income.   As of the end of 2018, more than 1,000 farmers and technicians had been trained and more than 20,000 substrate tubes and 200,000 roots of Juncao grass had been distributed to Fijian farmers. The project also created a production line for mushrooms at the demonstration arm – from seedlings to packaging and storage – with an annual production capacity of 300 tons of fresh mushrooms.

Title: Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region donates cars and agricultural machinery worth 2.5 million RMB to Myanmar
Description: In early April 2005, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region committed to donating cars and agricultural machinery worth a total of 2.5 million RMB to the Government of Myanmar (p. 384). It is unclear when these goods were delivered.

Title: Chinese Government donates 43,904 metric tons of wheat in 2001
Description: According to Chinese Government reporting to the World Food Program’s International Food Aid Information System (INTERFAIS), the Chinese Government donated and delivered 43,904 metric tons of wheat (in twelve separate deliveries of 573 tons, 579 tons, 1370 tons, 1586 tons, 4037 tons, 5157 tons, 3319 tons, 4406 tons, 4008 tons, 4066 tons, 3534 tons, and 11269 tons) to North Korea in 2001.  To estimate the monetary value of the wheat donation ($4,806,170.88), AidData takes the international price of a ton of wheat in January 2001 ($109.47) and multiplies it by 43,904 tons.

Title: Chinese and Rwandan governments sign an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement in January 2009 (linked to #2009 and #2010)
Description: On January 14, 2009, the governments of China and Rwanda signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement in which China will give free assistance to Rwanda for development. A number of projects were financed through this agreement; however, the exact projects financed are unknown. However, two likely projects that were signed on the same day are captured below:_x000D_ _x000D_ Chinese financing for the construction and operationalization of the cement factory (CIMERWA) at Bugarama (captured in #2009)_x000D_ Chinese financing for the construction and operationalization of a rice processing plant in Rwamagana (captured in #2010)_x000D_ _x000D_ Additional projects, as well as the financing amount or type are unknown.

Title: China assists the construction of a farm tool assembly plant in Niger
Description: According to a report in 2005, a farm tool assembly plant was constructed in Niger with the assistance of the Chinese government. The commitment year, implementing organization, and financial value for this project remain unknown.

Title: China donates $3.2 million USD to WFP for emergency food aid in Chad (Linked to #55819)
Description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID 157202), on 17 April 2017, the Chinese government committed a total of $4 million USD to the World Food Programme (WFP) for emergency food assistance in Chad. Of the $4 million USD, $3,213,308 USD was allocated toward an emergency operation (ID 200777) "providing life-saving support to households in Cameroon, Chad, and Niger directly affected by insecurity in northern Nigeria." The remaining $786,692 USD is captured in project #55819. This donation is marked as fully paid.  The Chinese government officially handed over the food donation to the Government of Chad on 7 June 2017. According to WFP press releases, this donation helped feed nearly 60,000 people in the Lake Chad region. Page 60 of the operation's Standard Project Report 2017 says the Chinese aid specifically purchased corn soya blend, rice, split peas, vegetable oil, and millet.

Title: China donates social welfare materials to Togo charity in 2015
Description: On December 16, 2015, the Chinese Ambassador, on behalf of the overseas Chinese community living in Togo, officially donated social welfare materials to a national relief center in Togo. The materials, which included toys and food, were then distributed to disadvantaged groups as a Christmas present. The value of this donation is unknown.

Title: China and Ethiopia sign Memorandum of Understanding for humanitarian assistance, bamboo center, and commodity purchases (linked to #71688 & #88911)
Description: During the FOCAC Summit held on September 1-3 2018, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Chinese President Xi Jinping, alongside their foreign ministers had signed a Memorandum of Understanding for the following items to be completed: China to provide 50 million RMB in food aid/assistance (#71688), construction of a Bamboo Cultivation and Training Center (#88911), and for China to purchase Ethiopian Beans.

Title: Chinese Agricultural Mission trains farmers of Castle Bruce [linked to Project #56170 & #56148]
Description: In 2015, Chinese Agricultural Mission handed over a greenhouse to the farmers of Castle Bruce as a gift to Dominica (#56170). The mission also provides seedlings and trained farmers in seedling production and farming techniques. Farmers and extension officers of the Ministry of Agriculture underwent an eight-week course in crop husbandry and tractor operation and maintenance and awarded certificates of completion on Wednesday, September 21.

Title: Chinese Government provides training for 25 members of Angola's agricultural sector
Description: From July 11-31, 2018, 25 members of Angola's agricultural sector, including members of the Angolan Ministry of Agriculture, various agricultural research institutes, and agricultural institutions in various provinces attended the "2018 Angola Modern Agricultural Development Seminar" (Chinese: "2018年安哥拉现代农业发展研修班") hosted by the Chinese Government in Shaanxi Province at the Yangling Agricultural High-tech Industry Demonstration Zone.  A farewell ceremony was hosted on July 8, 2018. Cui Aimin, Ambassador to Angola, Pinto, Secretary of State for Agriculture in Angola, and the Director of the Human Resources Department of the Ministry of Agriculture for Angola attended. The financial value of the training is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government grants multi-purpose cargo vessel worth USD 3.54 million to Fiji
Description: On July 11, 2004, China agreed to grant Fiji a multi-purpose fishing vessel. Prime Minister Laisenia Qarase along with Fisheries Minister Konisi Yabaki requested the Chinese National Fisheries Corporation, the largest Chinese government-owned fishing corporation, for a fishing vessel. It was proposed that the vessel will be used as a research and training facility and also to transport catch from the outer islands. On August 8, 2006, the Fiji Ministry of Fisheries and Forestry and Wuhan Changjiang Ship Design Institue (CSDI) signed the Memorandum of Understanding for the design of the ship. On September 11, 2006, the Ambassador of the Embassy of China in Fiji visited the CSDI to exchange ideas about the project. _x000D_ _x000D_ On June 15, 2010, the China Assistance Fiji Multi-Purpose Ship Construction Contract with Wuhan Nanhua High-speed Ship Engineering Co., Ltd to build the ship was signed at the Prime Minister's Office in Fiji by the Permanent Secretary of the Prime Minister's Office of Fiji, Pio Ticdu Adua, and the temporary head of the Economic and Commercial Counsellor's Office of the Chinese Embassy, ​​Yang Xuegang. The vessel cost USD 3.54 million, which was funded through a Chinese Government grant. The vessel would be used mainly for the transport of frozen fish, fresh fish on ice, dry and sundry goods in Fiji among the main island and offshore islands. _x000D_ _x000D_ On December 21, 2011, construction was completed and the new multi-purpose cargo vessel "Bai-Ni-Takali," measuring 36.8m long and 8m wide, arrived in Suva on her delivery voyage from China. Fiji's Minister of Primary Industries Joketani Cokanasiga and Chinese Ambassador to Fiji Huang Yong signed the acceptance agreement at the hand-over ceremony held at the Narayan Jetty in Suva._x000D_ _x000D_ Personnel from the Department of Fisheries received two months of training in China. However, the vessel has had some operating problems. Mistakes were made because the instructions were in Chinese and could not be read by the crew. Documents have now been provided in English and Chinese engineers will be sent if the vessel can’t be fixed locally.

Title: China sends agriculture experts for technology training
Description: China has sent experts on agricultural machinery and equipment to Timor-Leste to conduct training in the maintenance of agricultural technology. This small pilot project ran from November 2013 to December 2014. Specifically, the project taught Timorese farmers the knowledge and skills to increase production of maize.

Title: China Eximbank provides $85.7 million buyer’s credit loan for for Phase 1 of Caxito, Gandjelas, Luena, and Wako-Kungo Irrigation System Project (Linked to Project ID#34898, #42029)
Description: On November 28, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Angolan Government signed a framework agreement pertaining to a special economic cooperation arrangement (Agreement name in Chinese: 中华人民共和国商务部与安哥拉共和国财政部关于两国经贸合作特殊安排的框架协议).  Following the signing of the framework agreement, on March 2, 2004, China Eximbank entered into a $2 billion Master Loan Facility Agreement (MLFA) with the Government of Angola. All borrowings under the MLFA, which is an oil prepayment facility,  carried the following estimated borrowing terms: a 21.5 maturity, a 1.5 year grace period, an interest rate of 3-month LIBOR plus a 1.5% margin, a 0.3% management fee, and a 0.3% commitment fee.  The facility was split between a $1.0 billion Phase I facility and a $1.0 billion Phase II facility.  Availability of the Phase II facility was subject to confirmation by the lender on or prior to the date falling five years after satisfaction of the conditions precedent to the MLFA and was made available by China Eximbank during that period.  The MLFA is a framework agreement under which the Government of Angola and China Eximbank may conclude individual buyer’s credit loan agreements (ILAs or subsidiary loan agreements) for the purpose of financing up to 90% of the contract price owing to certain contractors in respect of certain contracts.  The first tranche of the facility was released in December 2004.  The facility was fully drawn down as of December 31, 2017.  Sonangol provided a source of collateral under the MLFA, and repayments were made with the proceeds of oil sales from Sonangol to UNIPEC (China international United Petroleum & Chemicals Co. Ltd, Sinopec group), which were deposited in an Angolan Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) account at China Eximbank.  The volume of oil to be sold to UNIPEC each month for repayment of the loan varied according to market oil prices.  Under the agreement, 70% of works have to be contracted with Chinese companies and the same proportion of construction material, equipment and labour has to be contracted in China.  Loan disbursements were made on a project-by-project basis.  Tendering, management and payments were jointly managed by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the Angolan Ministry of Finance (which coordinated the various Angolan line ministries responsible for supervising the projects).   The Angolan Ministry of Finance submitted the projects for tendering; China Eximbank selected Chinese candidate firms for the projects; and a joint commission made the final firm selections. The process was managed by an office in the Angolan Ministry of Finance -- known as Gabinete de Apoio Técnico (GAT) -- that was specifically created to manage the MLFA with China Eximbank.  In March 2005, China Eximbank and the Government of Angola signed a $85,775,400.00 subsidiary buyer’s credit loan agreement under the MLFA for Phase 1 of the Caxito, Gandjelas, Luena, and Wako-Kungo Irrigation System Project.  The proceeds of the loan were used to partially finance a $95,306.000.00 commercial (EPC) contract with Sinohydro, which was signed on March 2, 2005.    The purpose of this project, which employed 307 Angolan workers and 72 Chinese workers, was to construct irrigation systems in the locality of Caxito within Bengo Province, the locality of Gandjelas within Huila Province, the locality of Luena within Moxico Province, and the locality of Wako-Kungo within Kwanza Sul Province.  Sinohydro was the EPC contractor responsible for project implementation. The EPC contract supporting the project went into effect on July 28, 2005 and the originally scheduled project handover date was August 31, 2007.  According to the Angola’s Ministry of Finance, the project was completed as of June 30, 2008.

Title: CDB provides $20 million loan to Georgia's JSC Partnership Fund
Description: On March 20, 2019, China Development Bank signed an agreement to provide a $20 million loan to the state-owned investment fund, JSC Partnership in Georgia. The Framework Agreement on Cooperation envisions an increase in the loan to 50 million by 2020. The first round of talks between the fund and the bank has been completed. The China Development Bank will issue the loan without a state guarantee, which is the first precedent for state-owned companies in Georgia. The funds will go to the investment portfolio of the Partnership Fund, which will then be allocated to various projects. Historically, the JSC Partnership Fund has promoted investment in Georgia by providing co-financing (e.g., equity, mezzanine) in projects at their initial stage of development via special purpose vehicles. The main areas of investment for the fund are power generation, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing (Source: p. 113 in "PUBLIC–PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP MONITOR SECOND EDITION").  Prior to the loan agreement, on the 21st and 22nd of December 2015, a Georgian delegation led by David Saganelidze, head of the state-owned shareholding company the Partnership Fund, met officials from Chinese financial institutions to discuss the prospects for future cooperation. The general director of the China Development Bank also promised to financially support Chinese companies that invested in Georgia’s infrastructural or energy projects. On January 25, 2017, Saganelidze noted at his meeting with businessmen at the Employers Association that the Partnership Fund of Georgia planned to sign an agreement with China Development Bank to authorize the latter to enter all projects of the Partnership Fund.  Despite the agreement envisioning an increase in the loan to 50 million by 2020, there is no proof of this development.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 200 million grant — through ETCA — for Nouakchott Olympic Stadium Renovation Project and Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Project (Linked to Project ID#52290 and #32636)
Description: On September 14, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an RMB 200 million grant for the Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Project and an Nouakchott Olympic Stadium Renovation Project. The Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Project is captured in Project ID#32636. The Olympic Stadium Renovation Project is captured in Project ID#52290.

Title: China Provides Training Experts in Agriculture for Tanzania
Description: In a June 23, 2006 statement, Wen Jiabao promised to provide agriculture experts to Tanzania to train Tanzanian experts. In 2008, the Chinese embassy in Tanzania confirmed that three experts had been dispatched to the Tanzanian Ministry of Agriculture. Two of the experts focused on promotion of advanced techniques and nontraditional crops (for example, soybeans); one was an irrigation expert. The value of this project and exact start and end dates are still unknown.

Title: Chinese Government grants USD 140 million to the Cambodian Government to aid with urgent development projects in October 2020
Description: On October 12, 2020, the Chinese Government provided the Cambodian Government with USD 140 million to be used towards its urgent development projects. The grant is expected to be allocated towards projects in Sihanoukville, including the Hong Kong submarine fiber optic cable, the National Road 71C, the rural power transmission line, and the boosting of rice production and export. Additionally, the grant is expected to be used to increase irrigation and flood protection projects in Kampong Speu province’s Prek Tnaot River, and to upgrade National Roads 41, 33, and 31.

Title: China donates first batch of food aid worth 8.5 million RMB to Djibouti following the 2011-2012 East Africa drought (Linked to #85132, #59621)
Description: Between July 2011 and mid-2012, a severe drought affected the entire East African region causing severe food shortages in countries like Djibouti. In response, on August 15, 2011, Premier Wen Jiabao announced that the Chinese government would donate food aid to Djibouti worth 50 million RMB. It was delivered in two batches: one on November 13, 2011 and another on December 18, 2011 (project #85132). The first batch, worth 8.5 million RMB, included 1,000 tons of flour and 40,000 boxes of soybean oil. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service records this donation in flow ID #87767.  Project #59621 captures another batch of Chinese emergency food aid in support of Djiboutian drought victims worth 10 million RMB.

Title: The 7th Chinese medical team donates food and medical assistance to orphanage in South Sudan (link to #59020)
Description: On December 22, 2019, China's seventh medical team donated milk, biscuits and provided medical consultations to minors at Confident Children out of Conflict (CCC), a Juba-based orphanage for vulnerable children lacking parental care. The total value of this donation is unknown. _x000D_ _x000D_ See project #59020 for details about the team's general mission.

Title: China Donates 1,280 tons rice to Niger (Linked to #58645)
Description: On 5 July 2012, Chinese ambassador to Niger, Xia Huang, donated 1,182 tons of rice to address food insecurity in Niger. The Chinese donation is dedicated to reinforcing the country’s cereal stock which was depleted after poor harvests in 2011, through the filling of warehouses of the Niger Food Product Office (OPVN). Title: Chinese Ministry of Agriculture and Huila Province partner to create Center for Research and Training in Biogas in Lubango and train farmers
Description: On December 11, 2019, an agreement was signed between China and Angola, which provides for the creation of the Center for Research and Training in Biogas in a partnership between the Biogas Institute of the Chinese Ministry of Agriculture (BIOMA) and Universidade Mandume ya Ndemufayo at the Universidade Mandume ya Ndemufayo in Lubango, Angola. Its campus is located at ISPH-UMN, in the city of Lubango, the regional capital of Huila, in the southern part of Angola. The new center will enable the implementation of joint (China-Angola) research projects and technological innovation in the field of biogas as well as the exchange of personnel for training and research. On the same day, the center was officially established.  The new institute should thus train Angolans, especially those living in the rural areas of the Huila region. In this part of the country, which is partly mountainous, the land is fertile and the people in rural areas are mainly engaged in agriculture. They produce cereals, vegetables, legumes, fruits and roots.  The new Biogas Research and Training Centre is supported by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).

Title: Tai Fung Bank participates in a $450 million syndicated loan to Food Investment SpA for the acquisition of Australis Seafoods
Description: On June 5, 2019, Food Investment SpA — a special purpose vehicle and subsidiary of the Legend Holdings Corporation-owned Joyvio Agriculture Development Co. (or ‘Joyvio Group’) — signed a $450 million syndicated loan agreement with a group of banks for the acquisition of up to 100% of Australis Seafoods S.A. (a major participant in the Chilean salmon industry). Members of the loan syndicate included the Macau Branch of Bank Of China Limited (mandated lead arranger, bookrunner, offshore security agent, and original lender), Beijing Haidian Sub-Branch of Bank of China Limited (lead signed registrar, book runner, PRC security agent, and original lender), Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone Branch of China Minsheng Banking Corp., Ltd. (mandated lead arranger and original lender), and Tai Fung Bank Limited (lead arranger and original creditor). Then, on October 18, 2019, Australis Seafoods S.A. issued a corporate guarantee in support of the loan that was issued to Food Investment SpA. Joyvio Group, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Legend Holdings, executed the acquisition of an 94.47% equity stake Australis Seafoods S.A. for $880 million in January 2019. Joyvio Group claimed that the acquisition will guarantee consistent supply of salmon, optimizing its supply chain and allowing it to effectively serve its customers as the demand for salmon increases.

Title: Chinese Government donates 1,000 tons of rice worth $1.02 million USD to North Korea in 2018 (Linked to Project ID#63132)
Description: From May 7, 2018 to May 8, 2018, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with North Korean Kim Jong-Un in Dalian, China. It was widely reported at the time that the Chinese Government would promise a new aid package to North Korea during the meeting. Then, in July 2018, the Chinese Government donated 1,000 tons of rice worth $1.02 million to the Government of North Korea (captured via Project ID#63061). By October 2018, the Chinese Government had also donated 162,007 tons of urea fertilizer worth $55.03 million to the Government of North Korea (captured via Project ID#63132).

Title: China donates food aid
Description: Chinese Ambassador to Niger, Chen Gonglai, announced that Chinese government has promised to donate 500 metric tonnes of food aid to Niger in 2006. Neither the current status of this project nor its financial value can be determined.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates food and and other aid to orphans and vulnerable children
Description: On December 18, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Togo officially donated food and non-food stuffs to 6,000 children in need. The donation was delivered to the Togolese Ministry of Social Action, Women, and Literacy Advancement. The donation consisted of 10 tons of rice, 200 boxes of tomato pasta, alimentary pastes, biscuits, detergents, tea, sandals, toys, and school supplies. The monetary value of this project is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD 700,000 via Food & Agriculture Organization of the United Nations to Kenya, Somalia and Uganda in June 2021
Description: In June 2021, Chinese government provides USD 700,000 via Food & Agriculture Organization of the United Nations as the desert locust response to mitigate impacts on food security and livelihoods in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and Uganda.

Title: Hunan Arms International Engineering Co. aids Micronesia with Pohnpei Agricultural Products Exhibition Center Project (linked to project #64026)
Description: On August 17, 2018, the opening ceremony of the China Aid Agricultural Products Exhibition Center in Pohnpei State was held. The exhibition center occupies an area of 60 square meters with a 10-meter length and a 6-meter width. The company also donates a toilet (7 square meters) and 8 exhibition desks. The construction completed on August 13, 2018..  This project was one of the missions of the 10th phase of agricultural technical assistance project (linked to project #64026). It is funded by Hunan Arms International Engineering Co (a state-owned company).
Funding_Agencies: Hunan Arms International Engineering Co., Ltd

Title: Chinese Government donates $2 million in food aid to Guinea through WFP (Linked to #45060 and #44593)
Description: On October 9, 2014 the Chinese Government signed an agreement to donate $2 million to Guinea through the World Food Program, as a part of a larger $6 million USD grant to help stave off food shortages in the three African countries worst affected by the Ebola virus. WFP China representative Brett Rierson said the money would be spent on one month of emergency food rations of mainly rice, lentils and yellow peas for 300,000 people in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. On December 24, 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Guinea, Bian Jianqia, attended a handover ceremony for the donation of 2 tons of food aid to Ebola patients in Guinea worth $2 million.  According to UN OCHA financial tracking system, China split $6 million USD equally to aid Liberia, Guinea and Sierra Leone (see projects #45060 and #44593 for the donations to Liberia and Sierra Leone). This is part of the aid package from China to three West African countries in that year in response to Ebola (#36373).

Title: China signs MoU for 800 million USD agriculture project in Haiti
Description: On October 14, 2016, China signed a memorandum of understanding with Haiti for an unspecified 800 million USD agricultural project. It is unclear what type of flow this project is. This project involves several organizations, including the China National Machinery Industry Corporation through its subsidiary, the China Automation Control System Corporation. This memorandum of understanding was signed at the same time as a 800 million USD agricultural project described in project #52641.

Title: Embassy of China in Thailand builds wells for citizens in Northern Thailand
Description: In February 25-29, 2016, the ambassador Kuiwu Ning participated in the opening ceremony of building water wells for the citizens of Northern Thailand against the drought, according to the news release from the Embassy of China in Thailand._x000D_ _x000D_ According to the same news release, Thailand was suffering from severe droughts this year and water use in some areas was relatively tight. The Chinese Embassy assisted the building of wells in several Northern provinces. Ambassador Ning came to Saraphi village to attend the well drilling ceremony. Local government officials said that the well will provide the villagers with the necessary domestic water to effectively alleviate the drought.

Title: China conducts Geopark Project Feasibility Study for Tanzania
Description: On September 30, 2017, officials from Tanzania's Ministry of Finance signed 3 letters of exchange with Chinese representatives worth 29.4 billion Tanzanian Schillings. The third agreement is for the provision of Chinese experts to study the feasibility of establishing a Geopark Project in Ngorongoro National Park, estimated at 300 million Tanzanian Schillings.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD $1 million grant for food assistance to DRC in 2012
Description: On October 21, 2012, the Chinese government provided a grant of $1,000,000 to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The grant was implemented through the World Food Programme (WFP), and was provided for emergency food assistance to newly displaced people in North Kivu and spillover into South Kivu (Kalehe and Kabare territories). This project is completed, and is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #99620.

Title: Chinese Government provides a $500,000 USD grant for locust eradication efforts
Description: On December 18, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tunisia signed a handover certificate (Chinese agreement name: 《中华人民共和国向突尼斯共和国政府提供灭蝗援助交接证书》) for $500,000 USD from the Chinese Government for locust eradication efforts in Tunisia.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 23 million grant for Phase II of the Parwan Water Conservancy Restoration Project (Linked to Project ID #34509, #34498)
Description: In 2010, the Chinese Government committed grant funding for Phase II of the Parwan Water Conservancy Restoration Project. The purpose of this project was to rehabilitate an irrigation canal in Parwan Province, which is one of the most agriculturally productive areas of Afghanistan. It involved enlarging the main canal, constructing additional gutters and retaining walls, and building fences around the Charikar pumping station and the Parwan Authority office. The total reported cost of this project is RMB 23 million. _x000D_ _x000D_ Jiangxi Water and Hydropower Construction Co., Ltd. (JWHC) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Project implementation began on December 31, 2010. The project was completed on June 15, 2012, and the formal project handover ceremony took place on August 15, 2012. _x000D_ _x000D_ The main (85.578 km) irrigation canal was originally constructed with a grant from the Chinese Government in the late 1960s and 1970s. Construction was initiated on December 31, 1968 and completed on December 31, 1976. It was designed to irrigate 24,800 hectares (or 372,000 acres) of land. However, due to the effects of war and wear and tear, the irrigation canal fell into a state of disrepair and was unable to supply water in a reliable and effective manner._x000D_ _x000D_ Phase-1 of the Parwan Conservancy project is recorded in #34509. In a news article published by the Chinese Embassy Website, the funding for the project was drawn from the US$150 million that China has pledged in 2002 and is a sub-umbrella project of #34498.

Title: Chinese government grants $6 million to WFP for Ethiopia drought relief
Description: UNOCHA indicates that on August 2017 the Chinese Government provided $3,000,000 to Ethiopia through WFP to provide assistance to refugees (Flow ID: 165361 and 165362) along with another August 2017 flow of $3,000,000 recorded in UNOCHA to respond to the humanitarian crises and enhancing resilience to food insecurity (Flow ID: 165363 and 165364).  It has been reported that in March 13, 2018, the Chinese government disbursed the $6 million to the World Food Program (WFP) in Ethiopia in response to drought conditions in the country. The WFP will use this money towards the 350,000 people living either in refugee camps or in drought-affected communities for two months with over 4,000 metric tons of rice and 800 tons of vegetable oil.   The grant came shortly after the joint appeal by two UN agencies, WFP and the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), for 80 million dollars to provide food assistance to refugees in Ethiopia. According to Xinhua, an estimated 7.9 million people in Ethiopia are currently in need of emergency food assistance, while Ethiopia also hosts more than 900,000 refugees, mainly from Eritrea, South Sudan, Somalia and Sudan.

Title: Chinese Embassy and the Gambian Ministry of the Environment plant 500 coconut seedlings for the Gambia-China Coconut Tree Planting Initiative
Description: On August 8, 2018, the Gambia-China Coconut Tree Planting Initiative was launched in Banjul Beach, Gambia. The Chinese Embassy in Gambia and the Gambian Ministry of the Environment planted 500 coconut seedlings in the capital of Gambia, Banjul Beach for this initiative. The cost of the seedlings donation is unknown. This project was led by the Chinese Ambassador to Gambia, Zhang Jiming. The purpose of the project was to help beautify the beach and provide environmental benefits.   This is an annual event, with the first coconut seedling planting being in 2017, as recorded by project #57403. In this project, the Chinese Embassy in Gambia planted over 2,000 seedlings on the west coast of Gambia.   The Gambia-China Coconut Tree Planting Initiative was launched with the hopes of furthering China and Africa's cooperation plan of green development. This project is completed.

Title: China Grants Iftar Meals in Jordan in 2019
Description: On June 3rd, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Jordan and the "Mother of Ali" Charity Organization hosted a charitable Iftar meal for Ramadan and provided food packages for further distribution. Throughout the event, staff from the Chinese Embassy participated in handing out 1,650 vegetarian Iftar meals to Jordanians.   Additionally, on the same day, the Chinese Ambassador, Pan Weifang, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the "Mother of Ali" Charity Organization, committing to further cooperation in the future. According to the Chinese Ambassador, the intent of the project is to improve Jordanian's livelihoods and deepen relations between the two countries.

Title: Chinese Government signs ETCA in May 2018 with the Government of Ethiopia (Linked to Project ID#66045)
Description: On May 10, 2018, China and Ethiopia signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA). The signing ceremony was attended by Chinese legislator Li Zhanshu, and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. According to press releases covering the signing ceremony, the ETCA was one of three signed agreements, the other signed agreements are captured by: #71688 and   The financial flows captured by this ETCA are: Project #66045 - Chinese Government provides RMB 540 million interest-free loan for Mekelle City Water Supply Project

Title: China donates agricultural equipment worth 130 million CFA to Cote d'Ivoire (Linked to #66175)
Description: On 27 April 2019, the Chinese Ambassador officially donated agricultural equipment worth 130 million CFA to the Cote d'Ivoire Agency for Rice Development, under the 10th Chinese Agricultural Technical Assistance Mission (MATAC or Mission d'Assistance Technique Agricole Chinoise) for 2018-2020 (project #66175) in Guiguidou near Divo. The donation included combine harvesters, walking tractors, rice transplanters, seed sorters, rice milling machines, 4.5 tons of rice seeds, and a motorcycle.

Title: Chinese Embassy provides 940 food kits to Simón Palacios Intriago Foundation in Manabí, Ecuador
Description: On December 9, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Ecuador donated 940 food kits to the Simón Palacios Intriago Foundation in Manabí, Ecuador. This donation was made to support needy families in the province. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Ecuador’s Assemblywoman Wilma Andrade and China’s Ambassador to Ecuador Chen Guoyou attended the ceremony.

Title: Chinese government grants $400,000 for China-Cambodia-UNDP Trilateral Cassava Pilot project
Description: On May 21, 2013, the Chinese government provided a US$400,000 grant for Phase 2 of the China-Cambodia-UNDP Trilateral Cassava Pilot project to develop Cambodia's cassava industry (or 中国-柬埔寨-UNDP三方合作木薯试点二期项目). At the start of the project in December 2010, Cambodia and China signed a Protocol on the Exports of Cambodian Cassava to the Chinese Market, which aimed to increase the Cambodian share of cassava in the market and facilitate exports to China. The China-Cambodia-UNDP three-party cooperative cassava pilot project has two phases: Phase 1 was from December 27th, 2011 to January 16th, 2012 and Phase 2 was from May 21st, 2013 to March 2015 ("中国-柬埔寨-联合国开发计划署三方合作木薯试点项目概览"). The first phase of the project helped train Cambodian farmers. On May 21, 2013, the launching ceremony of Phase 2 of the project was held in Phnom Penh ("中国-柬埔寨-UNDP三方合作木薯试点二期项目启动"). For Phase 2, the Ministry of Commerce of China agreed to provide US$400,000 to this project. This is the first time the Chinese government provided financial support for this project ("中国-柬埔寨-联合国开发计划署三方合作木薯试点项目概览"). _x000D_ _x000D_ Ding Lao, State Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Cambodia, Jin Yuan, Counsellor of the Economic and Commercial Office of the Chinese Embassy in Cambodia, Setsuko Yamazaki, Representative of the United Nations Development Programme in Cambodia, and Lu Zhouxiang, Secretary of Commerce, Department of International Economic and Trade Relations, Ministry of Commerce of China, attended the Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding signing ceremony for Phase 2 ("柬中联合国签署木薯开发项目备忘录 提高柬木薯种植栽培加工出口能力").

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 50 million grant - through March 2004 ETCA - to Myanmar for multiple projects (linked to project #49941 and #64998)
Description: On March 24, 2004, the Chinese Government and the Government of Myanmar signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed RMB 50 million of grant funding for multiple projects. The grant was for a number of projects which included the renovation of Yangon National Cultural Theatre at the cost of Yuan 12.4 million (recorded in project #49941), and the rice milling machine installation project (recorded in project #64998). As part of this ETCA, the Chinese government also provided an RMB 200 million interest-free loan, which is recorded in project #64759.

Title: China donates emergency food aid to Lesotho
Description: On April 19, 2018, Chinese Ambassador to Lesotho Sun Xianghua attended the handover ceremony of China's emergency food aid project in Lesotho, and signed a handover certificate with Lesotho's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations and Acting Minister Sechabi. About 40 people including Minister of the Prime Minister's Office of Lesotho Tso Luo, Acting Permanent Secretary Mahoshi, Acting Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Lehra, heads of relevant departments, Ma Guoliang, Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Lesotho, and local media reporters attended the event.  This is the second batch of emergency food aid provided by the Chinese government to Lesotho since November 2017. In 2016, when there was a serious shortage of food in Las Vegas, the Chinese government provided a batch of emergency food aid to Las Vegas in time, benefiting more than 400,000 people in Las Vegas. In 2017, at the request of the Lesotho government, the Chinese government once again provided emergency food aid to Lesotho and increased the amount of aid.  However, the exact donation amount for this emergency food aid is unknown.

Title: China Eximbank provides $89.15 million preferential buyer's credit for Agno River Integrated Irrigation Project
Description: On November 9, 2009, China Eximbank and the Government of the Philippines signed a $89.15 million preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement [China Eximbank PBC 2009 No. (23)] for the Agno River Integrated Irrigation Project (ARIIP). The estimated borrowing terms of the PBC are as follows: a 20 year maturity, a 5 year grace period, and a 3% interest rate. The final maturity date of the PBC is January 21, 2030. The loan entered into force on February 1, 2010. The proceeds of the PBC were to be used by the borrower to partially finance a commercial contract (No. ARIIPI-C-1) between the National Irrigation Agency of the Philippines and China CAMC Engineering Co., Ltd. (CAMCE), which was signed on May 25, 2009.    The project involved the construction of a 350 meter long and 18 meter high overflow dam (San Roque Power Dam) on the Agno River and a regulating reservoir that was aimed at providing year-round irrigation to 34,450 hectares of farmlands that would benefit 29,207 farmers in Pangasinan province within the Ilocos Region of Luzon. The ultimate purpose of the project was to provide water for irrigation through the construction of new diversion and canal systems, to rehabilitate existing irrigation facilities to improve water delivery in the service area, to restore non-functional service area through improved water delivery or augmentation of water supply, to increase agricultural productivity and farmers income, to generate employment.
