The municipalities that were expected to benefit from the project included Asingan, Balungao, Bautista, Binalonan, Calasiao, Laoac, Manaoag, Mapandan, Mangaldan, Natividad, Sta. Maria, San Manuel, San Nicolas, San Quintin, Sta. Barbara, Tayug, Villasis, Urdaneta City.   CAMCE was the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. The owner of the project is the National Irrigation Agency of the Philippines. The project commenced in February 2010 and it was completed ahead of schedule on June 20, 2013.  Then, on July 9, 2014, the National Irrigation Agency of the Philippines issued a final acceptance certificate (FAC) for the project. A formal project completion ceremony took place on August 8, 2014.

Title: China donates USD $670,000 worth of military aid and farm machinery to Guinea-Bissau
Description: On February 21, 2019, China handed over a batch of military aid and farm/construction machinery to the General Staff of Guinea-Bissau. The donation included 6 agricultural pieces of machinery and 5 construction machinery with an estimated value of $670,000 or 385 million CFA francs. The equipment is intended to help Guinea-Bissau's military to carry out agricultural production and engineering construction, and take solid steps towards the goal of building a more powerful army.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Kenya donates 737,800 Ksh for International Free Lunch Project at Mcedo-Beijing School in Kenya (link to #70256)
Description: On December 11th, 2019 the Embassy of China held a free brunch donation ceremony at Mcedo-Beijing Elementary School to provide 526 students with breakfast and lunch fees for one semester. The total value of the donation is equal to 737,800 Kenyan shillings. The project was implemented with the help of the "International Free Lunch Project" ( 国际免费午餐项目). It is hoped that the supplies will help alleviate the effects of poverty and bolster school attendance. In attendance were the school students and staff, Guo Ce, Minister Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Kenya, and Li Changgui, President of the Kenya-China Economic and Trade Association.   Mcedo-Beijing School,  located in the Makere Slum, was set up in 2007 with the financial support of the Chinese Embassy. Chinese firms have also provided donations to the school in the past including food aid, school uniforms, and educational materials.   The donation accompanied another donation on the same day from the Kenya-China Economic Trade Association captured in project ID #70256.

Title: Chinese Government provides $5.7 million grant for provision of agricultural equipment, vehicle maintenance, and government offices
Description: Between 2000 and 2008, the Chinese Government committed $5,788,953.17 in grant funding to the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo for the provision of agricultural equipment, vehicle maintenance, and government offices. This funding was said to be in kind through the donation of products. According to the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the Chinese Government disbursed a total of $2,996,849.14 for this project. The disbursements for the project were as follows: 2000: $1,812,117.36; 2007: $177,514.792; 2008: $128,739.67; and 2009: $878,798.974. The first payment was made on December 31, 2000 and the last payement was made on December 31, 2009.  The French project title is Lot des matériels agricoles, des bureaux, des maintenances et des véhicules. This project is completed.

Title: Chinese Government Sends a Team of 7 Agricultural Experts to Burkina Faso (linked to ProjectID#88762)
Description: As part of the cooperation agreements signed between China and Burkina Faso after the re-establishment of a diplomatic relationship between the two nations, in 2018, China started providing Burkina Faso with agricultural technical assistance. This assistance includes large-scale irrigation facilities as well as agricultural advice and support services.  A team of 7 agricultural experts was dispatched in late June 2018. "The agricultural technology team is the most disciplined and successful Chinese aid team in Burkina Faso with the widest reach across the country," said Li Jian, China's Ambassador to Burkina Faso. The first agricultural aid project completed its 1-year term on June 30, 2019, and after that, the experts will stay for another 2 years in Burkina Faso for the second aid mission (see ProjectID#88762).

Title: Chinese Government pledges 300,000 tons of food aid to North Korea in 2008
Description: When Xi Jinping went to North Korea in 2008 as vice president, the Chinese Government agreed to provide more than 300,000 tons of food to North Korea, according to Park Byung Kwang, director of the center for Northeast Asia at the Seoul-based Institute for National Security Strategy, a think tank affiliated with South Korea’s main spy agency.  However, according to Chinese Government reporting to the World Food Program’s International Food Aid Information System (INTERFAIS), it ultimately provided no food aid deliveries to North Korea in 2008. Chinese food aid deliveries in 2009 are captured via Project ID#63004.

Title: China signs USD20m cotton agreement with Burkina Faso, Mali, Chad, and Benin
Description: In December 2011, China signed a cotton agreement with four key cotton-producing African countries, Burkina Faso, Mali, Chad and Benin (known as the C4), providing China with an alternative source of cotton. China stated it would provide seeds, machinery, fertilizer and other materials in a bid to increase and improve the quality of local production. Chinese commerce minister Chen Deming attended the signing ceremony.   On December 3, 2013, China and the C4 countries jointly issued Press Communiqué of Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China and C4 Board of Trade on Cooperation in Cotton Industry, and stated that under the agreement signed in 2011, China has dispatched expert groups, provided training, and donated materials to the C4 worth USD20 million.

Title: Chinese Government donates first batch of tsunami relief goods worth RMB 50 million following 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (Linked to Project ID#33240, #33226)
Description: On 26 December 2004, a severe earthquake near the Indonesian island of Sumatra triggered an enormous tsunami in the Indian Ocean that hit many countries, including Sri Lanka. In response, the Chinese government sent three aid packages for tsunami relief to Sri Lanka. This project captures the first batch worth 50 million RMB consisting of blankets, tents, bedding, food, and medical equipment which all arrived in Sri Lanka on 28 December 2004._x000D_ _x000D_ The other two aid packages are captured in project #33240 and #33226. _x000D_ _x000D_ The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service captures this first batch in flow ID #24789.

Title: China donates agricultural equipment to Tonga after cyclone
Description: On May 23, 2018, Wang Baodong, Chinese Ambassador to Tonga, and Hon. Semisi Fakahau, Minister for Agriculture, Food, Forests and Fisheries signed the Handover Certificate of Donated Agricultural Equipment from Dongguan Municipality, Guandong Province of China to the Kingdom of Tonga. This batch of equipment is aimed to help the agriculture sector recover from the damages caused by Cyclone Gita and improve the livelihood of the Tongan people. The donation included 4 plow tractors and 50 chainsaws, which will help the Tonga Ministry of Agriculture, Food, Forests and Fisheries clear the trees which were uprooted from the cyclone. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.
Funding_Agencies: People's Government of Dongguan City, Guangdong Province

Title: CDB provides $79 million loan for Camaiangala Agroindustrial Farm Project (Linked to Project ID#67)
Description: In 2013, China Development Bank approved an $79 million subsidiary loan for the Camaiangala Agroindustrial Farm Project through a larger $1.5 billion line of credit (common terms) agreement that it signed with the Government of Angola (as captured via Project ID#67). The proceeds of the loan were to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract that the Government of Angola signed with China National Electronics Import & Export Corporation (CEIEC) in 2011.   This project involved the construction of an agroindustrial farm in Camanongue in Moxico Province. More specifically, the project involved cultivation of 16,000 hectares of maize, soybeans, maize flour, and pork.   CEIEC was the contractor responsible for implementation. However, Gesterra, a land management company owned by the Angolan Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development, and Fisheries, was also involved in the management of the project. The first three years of the project (and CEIEC contract period) were used to clear land, build farm infrastructure, and conduct plant experimentation; the final two years of the project (and CEIEC contract period) were used to train Angolan farmers in technology and land management.

Title: FAO-China South-South Cooperation Trust Fund grants $1 million USD to Liberia's National Program for Food Security (Linked to #85169, Umbrella #87769)
Description: In November 2011, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) co-signed two new tripartite agreements with China, Liberia and Senegal respectively to support implementation of a series of food security initiatives and projects in Liberia and Senegal. The funding provided through the new agreement comes from the China Ministry of Agriculture through the FAO-China Trust Fund (see Umbrella Project #87769).   Under the agreement with Liberia, China contributed over $1 million USD and provided technical assistance through 24 Chinese experts (#85169) to support Liberia's National Program for Food Security over a two-year period. The Chinese South-South Cooperation (SSC) team arrived at Liberia in May 2012 and left in April 2014.

Title: China donates $3,168 USD to WFP for food aid to HIV and TB patients in Lesotho (Linked to umbrella project #30591)
Description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID #103432), on 8 October 2012, the Chinese government donated $3,168 USD to the World Food Programme (WFP) for nutrition support to moderately undernourished antiretroviral therapy (ART) and tuberculosis (TB) patients through supplementary feeding in Lesotho. This is a sub-project of umbrella project #30591.

Title: China BBCA Group provides USD 15,387.84 supplier's credit loan to Voraxxx Trade and Import of Industrialized Products Eireli
Description: In January 2018, China BBCA Group Corporation Limited (or Anhui Fengyuan Group), a state-owned enterprise, provided a USD 15,387.84 supplier's credit loan to Voraxxx Trade and Import of Industrialized Products, a Brazil-based company. The loan's borrowing terms and purpose are unclear. The Central Bank of Brazil lists the loan registration (ID TA820208) as complete.  According to the BBCA Group website, Fengyuan Brazil Industrial Investment Co., Ltd. is a holding subsidiary of Fengyuan Group in Brazil. It is building the largest corn deep-processing industrial base in South America in Maracaju, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. The main products include organic acids, corn Starch, maltodextrin, maltose syrup, by-product corn gluten meal, corn gluten feed, and other products. Mato Grosso do Sul is an important corn and soybean production area with an annual output of 7 million tons of corn. It is unclear whether or how this related to the USD 15,387.84 supplier's credit loan to Voraxxx.   In July 2019, a director from Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture visited BBCA Group officials are their project site in Maracaju, Mato Grosso do Sul. The director said they welcomed BBCA Group's investment in Brazil, and that the Southern State Government and the Federal Ministry of Agriculture will continue to provide various assistance and preferential treatment to BBCA Group Brazil.
Funding_Agencies: BBCA Group Corporation Limited (or Anhui Fengyuan Group or BBCA Group)

Title: China Ministry of Agriculture contributes $30 million USD for Phase I of the FAO-China South-South Cooperation Trust Fund (Linked to #87779)
Description: On 25 March 2009, the Chinese Vice Minister of Agriculture and UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Assistant Director General signed a agreement to establish the FAO-China South-South Cooperation Trust Fund. China contributed $30 million USD to Phase I (Project #87769) and $50 million USD for Phase II (see Project #87779). Phase I took place over three years in which $10 million USD was released each year.   The purpose of this special fund was to improve agricultural productivity in the Global South by providing Chinese experts for technical assistance, training, and knowledge exchange. This project has a strong focus on Africa but also included countries in Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East.   The known sub-projects are as follows:  1) $1,050,098 USD for technical assistance to Malawi (Project #58138 and #48940) 2) $1 million for Liberia's National Program for Food Security (see Projects #35267 and #85169) 3) $1.5 million USD for the China-Namibia South-South Cooperation Project (see Projects #62095 and #62098) 4) Unknown amount for the China, Sierra Leone, FAO tripartite agreement (see Projects #30005, #67794, #67793).

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 18 million grant for Hardap Inland Aquaculture Center Upgrade Project (Linked to project #1339)
Description: On April 2, 2012, the Chinese Government and the Government of Namibia signed an exchange of letters regarding the Hardap Inland Aquaculture Center Upgrade Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce reportedly committed RMB 18 million of grant funding in support of the project. These funds were drawn from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) that the two governments signed on February 9, 2009 (recorded in project #1296).  The project involved the upgrading of the Hardap Inland Aquaculture Center, which is located about 270 kilometers from capital Windhoek. Upon completion, the Center was expected to produce around 37 tons of marketable fish and half a million fingerlings per annum. Sinohydro Tianjin Engineering was the contractor responsible for implementation of the project. The company signed a construction contract with the Government of Namibia on August 29, 2014. The originally anticipated period of project implementation was from November 20, 2014 to November 19, 2015. The actual project commencement date was November 24, 2014. The project was completed on July 8, 2016.  The Hardap Center is referred to as the "Hadap" or "Hadapu"" center. The Chinese project title is 哈达普水产养殖中心改造项目 or 纳米比亚哈达普水产养殖中心改造项目.

Title: China Eximbank provides $45million preferential buyer’s credit for Rubber and Rice Planting and Processing Project (Linked to Project ID#31006, #31008, #31007)
Description: In 2013, China Eximbank signaled its interest in signing a $45million preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement with Sierra Leone China Agriculture Development Limited Company (SLeCHAD) for a Rubber and Rice Planting and Processing Project. SLeCHAD is a joint venture and project company created by Hainan Zhonghai International Economic Cooperation Co., Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group, Hainan Rubber State Industry Group Co., Ltd., and the Government of Sierra Leone. The proceeds from the PBC would have been used to develop 100,000 hectares of rubber plantation and 35,000 hectares of irrigated rice field with processing facilities from both rubber and rice. This project would have been implemented in the Kolifa Mabang, Kolifa Rowala, Yoni and Fakunya chiefdoms within the Moyamba district and Tonkolili district. The commitment was made later but no specific date was found.

Title: Chinese Government provides $100,000 grant to support Grenada’s Irrigation and Drainage System
Description: According to internal records that the Government of Grenada shared with AidData in June 2018, the Chinese Government provided a $100,000 grant to the Government of Grenada in 2005 to support its irrigation and drainage system.

Title: China Ministry of Agriculture and Bulgarian Ministry of Agriculture jointly launched Agricultural Demonstration Zone
Description: On 23 May 2017, the China Ministry of Agriculture and Bulgaria Ministry of Agriculture signed a joint statement to launch the first agricultural demonstration zone between China and the Central and Eastern European countries. The original memorandum of understanding was signed between China and Bulgaria in 2017. The agricultural demonstration zone was launched at the Agricultural University of Plovdiv. The cooperation will focus on agricultural scientific research, development of agricultural machinery, planting, breeding, and improving the supply chain. The "16 + 1" framework is the basis for the cooperation agreement. China and Bulgaria will support the construction of the demonstration zone in terms of policies, manpower, materials, and funds. The demonstration zone is a result of talks between Prime Minister Boyko Borissov and Chinese counterpart Li Keqiang, which took place in Sofia in 2016. On 24 November 2017 construction of the agricultural demonstration zone had been completed. The maintenance of the building will be funded by the Bulgarian Ministry of Agriculture and through donations.

Title: China Eximbank provides $41.7 million loan for Phase I of Dehkanabad Potash Fertilizer Plant Project (Linked to Project ID#72169 and #40128)
Description: In 2007, China Eximbank provided a $41.705 million loan to Uzbek Industrial and Construction Bank (JSC Uzpromstroybank) for Phase I of Dehkanabad Potash Fertilizer Plant Project. The terms of the loan are as follows: 20 year maturity, 5 year grace period, and 2% interest rate. This project involved the construction of the Dehkanabad potash plant located at the Tyubegatan deposit.    Construction of phase 1 of the plant started in 2010. The total cost of the project is $123.7 million. In addition to the China Eximbank funding, the Fund for Reconstruction and Development of Uzbekistan allocated a $61.9 million loan, and Uzkimyosanoat also directed its own funds to finance the construction. This project sought to increase the capacity of the plan to produce 200,000 tonnes of potash per year. In 2008, SJSC Uzkimyosanoat concluded contracts with ZAO UK Zapadouralsky Machine-Building Concern (Russia) and CITIC Pacific Ltd. (China) for the turnkey construction of the facility. Construction began in 2007 and the first phase of the project was completed on October 5, 2010.

Title: China grants Niue 1,500,000 NZD to purchase 25 tractors
Description: In January 2011, China granted Niue 1,500,000 NZD to purchasing 25 tractors.

Title: China grants 3 million TOP to Tonga [Subprojects: #37707]
Description: On January 9, 2009, Chinese and Tongan officials signed an agreement for the provision of a 3 million TOP grant to Tonga aimed to assist in Tonga's development. Of this 3 million, 50,000 was utilized for the construction of a piggery at the agricultural demonstration farm (#37707). The remaining allocation is unknown.   Construction of the farm was completed by December 5, 2010 (#37707).

Title: China Eximbank provides RMB 239.6 million government concessional loan for Di-Ammonium Phosphate Fertilizer Plant Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#39369)
Description: In 2000, the Chinese Government offered $53.29 million of debt financing to the Government of Bangladesh for the Di-Ammonium Phosphate Fertilizer Plant Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) agreed to issue an RMB 200 million loan for the project. The loan agreement between MOFCOM and the Government of Bangladesh (captured via Project ID#39369) was finalized on September 13, 2000 and it carried the following borrowing terms: a 15-year maturity, a 10-year grace period, and a 0% interest rate. China Eximbank and the Government of Bangladesh also signed an RMB 239,667,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the project on September 7, 2005 (captured via Project ID#33929).   The GCL carried the following borrowing terms: a 16-year maturity, a 4-year grace period, a 2% interest rate, and a 0.2% commitment fee (service charge). The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the GCL and the interest-free loan to partially finance a $59.21 million commercial contract between China National Complete Plant Import and Export Corporation Limited (COMPLANT) and Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC). According to the Government of Bangladesh’s Economic Relations Division (ERD), the interest-free loan from MOFCOM had achieved a disbursement rate of 100% (RMB 200,000,000 out of RMB 200,000,000) as of June 30, 2014 and the borrower had repaid RMB 187,500,000 to MOFCOM as of June 30, 2014. According to the Government of Bangladesh’s ERD, the GCL had achieved a disbursement rate of 100% (RMB 239,667,000 out of RMB 239,667,000) as of June 30, 2014 and the borrower had repaid China Eximbank RMB 132,353,000 as of June 30, 2014 and RMB 239,667,000 as of June 30, 2019.   The purpose of the project was to build an 800-ton-per-day di-ammonia phosphate fertilizer plant in the Anowara Upazilla (SubDistrict) of Chittagong Division. COMPLANT was the EPC contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction of the di-ammonium phosphate fertilizer plant — known as Di-Ammonium Phosphate Fertiliser Company Ltd (DAPFCL) — was originally expected to begin at the end of 2000 and projected to commence operations within 30 months (July 1, 2003). However, the project did not commence until April 2004 and it was not completed until June 2006. Then, in August 2016, an ammonia tank at the plant exploded, causing at least 50 people to fall sick from inhaling toxic gas. The emission of toxic ammonia at the fertilizer factory was brought under control on August 23, 2016, some 11 hours after one of two smaller 500-tonne capacity ammonia storage tanks exploded. Fifty people, including women, were admitted to the Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH). BCIC, which now runs the factory, formed a 10-member committee to investigate the incident.

Title: Chinese embassy donates proceeds from charity sale to Malawi International Women's Association
Description: On October 30, 2010, the Chinese embassy donated proceeds from charity sale to Malawi International Women's Association, according to the Chinese Embassy and Chinese Ministry of Commerce. The charity sale is called the annual Lilongwe International Charity Bazaar. At the charity sale, the embassy sold Chinese food and cultural items. The amount of the donation is unknown._x000D_ _x000D_ Similar donations from Chinese embassy events have been donated to IWAM in 2009 (#58217), in 2015 (#58096) and in 2017 (#58644).

Title: China Eximbank contributes $154 million to $220 million syndicated buyer’s credit loan for Ca Mau Fertilizer Plant Construction Project
Description: On September 15, 2011, PetroVietnam Ca Mau Fertilizer Company Limited (PVCFC) — a project company and subsidiary of the state-owned Vietnam Oil and Gas Group (PetroVietnam) — signed a $220 million syndicated buyer’s credit loan (BCL) agreement with BNP Paribas Bank, China Eximbank, and Credit Agricole Bank for the Ca Mau Fertilizer Plant Construction Project. China Eximbank contributed $154 million to the syndicated loan. The borrowing terms are as follows: an 10-year maturity (120 months from the first disbursement date on July 25, 2012), a 3-year grace period, and an interest rate of 6-month LIBOR plus 2.6% margin (3.122%). Sinosure provided buyer’s credit insurance and the Vietnam Ministry of Finance provided a sovereign guarantee.   The proceeds of the loan were to be used by the borrower to partially finance an EPC contract signed on May 6, 2008 with Wuhuan Engineering Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China National Chemical Engineering Group Corporation Ltd. (CNCEC). The purpose of the project was to construct a fertilizer plant in Khánh An commune, U Minh District, and Cà Mau Province.   CNCEC was the contractor responsible for project implementation. A formal groundbreaking ceremony was held on July 26, 2008. The project passed a performance appraisal an April 20, 2012, and the owner issued a temporary project acceptance certificate (PAC) on April 25, 2012. Then, on April 25, 2014, the project owner issued the final acceptance certificate (FAC).

Title: Chinese Government Donates Drugs and Medical Equipment to Niger (Linked to #32673)
Description: On 19 January 2012, the Chinese Government officially donated medical equipment and medicine to Niger. The cost, quantity, and types of supplies are unknown._x000D_ _x000D_ This is linked to the 17th Chinese medical team serving at the same time as this donation (#32673)

Title: Chinese Government donates 500,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $9 million in August 2021
Description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 750,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Iraq. The Chinese Government delivered 50,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Iraq on March 2, 2021. Then, on April 11, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Iraq.  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 500,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Iraq in August 2021. Then, in October 2021, the Chinese Government donated another batch of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines (including an unknown number of doses) to the Government of Iraq.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Timor-Leste provides 40,000 face masks to the Timor-Leste Ministry of the Interior in August 2020
Description: On August 27, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Timor-Leste donated 40,000 face masks to the Timor-Leste Ministry of the Interior. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. The materials will be distributed to the Border Patrol Unite Police (UPF) and immigration services for efforts against the COVID-19 pandemic.

Title: Chinese Government donates 52,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $936,000 in February 2021
Description: On February 10, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 52,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Brunei.  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 100,000 donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses and 102,400 syringes to the Government of Brunei. (Project #96150)

Title: China sends medical team to Ethiopia to support the fight against Covid-19 (Linked to Project ID#94525)
Description: On April 16, 2020, a twelve-person medical team arrived in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia from China to help the country contain the spread of Covid-19. During the team's fifteen-day visit, they visited treatment facilities and shared their experiences fighting the virus with their Ethiopian counterparts. The members of the team were selected from fields such as nosocomial sense, public health, nursing, traditional Chinese medicine, etc.  On the same flight that brought the medical team, there were also supplies donated by the Chinese government to the Ethiopian government (see Project ID#94525).

Title: China donates anti-epidemic supplies to Grenada in May 2020 for COVID-19 relief
Description: On May 6, 2020, the health ministry in Grenada received a donation of anti-epidemic supplies from China. The donations included 15,000 surgical masks, 50 goggles, 100 Personal Protective Equipment, and 1,500 viral swabs. Also included were 5,000 surgical masks and 10 ventilators, through a joint donor collaboration between Ambassador Warren Newfield and his main CBI agent in China, Ms. Anna Chen.

Title: China donates anti-malarial drugs worth 12 million DJF to Djibouti
Description: On 5 December 2007, the Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaodu officially handed over anti-malaria medicine worth 12 million DJF (approximately 500,000 RMB) to the Djibouti Ministry of Health. The ceremony took place at the Central Purchasing Center for Essential Materials and Medicines headquarters in Djibouti.

Title: China provides Covid-19 supplies to Vecer Press in North Macedonia in April 2020 (Linked to #93708, 94913)
Description: On April 9, 2020, the Chinese Embassy provided a batch of Covid-19 supplies to three media outlets in North Macedonia on behalf of the Chinese government. These outlets included North Macedonia Media Information Agency (#93708), the Macedonia Radio and Television (# 94913), and the Vecer (Evening News) (# 94916 ). The exact type, amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to North Macedonia, Zhang Zuo, attended the ceremony and handed over the donation to these three organizations.

Title: China provides a medical team to Antigua & Barbuda to carry out a Cataract Surgery Clinic (linked to #54934)
Description: In the first half of 2015, China sent Antigua & Barbuda an 8 member Ophthalmologist Medical Team to carry out a Cataract Surgery Clinic through an initiative called Bright Journey. The team will stay for one month carrying out surgical procedures at the Mount St. John's Medical Center and will donate all surgical equipment after completion. _x000D_ _x000D_ According to the Antiguan Observer article, over 200 cataract surgeries have been completed as a result of this initiative. In 2018, the "Bright Journey" team returned to Antigua and Barbuda, which was captured in #54943.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 10 million grant — via ETCA — for medical equipment and vehicles
Description: On July 11, 2011, an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) was signed between the government of China and Serbia in Belgrade, Serbia. The agreement was signed by China Ministry of Commerce and European Integration Office (SEIO) of Serbia. The agreement provided Serbia with a 10 million RMB grant for the purchase of medical equipment and vehicles.

Title: Chinese government donates 47 courtesy first aid vehicles to Chad
Description: On December 15, 2015, the ceremony of handover of 47 courtesy first aid vehicles donated by Chinese government to Chad was held in the Great Hall of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Chinese Embassy in Chad, Nie Bo, and the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Chad, Dago, signed the handover certificate on behalf of their respective governments. The 47 courtesy vehicles were donated to support the government's bid to host the AU summit.

Title: Chinese Government agrees to donate 1 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $18 million in September 2021
Description: The Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Malaysia on July 16, 2021. Upon arrival, the vaccines were escorted by the Royal Malaysian Police Force (PDRM) to Pharmaniaga’s warehouse before being distributed nationwide as part of the National COVID-19 Immunization Program. Then, on September 29, 2021, Dato’ Saifuddin Abdullah, Malaysia's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Wang Yi, State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), held a telephone conversation. Wang Yi conveyed the decision by the Chinese Government to contribute an additional 1 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Malaysia, on the basis of the deep friendship between the two countries and peoples. It is unclear if the Chinese Government fulfilled this commitment.   Then, in December 2021, representatives of the Chinese Government and the Government of Malaysia attended the Malaysia-China High Level Committee (HLC) on Cooperation in the Post-Covid-19 Era. At that meeting, the Chinese Government reportedly made a commitment to donate an additional 2 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Malaysia. It is unclear if the Chinese Government fulfilled this commitment.

Title: Chinese Embassy provides first batch of 15 ventilators in April 2020 to Myanmar Ministry of Health for fighting COVID-19 (Linked to Project ID#90285)
Description: On April 22, 2020, the Chinese Embassy officially donated the first batch of 15 YH-830-11 bi-level positive pressure ventilators to the Myanmar Ministry of Health and Sports as they arrived at the Yangon International Airport (captured via Project ID #90274). The monetary value of the 15 ventilators is unknown.  On April 28, 2020, the Chinese Embassy officially donated the second batch of an additional 15 YH-830-11 bi-level positive pressure ventilators to the Myanmar Ministry of Health and Sports as well as the Myanmar Military as they arrived at the China-Myanmar border (captured via Project ID #90285). The monetary value of the 15 ventilators is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government donates footballs, basketballs, volleyballs, badminton rackets and other sporting equipment to Ministry of Youth and Sports of Mauritius
Description: In 2004, China donated 30 Footballs, 50 Basketballs, 50 Volleyballs, 100 Badminton Rackets, and 600 tubes of Shuttlecocks to the Mauritian Ministry of Youth and Sports. The estimated value of this donation is 194,000 MUR. The exact start and end dates for this project are unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides interest-free loan for Karonga-Chitipa Road (Bingu Highway) (Linked to Project ID#774)
Description: On March 17, 2008, the Chinese Government issued a $70 million grant (captured via Project ID#774) and an interest-free loan (captured via Project ID#69242) for the construction of the completion of the Karonga-Chitipa Road (also known as Bingu Highway) in the northern region of Malawi. The People's Republic of China (China) replaced the original financier, the Republic of China (Taiwan), when Government of Malawi ended its diplomatic relations with Taiwan.  The face value of the interest-free loan is unknown, but it carried the following borrowing terms: a 10 year grace period, a 20 year maturity, and a 0% interest rate.  The project involved the completion of the construction of 101 km Karonga-Chitipa Road (M26) to Bitumen Standard Class I road.   China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) was the contractor responsible for the construction of the first 13 km section between Karonga and Mwesya bridge for a total contract value of $70 million. The project design consultant was China Highway Planning and Design Institute (HPDI).  Project implementation commenced on March 17, 2008 and the originally expected completion date was April 17, 2010, which was later revised to October 30, 2011. The expected completion date was further revised to June 30, 2012 because of shortage of diesel and increased quantities of work items. The expected project completion date was again changed from June 30, 2012 to December 31, 2012 because of diesel shortage and change in pavement design from natural gravel to crushed stone. An official opening ceremony for the road was held on January 7, 2013. The road reportedly benefitted citizens of Chitipa, in the northern border district of Malawi, who formerly would have spent 5 hours journeying to Karonga.  The trip subsequently took 90 minutes and saved time for those who needed the road to do business or access services not available in Chitipa.

Title: Chinese Government donates 300,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $5.4 million in August 2021
Description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government and the Chinese Red Cross Society donated approximately 14 million doses of Sinopharm and Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia and the Ethiopian Red Cross Society. The Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia on March 29, 2021 (see project ID#95864). Then, on May 13, 2021, China's Ministry of Defense delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to Ethiopia's Ministry of Defense (see project ID#95866). Approximately one month later, on June 19, 2021, the Chinese Red Cross Society delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (see project ID#95868). Two months later, on August 19, 2021, China's Ministry of Defense delivered an additional 200,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to Ethiopia's Ministry of Defense (see project ID#95869).  On August 23, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (see project ID#95944). Approximately one month later, on October 24, 2021, Chinese Government delivered 800,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (see project ID#95946). Then, in December 2021, the Chinese Government announced that it had donated 2 million additional doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia via COVID-19 Vaccines Global Access (COVAX) — a worldwide initiative aimed at equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines directed by the GAVI vaccine alliance, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, the World Health Organization, and UNICEF (see project ID#95947). Then, on January 20, 2022, the Chinese Government delivered 2.2 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Ethiopia (see project ID#96127). The Chinese Government delivered an additional 10 million donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health on June 27, 2022 (see project ID#96143). According to the Chinese Government, its cumulative donations of Covid-19 vaccine doses to Ethiopia amounted to 500,000 doses as of June 2021, 1.8 million doses as of October 2021, 5 million doses as of December 2021, 7 million doses as of January 2022, 9.7 million doses as of March 2022, and 14 million doses as of June 2022.

Title: China donates medicines and medical equipment to Djibouti for the Bight Journey Project
Description: On 30 March 2016, the Chinese government officially handed over a donation of medical equipment and medicines to Djibouti. This donation is part of the "Guangmingxing" (光明行) or "Bright Journey" project initiated by China, which involved the provision of medical supplies and free cataract surgeries to 10 countries in Africa. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 21st medical team to Algiers, Aïn Defla, Tiaret, Sétif, Khenchela, Batna, Mascara, and Saïda
Description: Since 1963, the Chinese Government has been dispatching medical teams to the Algeria. Hubei Province is responsible for sending the teams.   In 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Algeria dispatched the 21st Chinese medical team to Algeria. The team was stationed in 8 of Algeria’s wilayas (provinces): Algiers, Aïn Defla, Tiaret, Sétif, Khenchela, Batna, Mascara, and Saïda. It completed its term of service between 2008 and 2010.

Title: Zhongshan Municipal Government of the People's Republic of China Donates 100,000 medical supplies to Costa Rican Public Hospital
Description: On June 30, 2020, the Zhongshan Municipal Government donated 100,000 pieces of medical supplies to the Hospital México in San José, Costa Rica, to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. These supplies include surgical masks, protective clothing, and infrared thermometers.
Funding_Agencies: Zhongshan Municipal Government of Guangdong Province

Title: Chinese Government provides $6 million grant for the construction of the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru (linked to Project ID#12177)
Description: On October 3, 2008, China's ambassador to Uganda, Sun Heping, announced that the Chinese Government would build a hospital and malaria treatment/prevention center called the China-Uganda Friendship Hospital in Naguru (CUFH-N) with a grant of $6 million. The purpose of the project was to (a) provide health services to the residents of Nakawa Division, Kampala Metropolitan Area; and (b) decongest Mulago National Referral Hospital, the only general public hospital serving an estimated 3 million inhabitants of the Kampala Metropolitan Area. It involved the construction of a two-storey hospital with a bed capacity of 100, the construction of staff houses, and the supply and installation of medical equipment including a CT-scan. China National Complete Plant Import and Export Corporation (COMPLANT) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA) donated the 5 acre site where the hospital was built. The Government of Uganda also contributed an estimated $2 million in tax waivers on construction materials used to build the hospital, landscaping, road access and licensing fees.   The 5772.8-square-meter hospital was slated to begin construction in August 2009. The groundbreaking ceremony was held on September 23, 2009. Construction was completed in November 2011. The handover ceremony was held on January 6, 2012  In June 2012, Jing Yanhui, an official from the Chinese embassy in Uganda, announced that a malaria treatment and prevention center would be added on to the hospital in the near future.

Title: China provides 250 PPE kits to Mexico for COVID-19 relief in December 2020
Description: On December 28, 2020, China donated 250 PPE kits to Mexico. These kits will be used for COVID-19 prevention in Mexico and they have an estimated value of 100 thousand Mexican pesos.  A virtual ceremony took place for the delivery/reception of these medical kits. The Minister Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Mexico, Wang Huijun, and the Secretary of Health of Chiapas, José Manuel Cruz Castellanos, attended the ceremony.

Title: Chinese Government donates ophthalmic equipment and consumables worth BWP 20.8 million
Description: From June 27 to July 1, 2011, during the "Hope of Light Cataract Project" (see Project ID #30843), Botswana also received a donation of ophthalmic equipment and consumables worth BWP 20.8 million from China during the same period. On July 3rd, 2011, a ceremony was held for the 30th anniversary of China's medical aid to Botswana. In the ceremony, ophthalmic equipment and medicine was officially handed over with handover certificates signed and exchanged.

Title: China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) donated 23 million RMB to the Jamaican National Premier League (Linked wth project #72021)
Description: On 28 August 2013, China Harbour Engineering Co., Ltd. (CHEC) donated J$23 million to the Jamaican National Premier League. The donation follows a similar donation in 2012 for nearly the same amount (see #70723). The Jamaican National Premier League is the top division for men's football (soccer) in Jamaica. Linked with project #72021, detailing the spending that CHEC undertook on awards to the Jamaican National Premier League.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 70 million grant for Phase 1 of China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#21460, #72842, #26668)
Description: During the 2006 Forum on China-Africa Co-operation in Beijing, the Chinese Government agreed in principle to construct a China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital in Mahusekwa District and Mashonaland East Province (approximately 70 km east of Harare). Then, in 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed an RMB 70 million grant agreement for Phase 1 of the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital Construction Project.   Phase 1 involved the construction and furnishing of a 17,000 square meter hospital with 129 beds. It also involved the construction of one block of 2-story outpatient and emergency treatment facilities, two blocks of 2-story buildings for inpatient treatment, the installation of a hospital canteen, a substation and generator room.   Nantong Construction Group Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation of Phase 1. A groundbreaking ceremony took place October 30, 2009, and the hospital was opened and handed over to the Zimbabwean authorities on September 21, 2012. The hospital was officially commissioned in 2013. Project ID#20443 captures Phase 1.   In 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zimbabwe signed a grant agreement for Phase 2 of the China-Zimbabwe Friendship Hospital Construction Project (captured via Project ID#72842). Phase 2 involved the installation of a mortuary and incinerator room, concrete water tower, borehole, access roads, and a parking lot. The monetary value of the grant provided for Phase 2 is unknown. China Railway Sixth Group was the contractor responsible for the project's implementation. The hospital was intended to be handed over to Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Welfare. This phase of the project began on January 17, 2018 and ended on February 28, 2019. An official project handover ceremony for Phase 2 took place on November 16, 2019.

Title: China sends 23rd medical team to Tunisia in 2018 (linked to projects #35605, #14020, #35604, #35603, #12970, #19565, #31082, #35585, #56660)
Description: China has been sending medical teams to Tunisia every two years since 1973. Jiangxi Province has been responsible for sending the medical teams. On November 3, 2018, the welcoming ceremony for the 23rd Chinese medical team to work in Tunisia was held. They were replaced by the 24th team on November 2, 2019, after a tour of one year. This project is completed.

Title: Chinese medical team conduct a free clinic for local people in Kamuli, Uganda
Description: On November 21, the 17th batch of medical teams from China to Uganda went to the location of the Isinba hydropower project in Kamuli province to conduct a free clinic for local people. The event was hosted by the Ugandan Chinese Enterprise Association and implemented by China Water Resources and Hydro Power Corporation. The medical team arrived at the Isinba Hydropower Project Camp on the afternoon of the 20th and took the ferry boat to the other side to start the clinic. Seven doctors worked continuously from the morning to the evening, and received a total of nearly 700 consultations. _x000D_ _x000D_  So far, the medical team has provided five free clinics for the Ugandan people. The clinic was the first time that the 17th batch of medical teams visit Uganda this year.

Title: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hubei Province Government, others, hold COVID-19 prevention conference with multiple countries
Description: On April 13, 2020, the China-Andean National Novel Coronavirus Prevention Video Exchange Conference (中国-安第斯国家新冠肺炎防治视频交流会) took place. At the conference, experts from China shared their strategies and experiences responding to the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic, with the intention of helping experts from Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and other unspecified Andean countries respond to the pandemic in their respective countries. The experts from all countries involved specifically discussed testing, detection methods, prevention and control measures, clinical treatment, and asymptomatic infections. It also included a question-and-answer session._x000D_ _x000D_ From China, experts in attendance were from the hospital associated with the Tongji Medical College (affiliated with Huazhong University of Science and Technology) and Hubei Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention (湖北省疾病预防控制中心). Experts from Bolivia were from the Bolivian Society of Infectious Diseases and Clinical Microbiology (Sociedad Boliviana de Enfermedades Infecciosas y Microbiología Clínica), the Bolivian Ministry of Health, and the Higher University of San Andrés School of Medicine. _x000D_ _x000D_ The videoconference was organized by the Department of Latin America of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Hubei Province Foreign Affairs Office (湖北省外事办 or 中共湖北省委外事工作委员会办公室), and the Hubei Province Health Commission (湖北省卫生健康委员会). The Chinese Embassies in the countries in attendance also provided assistance facilitating.
Funding_Agencies: China Ministry of Foreign Affairs|Hubei Province Health Commission

Title: Chinese Government donates two ambulances and antimalarial drugs to Equatorial Guinea
Description: On March 12, 2015, the representatives of the Chinese Embassy in Equatorial Guinea and the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea signed documents for the donation of two ambulances and antimalarial drugs to Equatorial Guinea. The donation was a continuation from the prior year, in which the Chinese had also donated two ambulances. The cost of the ambulances and antimalarial drugs is unclear.

Title: Chinese Government donates second batch of anti-COVID-19 pandemic materials to Madagascar in July 2020 (linked to project ID#91877 and 91912)
Description: On July 13th, 2020, a donation ceremony for the second batch of anti-pandemic materials was held at the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar. Minister Naharimamy, the Minister of Population, Social Protection and Promotion of Women, Chinese Ambassador Yang Xiaorong, and Brigadier General Elack Andriankaja, General Coordinator of COVID-19, were in attendance. The donation was made to the Fitia association, a charitable organization founded by Mialy Rajoelina Razakandisa, wife of Andry Rajoelina, the president of Madagascar. The grant was organized on the initiative of Peng Liyuan, the first lady of China, and was given by the Chinese government through the the African First Ladies Federation for Development (OAFLAD).   This batch of supplies included medical masks, forehead thermometers, and 7.5 tons of rice. The first donation was in May 2020 (see project ID#91877), and the third batch was handed over in August 2020 (see project ID#91912).

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 14th medical team to Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital
Description: From 2015 to 2017, China's 14th medical team completed its term of service in Zimbabwe. The team arrived to Zimbabwe in April 2015, and consisted of 10 members who were stationed at Harare Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Hospital. The Chinese Government has been sending medical teams to Zimbabwe every two years since 1985.  Hunan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. This project is completed.

Title: Anhui Conch Cement donate medical supplies to Myanmar in May 2020
Description: On May 15th, 2020, Anhui Conch Cement donates medical supplies covid tests, thermometers, and masks to Myanmar Ministry of Health and Sports, Ministry of Commerce, and Myanmar Investment Commission.

Title: Chinese Government donates batch of anti-malarial supplies worth 1.5 billion Kwacha
Description: On December 29, 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government Zambia signed three letters of exchange, one of which was for the donation of a batch of anti-malarial supplies worth 1.5 billion kwacha to Chainama Hills College Hospital. This batch of anti-malarial supplies was officially delivered and handed over to the authorities on September 17, 2013.   The two other letters of exchange that were signed are captured in projects #2337 and #15518.

Title: China-Mongolia Cultural and Education Foundation funds the 2020 'Warm Winter' Project for Mongolian households in need (Linked to Project ID#86962)
Description: According to an August 10, 2020, China-Mongolia CESDF press release, the organization -- in partnership with the Bank of China Representative Office in Ulaanbaatar, the Community of Immigrants in Mongolia, and the Embassy of China in Mongolia -- will be providing livelihood assistance to Mongolian families and Chinese immigrants without the means to live through the winter. The monetary value of the assistance is unknown.  The "Warm Winter" project (Mongolian: "Дулаан өвөл") started in 2014. All associated projects are captured by umbrella Project ID#86962.
Funding_Agencies: Bank of China (BOC)|China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Development Foundation

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 18th medical team to Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital in Libreville and Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital in Franceville
Description: Since 1977, Tianjin Province has been sending medical teams to Gabon. On February 21, 2014, the Chinese Government and the Government of Gabon signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 18th Chinese medical team to Gabon. The team was stationed at the Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital (Hôpital de la Coopération Sino-Gabonaise de Libreville) in the city of Libreville and the Sino-Gabonese Friendship Hospital (Hopital de L'amitie Sino Gabonaise) in the town of Franceville. The team completed its term of service between August 2014 and October 2016.

Title: China donates anti-epidemic materials to Montenegro in April 2020
Description: On April 16, 2020, anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government to fight against the COVID-19 pandemic arrived in Montenegro. The donation was received by representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Title: China donates 40 million Kenyan shillings reproductive health medical equipment to Kenya in 2010
Description: On July 29, 2010, the Chinese government donated reproductive health medical equipment worth 30 million US Dollars to the Kenyan government.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Peru grants 56 boxes of medical supplementary materials to Peruvian Ministry of Health
Description: On January 4, 2002, the Chinese Embassy in Peru presented 56 boxes of medical supplies to the Peruvian Ministry of Health. The supplies were granted to help treat people injured in the December 29, 2001 fire, which started when fireworks erupted in a shopping center in Lima.

Title: Bank of China donates 20,000 masks to KwaZulu-Natal in May 2020 (linked to project ID#93779, 93780, 93791, and 87211)
Description: On May 9, 2020 Bank of China Limited Johannesburg Branch donated 20,000 masks to the KwaZulu-Natal provincial government. The masks were intended to prevent the spread of Covid-19 and prevent the healthcare system from becoming overwhelmed.   Bank of China donated five batches of pandemic materials to South Africa in spring of 2020. In aggregate, the donation was 170,000 masks, 600 protective suits, and 5 ventilators. One donation consisted of 30,000 masks to Gauteng province on April 14, 2020 (see project ID#93779). The next was 100,000 masks, 600 protective suits, and 5 ventilators to South Africa Ministry of Health on May 7, 2020 (see project ID#87211). The final donation was 20,000 masks to KwaZulu-Natal on May 9, 2020, captured in this project. The other two donations were for 10,000 masks and were delivered at an unknown date before May 9, 2020. These donations are captured in project ID#93780 and 93791 respectively.

Title: Zhejiang Provincial Government donates medical equipment worth CAF 2 billion to China-Africa Friendship Hospital in Bangui
Description: On August 6, 2018, the Chinese National Health Commission and the Zhejiang Provincial Government donated 2 billion CAF worth of medical equipment — including digital ultrasound machine, a digital x-ray machine, an anesthesia machine, a blood aspirator for surgical procedures, a ventilator, and other medical equipment (including boxes of the antimalarial drugs) — to the China-Africa Friendship Hospital in the capital city of in Bangui (where a Chinese medical team is stationed, as captured via Project ID#55646). China’s Ambassador to the Central African Republic (CAF), Chen Dong, and the CAF Minister of Health of Central Africa Pierre Somse signed the equipment handover certificate at the donation ceremony. Faustin-Archange Touadéra, the President of the Central African Republic, Pascal Mbereso, head of the China-Africa Friendship Hospital, and Zhu Decai, the leader of the Chinese medical team, were also present at the ceremony.
Funding_Agencies: National Health Commission of China|Zhejiang Provincial Government

Title: Chinese government donates anti-epidemic materials to Malawi
Description: On March 31, 2020, the handover ceremony for the anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government to Malawi was held at the Kamuzu International Airport in Lilongwe. Chinese Ambassador Liu Hongyang and Malawian Minister of Disaster Management Everton Chimulirenji attended the event and delivered speeches. Nearly 50 people also attended the event, including officials from the Ministry of Disaster Affairs, media reporters and airport staff.   Before the ceremony, Ambassador Liu distributed masks to event attendees to remind everyone to take protective measures. After the event, Ambassador Liu also accepted a joint interview with media from China and Malawi.  The materials donated included protective face masks, disposable medical protective clothes, infrared thermometers, protective medical goggles, sterilized surgical gloves and medical isolation shoes.

Title: Sichuan and Henan provincial governments and the city of Xi'an donate medical supplies to Hospital No. 20
Description: On December 1, 2020, the Chinese Consulate General in St. Petersburg handed over medical supplies donated by the Provincial Government of Sichuan, the Provincial Government of Henan, and the city of Xi'an to St. Petersburg Hospital No. 20. The donation included 200 protective suits and 200,000 medical masks, equivalent to a roughly 20-day supply. The contribution would allow the hospital to allocate its money towards other costs such as medicines. The ceremony was attended by Chinese Consul General, the chief physician of Hospital No. 20, and representatives from Sichuan, Henan, and the city of Xi'an.
Funding_Agencies: Henan Provincial Government|Sichuan Provincial Government|Xi'an Municipal Government

Title: Chinese Donation of mobile clinics to Sudan worth 10 million Chinese yuan
Description: On June 2, 2010, an agreement was signed by China's Ambassador to Sudan, Li Chengwen, and Sudan's Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs on handing over about ten mobile clinics and medical equipment for Darfur at the cost of 10 million Chinese yuan. The ceremony was attended by Ambassador Charles Menyang, Sudan's Undersecretary of the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs. The exact commitment date is unknown.

Title: 12th Chinese Medical Team Offers Free Consultations (Linked to #62619, #62628)
Description: On November 16, 2018, the 12th Chinese medical team (project #62628) provided free medical consultations to nearly 200 Namibians and distributed Chinese medicine at a clinic event co-organized by the Embassy and Red Cross Society. The consultations were given to residents of Havana Primary School and the surrounding communities. At the same event, the Embassy donated 100,000 NAD worth of hygienic supplies (project #62619).

Title: CCCC Shanghai Dredging Co., Ltd. donated 10,000 masks to Uruguay in April 2020
Description: On April 9, 2020, CCCC Shanghai Dredging Co., Ltd. handed over a donation of 10,000 masks to the Consulate General of Uruguay in Shanghai. The masks were to be subsequently delivered to Uruguay for combatting the COVID-19 pandemic.  The donation was worth an estimated USD 4,000, per the Harvard Mask Diplomacy Dataset.

Title: Nanning Municipal Government donated medical supplies to Vientiane City and Oudomxay Province
Description: Sometime between March to April 2020, Nanning Municipal Government donated medical supplies to the city of Vientiane City and Oudomxay Province, Laos.

Title: Chinese Government provides medical team to Sri Lanka following 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
Description: On December 26, 2004, an earthquake struck the Indian Ocean, causing subsequent tsunamis in countries like Sri Lanka bordering the Indian Ocean. In response, the Chinese Government dispatched a series of medical teams to assist Sri Lanka. On January 4, 2005, the third Chinese medical team, consisting of 5 surgeons from Beijing Friendship Hospital, 2 nurses from Beijing Friendship Hospital, and 7 epidemic prevention workers from the Beijing Center for Disease Control, arrived in Hikkaduwa. The team was later joined by 3 medical professionals from Macau and 1 official from the Beijing Municipal Commission of Population and Family Planning. The 14-member team returned to China on January 19, 2005.  In total, the Chinese Government dispatched four "international medical teams for Indian Ocean Tsunami relief." The first and second were sent to Thailand (captured via Project ID #34816), the third was sent to Sri Lanka (captured via Project ID #33231), and the fourth was sent to Indonesia (captured via Project ID #35113).   Morevoer, the Chinese Government also provided about USD 63 million for tsunami relief in total (see Project IDs #33223, #33226, #33263, #34136, #34959, #34960, #34961, #35112, #35149, #33253, #38556, #39145, #39186, #33248, #34820, #1474, #39187, #42623).

Title: Chinese Government donates medical equipment worth RMB 400,000 to Guyana
Description: On December 7, 2009, the China Ministry of Health and Jiangsu Provincial People's Government donated medical equipment worth RMB 400,000 ($12 million GYD) to Guyana's  Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation. It was specifically donated to the Eye Centre and Centre for Laparoscopic Surgery at GPHC. The donated equipment included laparoscopic instruments.
Funding_Agencies: China Ministry of Health|Jiangsu Provincial People's Government

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 3.5 million grant for provision of medicines and medical equipment
Description: On December 7, 2009, these Chinese Government and the Government of Ukraine signed an RMB 3.5 million (about USD 500,000) grant agreement for the provision of facemasks, latex gloves, medicines, as well as medical and diagnostic equipment. The primary purpose of the grant was to help Ukraine prevent the spread of the A/H1N1 flu and acute respiratory infections. Ukrainian Ambassador to China, Yuriy Kostenko, and Chinese Assistant Minister of Commerce, Chong Quan, signed the agreement.

Title: Chinese Ministry of Defense donated anti-pandemic medical materials to the Tunisian Ministry of Defense in June 2020
Description: On June 3, 2020, The Chinese Ministry of Defense provided the Tunisian Ministry of National Defense with new coronary pneumonia epidemic prevention and control medical supplies. At this handover ceremony, Ambassador Wang Wenbin, Defense Military Office Wang Zhenyu, and Brigadier General Vergani went to the airport to attend the handover ceremony. The purpose of this donation is to help Tunisia fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

Title: China donates Ping Pong Table and Equipment to Sri Lanka
Description: According to a media report on December 8, 2013, China donated a table tennis table and equipment to Devi Balika Vidyalaya Colombo, Sri Lanka, through the Chinese Embassy. Sri Lanka-China society coordinated this donation with Jiangsu Province Friendship Association with Foreign countries.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates masks to the Los Santos Government in April 2020
Description: On April 22, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Panama, through the Las Tablas Chamber of Commerce, donated 2,000 surgical masks to the Los Santos Governor's office. The masks were to be distributed to workers on the front line combatting COVID-19. The donation was announced through a tweet by the head of the Chinese Embassy's Economic and Commercial Counsellor's Office, Wang Jian.

Title: China donates $303,595 USD to WHO for medical supply chain assets in Maldives following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
Description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID #35256), on 4 April 2005, the Chinese government donated $303, 595 USD to the World Health Organization (WHO) for replenishing essential medical supplies, equipment, and assets in Maldives following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (UN project code is TSU-MDV-05/H03-MALDIVES). OCHA marked this contribution as fully paid. This purpose of this project was to ensure that "medical supply chains function as efficiently as possible and respond to the needs of end-users" (see UN doc p. 46 and WHO doc p. 9).

Title: Chinese Government agrees to donate 2 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $36 million in December 2021
Description: The Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinovac Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Malaysia on July 16, 2021. Upon arrival, the vaccines were escorted by the Royal Malaysian Police Force (PDRM) to Pharmaniaga’s warehouse before being distributed nationwide as part of the National COVID-19 Immunization Program. Then, on September 29, 2021, Dato’ Saifuddin Abdullah, Malaysia's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Wang Yi, State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), held a telephone conversation. Wang Yi conveyed the decision by the Chinese Government to contribute an additional 1 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Malaysia, on the basis of the deep friendship between the two countries and peoples. It is unclear if the Chinese Government fulfilled this commitment.   Then, in December 2021, representatives of the Chinese Government and the Government of Malaysia attended the Malaysia-China High Level Committee (HLC) on Cooperation in the Post-Covid-19 Era. At that meeting, the Chinese Government reportedly made a commitment to donate an additional 2 million Sinovac Covid-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Malaysia. It is unclear if the Chinese Government fulfilled this commitment.

Title: China donates dental equipment worth K300,000 to East New Britain Health Authority in November 2021
Description: On November 16, 2021, China donated dental equipment worth K300,000 to the East New Britain Health Authority in Papua New Guinea. Governor Nakikus Konga of East New Britain Province said the equipment would go to Nonga General Hospital.

Title: China's CHEC donates US20,000 to Jamaica's Olympic Team (Linked to project #72027)
Description: In August 2012 China Harbour Engineering Company handed over US$20,000 to the Jamaica Olympic Association in support of the Jamaican athletes in their 2012 London Olympics Games competition, according to a Jamaica Observer article. The donation was followed up by a J$2 million donation for a celebration following the athletes' return (see project #72027).

Title: China Eximbank provides loan for Zaire Provincial Hospital Construction Project
Description: On 20 August, 2012, Angola's Minister of Health laid the cornerstone for the Zaire Provincial Hospital Construction Project. This project was reportedly financed by a China Eximbank loan. The value and terms of this loan are unknown. The total project cost was estimated to be about $42 million.   This hospital is located in Kiowa, on the outskirts of the city of M'banza Kongo (Mbanza-Kongo), which is the capital of Zaire Province. It was supposed to be the largest comprehensive hospital in Zaire Province, with a total construction area of ​​about 23,000 square meters and 332 beds. China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began on 7 November 2013.  Then, on 1 June, 2014, several Chinese MOFCOM officials inspected the project site. It is unknown whether of when this project was completed.

Title: Government of China sends anti-epidemic medical expert team to Sudan
Description: On May 28, 2020, the Chinese Government announced it would be sending a team of anti-epidemic medical experts to Sudan to fight the COVID-19 epidemic. The team arrived on the 28th. On June 6th, 2020, the medical experts met with officials in Sudan and discussed the prevention and control of COVID-19 with members of the 35th Chinese medical team in the country. On June 9th the team held consultations with Sudan's health officials on the necessary measures needed to be taken to prevent the COVID-19 spread.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 9th medical team to El-Maarouf National Hospital Center, Fomboni Hospital, and Hombo Hospital
Description: Since 1994, Guangxi Province has been sending medical teams to Comoros every two years. On February 24, 2012, the Chinese Government and the Government of Comoros signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 9th Chinese medical team to Comoros. The team was stationed at El-Maarouf National Hospital Center (Le Centre hospitalier national El-Maarouf) on the island of Grande Comore, Fomboni Hospital (L’hôpital de Fomboni or Centre Hospitalier de Fomboni) on the island of Mwali, and Hombo Hospital (L’hôpital Hombo) on the island of Anjouan. The team completed its term of service between July 2012 and July 2014.

Title: Chinese Government grants $4.7 million for the provision of medical equipment to 5 regional rehabilitation centers
Description: In 2016, the Chinese government agreed to grant $4.7 million USD to the Ministry of Health of Uzbekistan for the provision of modern medical equipment to regional rehabilitation centers for the disabled. The grant was distributed to equip 5 rehabilitation centers (Namangen, Navoi, Jizzakh, Samarkand and Tashkent regions) for the disabled with laboratories and medical equipment, including modern diagnostic and physiotherapy equipment, X-ray diagnostic equipment, exercise therapy equipment, and laboratory equipment._x000D_ _x000D_ According to the Review.Uz article, the MRI scanners were delivered to Uzbekistan in 2018.

Title: Chinese Government donates batch of anti-malarial drugs
Description: On September 10th, 2013, the Chinese Government signed a handover certificate with the Malagasy Ministry of Health for the donation of a batch of anti-malaria medicines, according to the Chinese Ministry of Commerce. Chinese Ambassador Yang Min and Malagasy Minister of Health and Family Planning Joanita Naimananram attended the ceremony and signed the certificate.

Title: Cambodia’s women’s national football team receives training in China [Linked to Project ID#48887]
Description: In September 2021, the Cambodian women’s national football team received training in China. The team consisted of 22 members that spent 90 days in China to train. This training is provided in preparation for the 32nd SEA Games that will be held in Cambodia in 2023. This football team is the first female national team to compete in the games. The 22 female players are from four different clubs in Cambodia, including Kampong Speu Provincial Education, Youth and Sports Department FC, Phnom Penh Crown FC, Preah Khan Reach Svay Rieng FC,, and Battambang Provincial Education, Youth, and Sports Department FC.  This training is provided by collaboration between the Football Federation of Cambodia (FFC) and the Chinese Government through the Cambodian SEA Games Organizing Committee (CAMSOC). The training is part of grant aid provided by China for the Morodok Techo National Stadium Construction project. The details on this project are captured in Project ID #48887.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 18th medical team to Maputo Central Hospital
Description: Since 1976, the Chinese Government has sent 22 medical teams to Mozambique from Sichuan Province. On September 20, 2010, the Chinese and Mozambican governments signed a protocol agreement, dispatching the 18th medical team to Mozambique. The 14 members of the 18th medical team were stationed at Maputo Central Hospital and they completed their term of service between 2010 and August 2012.  Other batches include the 13th medical team (#758) sent in 2002, the 14th medical team (#35668) sent in 2004, the 15th medical team (#58090) sent in 2004, the 16th medical team (#57430) sent in 2006, the 17th medical team in 2010(#57950), the 19th medical team in 2012 (#57908), and the 20th medical team in 2014 (#60784).

Title: Chinese Embassy donates anti-epidemic supplies to Bahamas Ministry of Health in April 2020
Description: On April 4, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in the Commonwealth of the Bahamas donated 1,000 Coronavirus testing kits, KN-95 masks, gloves, and other supplies to the Bahamas Ministry of Health in order to combat the Coronavirus. The Chinese Embassy in the Commonwealth of the Bahamas handed over the supplies.

Title: Chinese Government donates fourth batch of medical supplies for COVID-19 relief to Barbados in July 2020 (linked to project ID#93553, 71948, and 71976)
Description: On July 29, 2020, medical supplies donated by the Chinese government, were handed over to the Barbadian Ministry of Health and Wellness. The grant included 5,000 N95 respirators and 40,000 surgical face masks to fight the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic.   The first batch of supplies arrived in late March (see project ID#93553), the second donation arrived on April 1, 2020 (see project ID#71948), and the third batch was delivered on April 25, 2020 (see project ID#71976).

Title: Chinese Embassy donates sporting goods to Madagascar State Secretariat of the Gendarmerie
Description: On February 22, 2018, Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong, attended a ceremony commemorating the Chinese Embassy's donation of sporting goods to the State Secretariat of the Madagascar Gendarmerie. Landry Amaha Varisua, State Secretariat of the Gendarmerie of the Ministry of National Defense, and members of the Gendarmerie basketball team attended the ceremony. The donation appeared to include several basketballs, basketball shoes, and towels.

Title: China National Complete Plant Import & Export Corporation Group (COMPLANT) donates 3,000 testing swabs to Barbados to fight COVID-19 in June 2020
Description: On June 12, 2020, China National Complete Plant Import Export Corporation (COMPLANT) donated 3,000 testing swabs to the Barbados Ministry of Heath to fight COVID-19.   On the same day, the Hunan Provincial Government donated USD 31,920 worth of medical supplies (see project ID#71949)
Funding_Agencies: China National Complete Plant Import & Export Corporation Group (COMPLANT)

Title: Shandong Gold Mining Co. contributes to donation of 215,000 Coronavirus Testing Kits to Argentina's Ministry of Health in April 2020
Description: On April 23, 2020, Argentina's Ministry of Health received a donation of 214,500 COVID-19 testing kits, valued at ARS 275 million (about USD 4.1 million), from members of the Argentine Chamber of Mining Entrepreneurs (CAEM). Shandong Gold Mining Co. and Barrick Gold – partners in the Veladero Mine joint venture – lead the donation and provided the largest contribution: 157,000 RT-PCR and RNA test kits. The kits were to be distributed by the Ministry of Health throughout the country, with provinces with a large mining presence targeted in particular.  In monetary terms, Barrick reported that the Veladero joint venture's contribution was USD 2 million, and Barrick contributed another USD 1 million separately.  The kits were purchased from Wuhan BGI Clinical Laboratory Limited, and magnetic separator racks for test specimens were purchased from Shandong Shanzuo Holding Group. The supplies were then transported from China to Ezeiza International Airport on April 22, 2020, via Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 1071, as part of the "Air Bridge" ("Puente Aéreo") initiative.  In addition to CAEM, the Municipal Government of San Juan and Argentina's National Ministry of Mining helped facilitate the donation. Other contributors to the CAEM's portion of the donation included Cerro Vanguardia, Yamana Gold, Minera Santa Cruz, Glencore Pachon, SSR Mining Puna Operaciones, Minera Triton, Pan American Silver Argentina, Eramine Sudamerica, Minera Don Nicolás, Argentina Fortescue, San Juan Chamber of Mining, and GEMERA.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD 800,000 for COVID-19 response via United Nations Children's Fund in Myanmar in May 2020
Description: In May 2020, Chinese government provides USD 800,000 for COVID-19 response in Myanmar.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 50 million interest-free loan for China-Yemen Friendship Hospital Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#65175)
Description: On April 6, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Yemeni Government signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an RMB 40 million interest-free loan (captured in Project ID#65175) for the China-Yemen Friendship Hospital Construction Project. Then, on December 18, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Yemeni Government signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed an RMB 50 million interest-free loan (captured in Project ID#65174) for the China-Yemen Friendship Hospital Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) issued both of these loans and they were approved by the Yemeni Cabinet in July 2010 and passed into law by the Yemeni Parliament in August 2010 (Law No. 9 of 2010 and Law No. 10 of 2010).   The proceeds of the loans were used to finance a project implementation contract that was signed with Nantong Sanjian Holdings (Group) Co., Ltd. (or 江苏南通三建集团有限公司 or 南通三建) on March 9, 2010. The purpose of this project was to construct the 120-bed China-Yemen Friendship Hospital (or 48 Model Hospital) in the capital city of Sana'a. The project commenced on June 17, 2010 and passed a mid-term MOFCOM acceptance on March 20, 2011. The originally expected duration of project implementation was 26 months. However, during construction, war broke out in Yemen and the project was forced to shut down on May 29, 2011. 106 Chinese contractors (members of the project team) were evacuated on May 31, 2011. Then, on June 1, 2012, MOFCOM approved the resumption of project implementation. The project was completed and handed over to the local authorities on June 19, 2013. A formal handover certificate was issued on May 20, 2014. An opening ceremony took place on the same day.

Title: Government of China sends sixteen-member medical team to Guyana in 2021
Description: On February 9, 2021, Guyana's Minister of Health welcomed a sixteen-member medical team of doctors from China. The medical team included doctors specializing in various fields such as general surgery, burns and plastic surgery, orthopedics, nephrology, acupuncturist and moxibustion therapy, radiology, ophthalmology, obstetrics and gynecology, anesthesiology, and pathology.  China has been sending medical teams to Guyana since 1993.

Title: China sends their 4th medical team to Liberia
Description: Since 2005, China has sent medical teams to Liberia every other year. On June 1, 2011 Chinese ambassador to Liberia Zhao Jianhuo and Health Minister Dr. Walter Gwenigale signed a partnership agreement aimed at strengthening Liberia's health sector by sending the 4th medical team. Under the agreement, Chinese medical doctors will continue to help Liberia's largest referral hospital, the John F. Kennedy Medical Center, in the provision of medical services to the needy. The agreement provides that the Chinese government will continue to bring Chinese medical doctors to the country to take up various assignments in the health sector of the country._x000D_ _x000D_ Other medical teams to Liberia: See Project #1594, Project #30735, Project #30736, Project #30737_x000D_ According to a 2011 Working Series report, China has been sending medical teams to Liberia since 1984. The medical team was withdrew in1989 but resumed in 2005.

Title: China donates a batch of medical supplies to Tanzania in September 2021
Description: On September 1st, 2021, Chian donated a batch of epidemic prevention materials to Tanzania as the third wave of the epidemic hits Tanzania. The handover of materials was done at the China Assistance Center in Tanzania. The purpose of this donation is to help Tanzania fight against the pandemic.
