However, it is known that the proceeds of the loan were to be used by the borrower to partially finance a commercial contract worth 89 million Kina that the Government of Papua New Guinea signed with China Jiangsu International Economic and Technical Cooperation Corporation Ltd (CJIC) on August 14, 2014.   The purpose of the project is to expand and upgrade sewerage system of Kokopo Town — a growing international tourist destination — to account for ongoing urbanization and continue providing the residents and public & private institutions in the area with an acceptable standard of living while minimizing the spread of water borne diseases.   The project has four primary components. The first component is the source mobilization phase where the contractor (CJIC) will assemble the materials necessary for construction at the project site. The second component will involve preparation at the sites where the sewerage ponds will be constructed. The third component will involve the construction of the sewerage ponds, pipe lines, and pump stations in the town of Ulaveo. The fourth and final component will be making sure the project meets industrial standards.   Upon completion, it was envisaged that the sewerage system would have 19 pump stations along a reticulated sewerage system and two sewerage treatment ponds.  CJIC is the contractor responsible for implementation. Its work is being overseen by Islands Design and Engineering, a locally owned engineering firm. The project commenced in 2016 and it was originally expected to take 24 months to complete (6 months for design and 18 months for construction). However, the project encountered various problems and delays.   In November 2017, concerns were raised by a nearby resort (Rapopo Plantation Resort) that the sewerage plant at Ulaveo was too close to the resort and put at risk dolphins in a nearby lagoon. The resort’s Executive Director, James Ipang, warned that the treatment plant would be pumping waste into pristine sea water near Kokopo and Rabaul towns. He also said that the crystal-clear waters were a breeding and feeding ground for a pod of 300 dolphins directly in front of the plant, and that other alternatives should be considered.   The East New Britainn Chamber of Commerce Incorporated raised similar concerns in August 2019. As of December 31, 2019, the project had achieved a 98% completion rate, and the fourth component of the project was pending certification because of public concerns that the sewerage ponds were constructed too close to local communities, businesses, and the sea.

Title: China grants funds for Health Center in Cote d'Ivoire
Description: In 2014, China granted funds for a health center (Centre de sante or 阿加美卫生中心) in Adjamé, Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire. The official completion ceremony took place on 8 July 2014. The project value and construction start date are unknown. _x000D_ _x000D_ This project is part of the Sino-Africa People to People Friendship Action program (中非民间友好行动).

Title: Chinese Government donates the second batch of anti-COVID-19 pandemic supplies to Guinea in June 2020
Description: On June 18th, 2020, the second batch of anti-COVID-19 pandemic supplies donated by the Chinese government to Guinea arrived in Conakry. Chinese Ambassador Huang Wei and Guinean Foreign Minister Toure went to the airport to receive the supplies.  Ambassador Huang and Foreign Minister Toure signed handover certificates on behalf of the two governments respectively and were interviewed by several national TV stations and other local mainstream media. The first batch of medical supplies sent by China to address the COVID-19 pandemic was sent to Guinea in April 2020 (Project ID# 92697).

Title: China sends fourth medical team to Sao Tome & Principe in 2019
Description: On January 25, 2019, the fourth Chinese medical team flew from China to Sao Tome and Principe. The third medical team finished its one-year tour on February 2, 2019, and was replaced at this time by the fourth Chinese medical team. Both teams are sponsored by the West China Hospital at Sichuan University. The fourth team is said to consist of 8 medical experts.   It was originally planned that the team would return to China in January 2020, but because of the Covid-19 pandemic, the team postponed returning to China, and instead participated in the local front-line anti-pandemic work. The fourth Chinese medical team returned to China on October 5, 2020. They were replaced by the fifth Chinese medical team, which arrived in Sao Tome and Principe between September 9 and 14, 2020.

Title: China sends 13th Medical Team to Uganda
Description: China has been sending medical teams to Uganda since 1983. Yunnan Province has been responsible for sending the teams. The 13th medical team of 8 members worked in Uganda from August 2007 to August 2009. As part of this medical team project, China donated 300,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to Ghana for the Jinja Hospital (金贾医院).

Title: Chinese Government donates 3.5 million Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $63 million in December 2021
Description: In 2021, the Chinese Government donated approximately 3.6 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Bolivia. A cooperation agreement was signed between China National Pharmaceutical Group and the Government of Bolivia on February 11, 2021. The Chinese Government delivered 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Bolivia on February 24, 2021. Then, on March 30, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 100,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Bolivia. Then, on August 17, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Bolivia. Then, on December 26, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 3.5 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Bolivia.

Title: Government of China donates respiratory humidifiers to Bangladesh for COVID-19 relief
Description: On June 29, 2020, the Government of Bangladesh received a donation of respiratory humidifiers from the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka. The purpose of this donation was to help Bangladesh combat COVID-19 in the country. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: China donates 720,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to Equatorial Guinea
Description: On December 8, 2017, the Chinese Embassy in Equatorial Guinea handed over 720,000 RMB worth of medical equipment to the Equatorial Guinean government. Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Health State Secretary Daniel Cima and Commercial Counselor Su Jianguo attended the ceremony and representatives of the two governments signed the transfer certificate. The donation included medicine, white coats, bed sheets and medical equipment. The handover ceremony was held in Malabo.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 87.1 million grant for Central Laboratory of the Mongolian State Administration of Technical Supervision Construction Project
Description: In 2008, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mongolia signed an exchange of letters, which committed RMB 87.1 million of grant funding for the Central Laboratory of the Mongolian State Administration of Technical Supervision Construction Project. The purpose of the project was to construct a six-story laboratory — called the Mongolian National Technical Supervision Administration Center Laboratory or the Central Laboratory of the General Agency for Specialized Inspection (GASI) — for the testing of food and drugs using international standards.   The new Central Laboratory building is located on a government-owned land plot of 0.12 hectares within the territory of II Khoroo, Khan-Uul district, on Chinggis Street in Ulaanbaatar. This site was selected because it is located near industrial enterprises, and the services of the new laboratory will be close to many of its customers. There are few residences in this area also so the laboratory was also located to avoid any impacts to residential population. The Central Laboratory was designed to be connected to municipal water supply, wastewater collection, stormwater collection, central heating and central electrical systems of Ulaanbaatar. Hunan Construction Engineering Group (“Хунан констракшн инженеринг” групп) was the contractor responsible for the implementation of the project. The project commenced on June 18, 2010 and ended on December 15, 2012. A project handover certificate was issued on January 30, 2013, and an opening ceremony for the laboratory was held on March 1, 2013. The project was originally expected to reach completion in October 2011.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 60 million grant for construction of hospital and school in Baffa after 2005 earthquake (Linked to Project ID#53903)
Description: After the earthquake that struck Pakistan in 2005, the Chinese Government pledged to help with reconstruction efforts. On November 24, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Pakistan signed an RMB 80 million grant agreement, which provided 60 million RMB for the construction of a hospital and school in Baffa. The project involved the construction of a 6,525-square-meter high school (GHSS Baffa) that would cost Rs 487.5 million and a small hospital of 4,400 square meters (THQ Baffa) that would cost Rs 412.5 million.   The school would be designed to accommodate 720 students. At the beginning of 2011, an advance team of 6 people from the Shandong Expressway Qilu Construction Group arrived in Baffa and began the project preparation work. Construction started on July 2, 2011. Then, from December 16-22, 2011, a mid-term quality inspection team organized by the Economic Cooperation Bureau of China's Ministry of Commerce inspected and accepted the project. Based on the 2013 newsletter, the two buildings were constructed around February 2013.

Title: Gansu Province provides RMB 700,000 worth of traditional Chinese medicine to Madagascar in September 2021
Description: In September of 2021, the Gansu Provincial Government donated RMB 700,000 worth of traditional Chinese medicine to Madagascar. The donation included four different types of medicine targeted: one designed to boost immune systems of susceptible people; one aimed to treat mild to severe cases of COVID-19; one for serious infections; and another to help patients recover.

Title: China donated medical equipment to the National Health Services of Samoa
Description: On March 10, 2015, the Chinese Embassy donated medical equipment to the National Health Services of Samoa. The equipment included a portable ultrasound scanner, fetus ventilator and others to be used for surgery, the paediatric unit, and imaging. The donation was presented by Li Yanduan, the Chinese Ambassador, to Dr. Leao Tuitama, the Samoan Minister of Health, in Apia.

Title: Chinese Government provides $5 million grant for provision of medical equipment to China-Yemen Friendship Hospital (Linked to Project ID#65175 and Project ID#65174)
Description: On January 28, 2013, the Chinese Government donated medical equipment and furniture worth $5,000,000 to the China-Yemen Friendship Hospital (or 48 Model Hospital) in the capital city of Sana'a. The grant agreement was signed by Yemen’s Minister of Planning and International Cooperation Mohammed al-Sa'adi and the Chinese Ambassador to Yemen Chang Hwa. The equipment handover ceremony took place on October 2, 2013.

Title: 12th medical team dispatched to University of Zambia Teaching Hospital, Ndola General Hospital, Livingstone Central Hospital, Kitwe Central Hospital, Thomson Hospital, and Kabwe General Hospital
Description: China has been sending medical teams to Zambia since 1978. Henan Province is responsible for sending the teams. On November 14, 2002, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zambia signed a protocol agreement dispatching the 12th Chinese medical team to Zambia. The team's 28 members were distributed across the University of Zambia Teaching Hospital (also known as University Teaching Hospital), Ndola General Hospital, Livingstone Central Hospital, Kitwe Central Hospital, Thomson Hospital, and Kabwe General Hospital. The team completed its term of service between 2003 and 2005.   According to the protocol agreement, the Government of Zambia was responsible for the team's return tickets to China, housing, and immigration fees. The Government of China was responsible for plane tickets to Zambia, salaries, and general living expenses during service.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials to Peruvian Ministry of Health in February 2021
Description: On February 12, 2021, the Chinese Embassy donated anti-epidemic materials to the Peruvian Ministry of Health. The materials included oxygen concentrators and portable pulse oximeters. This donation was made to support Peru’s COVID-19 response efforts. The estimated monetary value of this donation is Sol $1,685,419.6.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 80 million interest-free loan for Orotta Referral Hospital Construction Project (linked to #30533)
Description: In 2000, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 80 million (equal to about $10 million) interest-free loan to the Government of Eritrea for the Orotta Referral Hospital Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a 200-bed hospital in the capital city of Asmara in an area that occupies 10,000 square meters. About 100 Chinese workers were employed to support this project. China Tianjin International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Corporation was the implementing contractor. Construction began in October 2000 and the project was officially handed over to the Eritrean authorities on May 31, 2003.  In 2009, the Chinese Government provided a $5 million grant for the renovation and expansion of this hospital (see Project #30533).

Title: MOFCOM provides RMB 50 million grant for Douala Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital Construction Project (linked to #22839, #314, #58705)
Description: On August 3, 2009, China's Ministry of Commerce signed a grant agreement -- through China Development Bank (CDB) -- worth RMB 50,000,000 with Cameroon's Ministry of Public Health for the construction of and equipment for the Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital in the city of Douala (Projet de construction et d’équipement de l’hôpital gynéco­obstétrique et pédiatrique de Douala (HGOPD)).  Shanxi Construction Engineering was responsible for the implementation of this project.  Construction for the Gyneco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital was completed November 17, 2015, and it was handed over on the same day.  Two interest-free loans from MOFCOM were also provided for this specific project (one worth RMB 30 million, as captured in linked ProjectID#58705, and one worth RMB 50 million, which is captured in linked Project ID#314.  In February 2007, the Chinese Government pledged the provision of expertise on studies for the construction of the Gynaeco-Obstetrics and Paediatric Hospital of Douala worth FCFA 44,800,000 (see linked ProjectID#22839).

Title: Chinese Embassy donates sports equipment to the Roche-Bois community center
Description: On December 7, 2007, the Chinese Embassy donated sports equipment, including table tennis, rackets, and footballs, to the Roche-Bois community center.

Title: Beibu Gulf Holding (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd along Chinese Embassy in Malaysia and Chinese enterprises donate 600,0000 face masks to Malaysian Ministry of Defense (Linked to Project ID#90232, 93894, 93895, 93896, 93897)
Description: On March 27, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Malaysia (Project ID#90232), Jianhui Paper (Project ID#93897), Beibu Gulf Holding (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (Project ID#93898), Malaysia-China Kuantan Industrial Park (Project ID#93894), Tencent Holdings Ltd (Project ID#93896), and Fosun Foundation (Project ID#93895) collectively donated 550,000 face masks and 50,000 N95 masks to the Malaysian Ministry of Defense to combat Covid-19. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: China donates $46,905 USD to WHO for disease surveillance in Maldives following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
Description: According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service (flow ID #35259), on 4 April 2005, the Chinese government donated $46,905 USD to the World Health Organization (WHO) for disease surveillance, verification, and response in Maldives following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (UN project code is TSU-MDV-05/H06-MALDIVES). OCHA marked this contribution as fully paid._x000D_ _x000D_ The purpose of this project was "to track patterns of life-threatening diseases among those at risk through the prompt set-up of a surveillance and early warning system, with regular epidemiological reports".

Title: Chinese government donates face masks and shields to the Philippines
Description: On October 30, 2020, the Chinese government, through its Ministry of Public Security (MPS), donated over 40 boxes of face masks and face shields to the Bureau of Customs (BOC). The donation from the MPS of the People's Republic of China was received by Commissioner Rey Leonardo Guerrero together with Deputy Commissioner for Intelligence Group (IG) Raniel Ramiro, during the turnover ceremony on Friday at the OCOM Conference Room, Port of Manila, the BOC said in a statement. According to the BOC, this batch of medical supplies consisting of 20 boxes of face masks and 22 boxes of face shields, the personal protective equipment shall be used in ensuring the safety and health of the men and women of the Bureau in the delivery of efficient public service.

Title: China sends 17th Medical Team to Tanzania
Description: On May 17, 2001, the Chinese government agreed to send a 17th Medical Team to Tanzania. The 25-person medical team includes translators, maintenance, and logistic technical experts, among others. The team worked in four hospitals: Mhibili Medical Center, Dodoma, Msoma, and Tabora Provincial Hospital. The medical team will assist Tanzanian medical staff with medical tasks, provide specialized training, and exchange medical experience. Their mission began in August 2001 and ended in August 2003.  Under the agreement, Tanzania is responsible for providing the medical team with living expenses; China and Tanzania share joint responsibility for providing salaries, transportation, and medical expenses. Shandong Province was responsible for selecting and preparing the team.   On August 15th, 2003, the Tanzanian Ministry of Health held a banquet for the team and awarded all team members with honorary certificates, thanking the medical team for 35 years of assistance. China has been sending medical teams to Tanzania every two years since 1968.

Title: Chinese Government donates 200,000 Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses worth $3.6 million in December 2021 to Government of Nicaragua
Description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 3 million doses of COVID-19  vaccines to the Government of Nicaragua. On December 9, 2021, the Government of Nicaragua suspended its diplomatic relations with the Republic of China ("Taiwan") and restored its diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China ("China"). Three days later, on December 12, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 200,000 donated doses of Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccines to the Government of Nicaragua. Then, on December 24, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered another 800,000 donated doses of Sinopharm COVID-19  vaccines to the Government of Nicaragua.  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 2 million donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Nicaragua on October 1, 2022.

Title: Chinese embassy donates sports equipment to Malawi Police
Description: On November 17, 2008, the Chinese embassy granted sports equipment to the Malawi Police. The value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government donates USD 738,822 via United Nations Population Fund to Mozambique in November 2021
Description: In November 2021, Chinese government provides USD 738,822 as part of CNA02/SRH/Mozambique Humanitarian Response Plan 2021.  This project is captured in UNOCHA Financial Tracking Service as Flow ID #241967.

Title: Chinese Government provides $4 million cash grant for Temporary Covid-19 Isolation Hospital Project
Description: Between the Government of Pakistan’s Fiscal Year 2019 (July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020) and Fiscal Year 2020 (July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021), the Chinese Government and the Government of Pakistan signed letters of exchange, which officially committed a $4 million cash donation for a Quarantine Hospital Project (or Temporary Covid-19 Isolation Hospital Project).  Construction began on March 25, 2020 and ended on May 10, 2020. Then, on July 9, 2020, Yao Jing, Ambassador to Pakistan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan attended the inauguration and opening ceremony of the China-aided COVID-19 Temporary Isolation Hospital — also known as the China-aided Isolation Hospital and Infections Treatment Center (IHITC) — in Islamabad. Pakistani Army Chief of Staff Bajwa, Minister of Planning Umer, Minister of Information Faraz, Chairman of the National Disaster Committee Afzal, Chairman of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor Bureau Asim and others attended.  According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan, the IHITC was built in 40 days  with the cooperation from China. The hospital has five different wards and 250 beds with maximum facilities to diagnose and treat the infectious diseases.

Title: China implements 'Bright Action' Cataract Surgery Project in Chad in 2018 (linked to project #56021, #86658)
Description: On September 28, 2018, the opening ceremony of the "Bright Action" Surgery Project ("Action la Lumiere" or 光明行) was held at the China-Chad Friendship Hospital and was attended by Chinese Ambassador Li Jinjin as well as Chadian Minister of Health Saleh, and a number of Chinese medical aid workers. The project will be done under the guidance of the International Exchange and Cooperation Center of the National Health Commission, organized by the Jiangxi Provincial Health Commission, and have experts from the Affiliated Eye Hospital of Nanchang University. This ophthalmological campaign, the cost of which is estimated at nearly 100,000,000 FCFA, is entirely financed by the Government of the People's Republic of China. Medical equipment worth 2 million RMB was donated to Chad during the ceremony (described in project #56021).   On October 15, 2018, the 2018 team returned to China after performing 233 surgeries.   As of October 31st, 2019, a total of 494 free cataract surgeries were completed through the project, with 9 cases of free complex ocular fundus disease and glaucoma surgery being carried out in 2019 alone. The "Bright Action" project has had 2 phases so far, with the first phase starting in September 2018 and the second phase spanning from August 31st to September 9th, 2019 (linked to #86658). Per the agreement, there will be more Bright Action Programs each year.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates materials to Chad National Blood Transfusion Center
Description: On April 26, 2012, Chinese Embassy in Chad donated materials to Chad's National Blood Transfusion Center. Chinese Ambassador to Chad, Qian Jin, oversaw the agreement and made a speech in which he discussed the state of Chinese-Chad healthcare relations. The donation included a television and a computer, among other things. The total value of the donation is not known.

Title: PowerChina donates personal protective equipment to Ghana's Ministry of Roads and Highways
Description: On April 14, 2020, on behalf of its parent organization, the Power Construction Corporation of China (POWERCHINA), PowerChina International Group Limited (PCIGL) donated personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies to Ghana's Ministry of Roads and Highways. The total value of this donation is unknown.

Title: Sinopharm and Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs send RMB 1,500,000 worth of COVID-19 vaccines and medical supplies to Myanmar
Description: On August 28, 2021, medical supplies and COVID-19 vaccines worth RMB 1,500,000 arrived in Myanmar from Sinopharm and the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The medical supplies consisted of ventilators, oxygen generators, medical protective masks, and medical protective clothing. The purpose of this donation is to aid COVID-19 prevention efforts in Myanmar. A delivery ceremony for this donation was held on September 3, 2021 in Kunming, Yunnan in Myanmar. Myanmar's Minister of Health Dai Khai Win was present at the ceremony and thanked China for their friendship and help. After the ceremony, the supplies were to be distributed throughout the country from Yunnan Duolu Port.
Funding_Agencies: China Ministry of Foreign Affairs|China National Pharmaceutical Group Corporation (Sinopharm)

Title: Chinese Embassy donates anti-epidemic materials to the Foreign Ministry of Panama in April 2020
Description: On April 2, 2020, China provided anti-epidemic materials to the Foreign Ministry of Panama. The donation included 5 portable respirators, test kits, N95 or surgical masks, fans, thermal cameras, rapid virus detection equipment and other medical devices. The amount and monetary value of this donation are unknown.   A video handover ceremony took place for this donation. Chinese Ambassador Wei Qiang, Foreign Minister of Panama, and Deputy Foreign Minister of Panama attended the ceremony. During the ceremony, Panama’s Foreign Minister thanked the Chinese government for providing supplies during Panama’s shortage of medical supplies. The two sides also discussed international cooperation in epidemic prevention following the ceremony.

Title: Chinese Government provides grant for OB-GYN Building Refurbishment Project (Linked to Project ID#35064)
Description: On December 20, 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Cape Verde and the Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs signed an implementation agreement for the OB-GYN Building Refurbishment Project. _x000D_ _x000D_ China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of the financial commitment is unknown. The purpose of this project was refurbish the basement of the obstetrics and gynaecology (OB-GYN) building (妇产科楼地下室进行局部改造) in Agostinho Neto Hospital (HAN or Praia Central Hospital or 普拉亚中心医院). The Chinese Government also funded the initial construction of the OB-GYN building, which is captured in Project ID#35064. China Liaoning International Cooperation Group (辽宁省国际经济技术合作集团有限) was the contractor responsible for implementation. _x000D_ _x000D_ The expected duration of its construction contract with MOFCOM was seven months. The project passed the final MOFCOM inspection in November 2013 and the official handover ceremony took place on December 30, 2013.

Title: SEPCO I donates Covid-19 supplies to Kyaukphyu Township in Myanmar in June 2020
Description: On June 10, 2020, PowerChina SEPCO1 Electric Power Construction Co., Ltd. (SEPCO1) provided a donation of an unspecified amount and type of medical supplies to Myanmar Kyaukphyu Township. SEPCO 1 is an implementing agency of Kyaukphyu Power Plant Project in Myanmar (see #88703). The donation ceremony was held in Kyaukphyu township and was attended by representatives of Myanmar's government as well as SEPCO.
Funding_Agencies: PowerChina SEPCO1 Electric Power Construction Co., Ltd. (SEPCO1)

Title: Chinese Government donates 25 tons of anti-epidemic supplies to Venezuela in May 2021
Description: On May 17, 2021, the Chinese Government sent a shipment of 25 tons of medicines and supplies to Venezuela. The supplies included materials to repair respirators, injectors, drugs, and other equipment. The purpose of this donation is to support Venezuela’s COVID-19 response efforts. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation at the Simón Bolívar International Airport.

Title: Chinese Vice Premier sends educational and medical experts to 30 African Nations
Description: On November 16, 2007, Chinese Vice-Premier Wu Yi called on a group of 100 Africa-bound experts and volunteers to provide good service to their African hosts, the group consists of 58 agricultural and 16 malarial experts sent to 30 African nations. 26 of these volunteers were sent to work in education and medical services in Mauritius, Tunisia, and Eritrea. The status of the workers is uncertain.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 24th medical team to Bata General Hospital and Malabo Regional Hospital
Description: Since 1971, Guangzhou Health Department has been sending medical teams to Equatorial Guinea. In 2008, the Chinese Government dispatched the 24th Chinese medical team to Equatorial Guinea. The 23-member team was stationed at the Bata General Hospital in the city of Bata and Malabo Regional Hospital in the city of Malabo. It completed its terms of service between June 2008 and 2010.   The team met with the Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea on June 26, 2008, shortly after arriving in the country. Then, on July 3, 2010, President Obiang presented awards and honors to the members of the 24th Chinese medical team prior to their departure from Equatorial Guinea.

Title: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs provides second batch of medical supplies worth RMB $2.97 million to Shan region of Myanmar in September 2021 (Linked to Project #96166)
Description: On September 5, 2021, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs donated a second batch medical supplies worth RMB $2.97 million to the Shan region of Myanmar. The donation included surgical gloves, masks, hazmat suits, medicine, nucleic acid testing kits and oxygen generators, and the purpose of this donation was to aid Myanmar in COVID-19 prevention efforts. A donation ceremony was held on the same day in the city of Ruili in the Yunnan province of China. This is the second batch of medical supplies sent to Myanmar via China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the first batch was sent on August 27, 2021.

Title: Chinese Government pledges MGA 300 million MGA loan to Ministry of Public Health to support the university hospital system (2019) (Linked to Project ID#60031, #89056, #89057)
Description: A Malagasy Budget Document for 2019 finances lists three loans committed-to by the Chinese Government for 300 million MGA in each of 2019, 2020 (see linked ProjectID#89056), and 2021 (see linked ProjectID#89057) to the Government of Madagascar to support the university hospital system. Further project information is currently unknown, including project status and what specific university or universities were funded.  In 2018, the Chinese Government also provided a grant worth 446 million MGA for the same project (see linked ProjectID#60031).

Title: Chinese government donates RMB 40,000 to Bangladesh Red Crescent Society for humanitarian relief
Description: On January 5, 2021, the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Bangladesh reported that Ambassador Li Jiming handed over a donation of RMB 40,000 to the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS). The purpose of this donation was to provide humanitarian relief to host communities in Cox's Bazar, a town on the southeast coast of Bangladesh, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Mr. Md. Feroz Salah Uddin, Secretary-General of the BDRCS, was present at the handover ceremony. The specific allocation of the donation is unknown.

Title: China grants $125,000 USD in medical equipment to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Barbados (Linked to Project ID #71321)
Description: On May 17, 2019, The Chinese embassy to Barbados handed over $125,000 in medical equipment (qehconnect) to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in order to further improve the hospital's diagnosis and treatment abilities. The handover occurred during the third Chinese medical team's visit to the Queen Elizabeth hospital in Barbados, which is detailed in Project ID #71321.   Specific medical equipment from the grant includes: a vital signs monitor (Mindray VS-900 model), two blood pressure monitors (Omron Intellisense HEM-7130 model), another patient monitor (Mindray brand, likely an iPM series), two syringe pumps (unknown manufacturer), a thyroid function checker and a portable ultrasound device (qehconnect).

Title: Sichuan Provincial Government donated 10,000 medical masks to the Department of Lavalleja in May 2020
Description: On May 8, 2020, the handover ceremony took place for a donation of 10,000 medical surgical masks from the Chinese province of Sichuan to the Department of Lavalleja in Uruguay to support the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The handover took place in Minas, the capital of Lavalleja, and the donation arrived to Uruguay by way of the Consulate General in Chongqing.  The Government of Sichuan informed reporters on April 18, 2020 that the province had recently provided a donation to Lavalleja, indicating the donation was committed and sent around that time, but did not arrive until May 8, 2020 in Lavalleja.  Harvard's Mask Diplomacy dataset estimated the donation was worth USD 4,000.

Title: Chinese 11th Medical Team Conducts Free Consultations (Linked to #61334)
Description: In September 2016, the 11th Chinese medical team (project #61334) arrived in Swakopmund, Namibia to offer free medical consultations and traditional Chinese medicinal services. The team consisted of 4 doctors and nurses of Traditional Chinese Medicine from China`s Zhejiang Province. The value of the medical team's services is unknown. In August, the Chinese medical team conducted the free consultations, conducting services such as treating lower back and neck pain with acupuncture. The team treated about 600 patients monthly at the Chinese Acupuncture Department of Katutura State Hospital.

Title: China donates medical equipment to Masaka Hospital in Rwanda
Description: On May 5, 2013 the Chinese government donated 1,624,000 USD worth of laboratory kits, consultation machines, baby incubators, syringes, an ambulance, and other types of equipment to Masaka Hospital in Rwanda. The donation was made by Shu Zhan, Chinese Ambassador to Rwanda, on behalf of the Chinese government, and is intended to improve the quality of service at the hospital.

Title: China donates 2 AEDs to the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Barbados
Description: Ambassador to Barbados for China, Wang Ke, donated 2 Automated External Defibrillators (AED) to the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Barbados on January 17th, 2017. The new CEO of the foundation, Fiona Anthony, noted that the new AEDs would help improve first aid skills and training related to cardiovascular illnesses.

Title: International Center for Cultural Exchange of Chongqing donates masks to the Municipality of Arequipa
Description: On June 26, 2020, the Government of Peru thanked the International Center for Cultural Exchange of Chongqing, an important industrial city in central China, for their donation of 8,000 masks to the Provincial Municipality of Arequipa.  The donation was implemented by the Embassy of Peru in China, the Decentralized Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Arequipa (ODE Arequipa), the Peruvian Agency for International Cooperation (APCI) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Title: Chinese government grants breast cancer prevention equipment worth USD 294,005
Description: On February 18 and April 15, 2008, the Chinese Government signed an exchange of letters committing to donate breast cancer prevention equipment to several health institutions in Ecuador. According to "La Cooperación Bilateral Ecuador-China," the equipment was worth USD 294,005.01.   More specifically, one x-ray machine (equipo de Rayos X) that went to the Ambato Teaching Hospital in Tungurahua, one x-ray machine went to the Alfonso Oramas González Health Center in Guayas, and one mammogram machine to the Martha de Roldos Health Center in Guayas. The equipment arrived in Guayaquil January 10, 2009, and the official handover took place on February 13, 2009.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Malaysia donates 30,000 masks to the Malaysia-China Friendship Association
Description: On April 15, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Malaysia donated 30,000 masks to the Malaysia-China Friendship Association. The donation will go towards medical institutions and groups in need within the country. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides BWP 1.1 million grant for National Referral STD Treatment and Training Centre Construction Project
Description: During the farewell ceremony for the 11th Chinese Medical Team in 2008, Health Minister, Ms Lesego Motsumi highlighted that the Chinese government has provided a grant of approximately BWP 1.1 million to finance the construction of the National Referral STD Treatment and Training Centre in Gaborone._x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese Government provides a $80,000 USD grant for the Renovation Project of the Reception Hall of the Maldives Ministry of Health
Description: On October 12, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Maldives signed an agreement for the Renovation Project of the Reception Hall of the Maldives Ministry of Health. In the agreement, the Chinese Government agreed to donate $80,000 USD to renovate the front office area of the Ministry of Health to make it more customer-friendly and improve the quality of service provided.

Title: Chinese government donates anti-epidemic supplies to Yemen government in July 2020
Description: On July 15, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Yemen, Kang Yong, handed over a batch of anti-epidemic supplies donated by the Chinese Embassy to Yemen to help Yemen in the combat against Covid-19. The donation includes 25,000 regular masks, 600 protective clothing, and 600 protective goggles, in addition to a set of medical supplies for workers in the health sector. The donation was received by the Minister of Public Health and Population, Dr. Nasser Baoum. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government donates 300,000 Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccine doses worth $5.4 million in August 2021
Description: In 2021 and 2022, the Chinese Government donated approximately 3 million doses of Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sri Lanka. The Chinese Government delivered 600,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sri Lanka on March 31, 2021 (see project ID#95884).  Then, on May 25, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 500,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sri Lanka (see project ID#95887).  The Chinese Government delivered an additional 1 million donated Sinopharm COVID-19 vaccine doses to the Government of Sri Lanka on June 6, 2021 (see project ID#95913).  Then, on July 27, 2021, the Chinese Government delivered 1.6 million donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Government of Sri Lanka (see project ID#95046).  One month later, on August 28, 2021, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of China delivered 300,000 donated doses of Sinopharm Covid-19 vaccines to the Sri Lankan Armed Forces (see project ID#95918).  Then, in September 2021, the Chinese Government announced that it would donate 1 million Sinovac doses to the Government of Sri Lanka in September 2021 (see project ID#95923). However, it is unclear if this batch of vaccines was ever delivered.

Title: Donation of Anti-Malaria Medicine to Equatorial Guinea
Description: On June 19, 2009, and February 4, 2010, China and Equatorial Guinea exchanged notes on the donation of anti-malaria drugs worth 1 million RMB. The medicine was handed over in August 2010.

Title: Peking University builds Malawi Research and Teaching Base of Peking University School of Public Health
Description: On November 21, 2017, an unveiling ceremony was held for the Malawi Research and Teaching Base of Peking University School of Public Health. The establishment of this public health campus was co-financed by the Malawi Participatory Rural Development Organisation (PRDO) and by Peking University School of Public Health. The commitment date of the project is unclear.

Title: China donates medical equipment and anti-malaria drugs to Anti-Malarial Center
Description: On August 13, 2008, the National Public Health Laboratory opened its center for the prevention and treatment of malaria in Brazzaville. The opening of the center was linked to a Chinese donation consisting of medical equipment and pharmaceutical drugs estimated to be worth 300 million CFA francs that was received by the Minister of Health, Social Affairs and Family, Emilienne Raoul. The center's goal is to conduct in-depth analysis and research on malaria. The Chinese government sent four experts, equipment, pharmaceuticals and reagents to ensure the operation of the center. These Chinese experts worked at the center for 45 days to train the Congolese staff.

Title: Chinese Government donates 500 tents for Iraqi Refugees
Description: On March 22, 2003, the Chinese government decided to provide the Jordanian government with emergency aid materials for humanitarian purpose, according to sources with the Chinese Foreign Ministry.  On March 30, 2003, the first batch of humanitarian aid from the Chinese government for Iraqi refugees was shipped to Jordan, according to China's Ministry of Commerce. The aid includes 500 tents, each four meters long, three meters wide and 2.5 meters high. The first batch of 100 tents were transported by air to Jordan from Urumqi, capital of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. The remaining 400 tents were sent to Jordan in batches in early April. The Chinese Government handed over the 500 tents to the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organization on April 2, 2003 for distribution.

Title: China Donates 2m CNY of Medical Instruments and Medicine to Rwanda
Description: On August 28-30, 2006, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Chinese Communist Party, Wu Guanzheng , and Rwandan President Paul Kagame exchanged a letter according to which China will provide some 2 million CNY worth of medical instruments, general medicine, and anti-malaria medicine. The current status and start and end dates are unknown.

Title: Chinese government sends military medical team to Ecuador 2010-2011 (Linked to Project ID #85603, #85605, and #89533)
Description: From November 13, 2010 to April 1, 2011, a medical team of doctors from the People's Liberation Army was sent by the Chinese government to the Armed Forces General Hospital in Ecuador to improve the health of both the military and civilian populations, as well as strengthen relations between the armed forces of both countries. The Chinese government financed the salaries of the medical team and their international travel expenses.  The medical team consisted of two acupuncture specialists, one massage therapist, and one interpreter. The Directorate of Interinstitutional Cooperation of the Armed Forces of Ecuador (Dirección de Cooperación Interinstitucional del CC.FF.AA) also helped with project implementation.  The team's visit fell under the framework established by the Cooperation Agreement Between the Ministry of National Defense of China and the Ministry of Defense of Ecuador about the Sending of Chinese Medics to the General Hospital of the Armed Forces of Ecuador, signed November 13, 2009. Other medical teams that arrived under this framework can be found in projects #85603 and #85605.   The November 13, 2009 agreement is the third of its kind, with the other two agreements signed February 19, 2004, which lasted three years, and September 18, 2008, which was in effect September 2007 to April 2009. The November 2009 agreement, unlike its predecessors, is automatically self-renewing, unless one of the parties wishes to stop it.

Title: 160 million yuan in non-compensatory assistance for various sectors
Description: On 24 March 2010, during Afghan President Karzai's visit to Beijing, China announced that it would provide 160 million in Chinese Yuan in aid to Afghanistan. The aid will be used for infrastructure construction, medical, health, and education. Details on which specific project would benefit from the aid are yet to be found. _x000D_ _x000D_ No updates have been made on the status of the pledge. _x000D_ _x000D_ On the same date, China and Afghanistan signed 3 agreements; one of them is reported to be a loan agreement (See Project ID#38971)_x000D_ _x000D_

Title: China’s Liaoning Department of Health conducts week-long free clinic to perform eye surgeries at Republican Hospital in Sana'a (Linked to project ID#65254)
Description: On August 17, 2013, a team of 6 experts led by Professor Zhang Jinsong, a well-known ophthalmologist from Chinese Medical University in Liaoning, conducted a week-long free clinic at the Eye (Ophthalmology) Center at the Republic Hospital (هيئة المستشفى الجمهوري التعليمي في صنعاء) in the capital city of Sana’a. They successfully performed an intraocular lens implantation operations for 20 Yemen cataract patients. This clinic sought to provide free surgery for 80 cataract patients. The crystals, instruments, consumables and other items used in the free clinic are all donated free of charge by China Medical University.  The Eye (Ophthalmology) Center at the Republic Hospital (هيئة المستشفى الجمهوري التعليمي في صنعاء) in the capital city of Sana’a, aided by the Chinese government, was established on January 17, 2011 (captured in project ID#65254). The Chinese side provided the center with advanced ophthalmic medical equipment and organized local doctors to go to China for training.

Title: China donates medical supplies to anti-cancer center in Gabon
Description: On April  18, 2018, Chinese ambassador to Gabon Hu Changchun (胡长春) attended a handover ceremony for the donation of medical supplies to The Alice House (a part of Fondation Sylvia Bongo Ondimba), an anti-cancer center in Gabon. The project was completed with the delivery of the supplies at the handover ceremony on April 18, 2018.

Title: China Construction Bank donates ventilators to the Malaysian Red Crescent Society and Ministry of Health for COVID-19 containment efforts
Description: On April 3, 2020, China Construction Bank's Malaysian office donated 10 ventilators to the Malaysian Red Crescent Society and Ministry of Health. The ventilators will be sent to various public hospitals to be used in the fight against COVID-19. The donation is valued at RM1.2 million.

Title: Nanning Municipal Government donates medical supplies to Ivano-Frankivsk
Description: Sometime between March to April 2020, Nanning Municipal Government donated medical supplies to the city of Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine.

Title: Chinese medical team donates $3,000 USD to Sitagu Shwe Pyi Hein Eye hospital to support the China-Myanmar Brightness Journey 2018 (Linked to Project ID#67030)
Description: On September 20, 2018, a Chinese medical team from China's Kunming Medical University donated $3,000 USD to Sitagu Shwe Pyi Hein Hospital to support the China-Myanmar Brightness Journey 2018 program, which involved the provision of free cataract surgeries in Myanmar over two days jointly conducted by China's Kunming Medical University medical team and the local medical team at Sitagu Shwe Pyi Hein Eye Hospital; for the main program project entry, see linked project ID#67030.

Title: China Railway 14th Bureau Group provides grant of medical masks to Argentina's Ministry of Health in July 2020
Description: On July 6, 2020, a 113 kilogram batch of disposable medical masks – donated by China Railway 14th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. – were shipped from China to Argentina's Ministry of Health. The masks were procured from Quingdao Zhangchen International Trade Co., Ltd. Both the precise number of units donated and the donation's monetary value are unknown.    The materials were transported via Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 1063 as part of the "Air Bridge" ("Puente Aéreo") initiative. This flight also included supplies donated by China Railway Construction Corporation International, Ltd., captured via Project ID#93957.
Funding_Agencies: China Railway 14th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. (CRCC14)

Title: Construction of Heglig Hospital
Description: In Heglig, Sudan, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) built a hospital to provide free check-up and free medicine for the patients. Khaled Bellal is the president of the hospital. While the end date is unknown, the first date mentioning it as complete was on July 13, 2007. The total funding of this hospital is unknown._x000D_ _x000D_ It is possible the hospital was damaged in fighting in Heglig in 2012. The current status, amount, commitment date, and start and end dates are unknown.

Title: China provides Water Source Analysis and Lab Practice Training Course in Fiji
Description: Based on the news release from the ECCO of the Embassy of China in Fiji, On November 5, 2018, the Fiji Water Source Analysis and Laboratory Practice Overseas Training Course was held in Suva and attended by nearly 60 people. It is the first oversea training course in Fiji sponsored by China. On November 16, 2018, the training course ended and the certificates were provided to the participant. This project is provided under the framework of China’s 2018 – China Aid training program.  Ministry of Commerce of China is the sponsor, and Power China Zhongnan Engi­neering Corporation Limited is the implementer. Personnel from Water Authority of Fiji (WAF), Ministry of Infra­structure and Transport (MoIT), Ministry of Health (MOH) as well as the Mineral Resources Depart­ment (MRD) will be part of this training. This 2-week training focuses on improvements in the analysis of water sources as well as laboratory practices in Fiji. It is expected to im­prove delivery of safe and qual­ity drinking water services for all Fijians.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Nigeria donates 11 million Naira to remodel psychiatric ward of Zauro General Hospital
Description: On November 20, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria donated 11 million Naira to the Kebbi State Government. The purpose of the donation was to remodel the psychiatric ward of the general hospital in Zauro, Kebbi State.

Title: Chinese Government dispatches 21st medical team to Niamey General Referral Hospital
Description: In 2019, the Chinese Government dispatched the 21st Chinese medical team to Niger. The 21st medical team consisted of 37 members working at Niamey General Referral Hospital. The team was organized and selected by the Health Commission of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.  People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region sent one of its doctors on the medical team. Nanxishan Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region sent two of its doctor on the medical team.The 21st medical team set off for Niger on March 15, 2019 for a 558-day long mission (for a planned end date of September 23, 2020). During the tour, the 21st medical team visited Chinese enterprises working on the Third Bridge Construction Project (see project ID#58039), provided consultations for 512 people, including 127 Chinese employees and 385 local employees, and donated 550 boxes of 27 varieties of medicine to the Chinese enterprises implementing the project. Additionally, during their mission, the COVID-19 pandemic emerged; the medical team provided advice and assistance to the Government of Niger in response. The team returned to China on February 13, 2021.  The Chinese Government has sent medical teams to Niger since 1976.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates paintings by Chinese artists to Belarusian healthcare institutions in 2019
Description: On August 6, 2019, the Embassy of China in Belarus donated five paintings by Chinese artists to hospitals in Minsk Oblast, Belarus. According to a media report released by BelTA Daily News, the paintings were donated to make room for Belarusian paintings at the Embassy of China to represent cooperation among both nations.   Two paintings will be in the regional clinical hospital, two more will go to the Belarusian Children's Hospice. The fifth painting will be placed in the Minsk Regional Children's Clinical Hospital. The event was attended by the Ambassador of Belarus to China Kirill Rudy.

Title: China granted $6.5 million for the construction of a psychiatric hospital in St. Lucia (Linked to #40059, #54920, #54921, and #54922)
Description: On December 19, 2003, the government of China granted EC$6.5 million to St. Lucia for the construction of a 104-bed psychiatric hospital in Le Perle. The construction was expected to begin in November 2005, but according to the Chinese Embassy source, actually began on April 3, 2006. The total cost of construction is EC$27 million, according to the WHO source. According to the 2005 press statement from the government of St. Lucia, the Chinese state-owned Anhui Foreign Economic Construction Group signed the construction contract in September 2005, following a presentation of the project design to health officials in August 2005._x000D_ _x000D_ According to a 2003 press statement by the government of Saint Lucia, the fund was signed through an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement. In April 2007, the government of St. Lucia formally recognized Taiwan. Following the severing of ties with the government of the People's Republic of China in favor of Taiwan, AFECC halted construction of the psychiatric hospital. The Chinese funding for this project has since been cancelled._x000D_ _x000D_ Linked to #40059 (China donates $4.8 million for psychiatric hospital), #54920 (China signed a $3.65 million Agreement on Economic and Technical Cooperation), #54921(China granted $3.41 million for the implementation of the Psychiatric Hospital), and #54922 (China granted $240,000 for general goods).

Title: China Granted 10,000 Kina to a Sub-Health Center
Description: On July 18, 2003, the Chinese Embassy granted 10,000 Kina in cash to a sub-health center in the Baiyer River Lumusa electorate in the Western Highlands Province._x000D_ _x000D_ A later media article listed the amount as around K30,000. The official amount is recorded for this project.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD 78,750 for health support via United Nations Population Fund in Gambia in April 2021
Description: In April 2021, Chinese government donates USD 78,750 to provide health assistance to Sao Tome and Principe and Gambia in West and Central Africa Region for COVID-19 pandemic response.

Title: Chinese Embassy and Chinese companies donate $6,000 USD for disaster relief in Myanmar after Cyclone Nargis
Description: On 2 May 2008, Cycone Nargis hit Myanmar leaving tens of thousands of people dead, missing, or homeless. In response, on 10 May 2008, the Chinese Economic Attaché Office, jointly with a number of Chinese firms active in Myanmar, donated $6,000 USD (1.35 million kyat) for disaster relief efforts. The firms included Anhui Foreign Economic, China National Aero-Technology, Chinese Building Materials Industrial Corporation (CBMIC), China National Heavy Machinery Co, China Chengda Engineering and other companies.
Funding_Agencies: China Building Material Industrial Corporation for Foreign Economic-Technical Corporation (CBMIC)|China Chengda Engineering Co. Ltd|China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation (CATIC)|China National Heavy Machinery Corporation (CHMC)|Chines
Funding_Agencies_Type: State-owned Company|State-owned Company|State-owned Company|State-owned Company|Government Agency

Title: Chinese Government Grants Two Scholarships to Fijian Students to Study in China
Description: In 2002, 10 students from Fiji went and studied in China, including two students with scholarships from the Chinese Government. Since 1984, the Chinese government provides scholarships to Fijian students in every year._x000D_ _x000D_ The value of the two scholarships from the Chinese Government are unknown.

Title: China provides training on Ethiopian Railway operation
Description: The 752-km Ethiopia-Djibouti rail line (captured in #30171) is the first modern railway in Ethiopia and Djibouti. To cope with the shortage of railway personnel of the two nations, a massive training program is underway. In Ethiopia, which hosts the majority of the railway, about 2,000 local stewards, technicians, drivers and other personnel are receiving training from China Railway Erju Co. Ltd., a major builder and operator of the railway. Apart from school-style classes and trips to China, they are following a team of 1,000 Chinese railway workers, who have been commissioned to run the railway.  It is unclear when the trainings started, although MOFCOM reported a 2018 Seminar on Railway Operation Management in Ethiopia that was held from July 9th to August 7th 2018.

Title: Chinese Government provides grant for Kétou and Djougou Primary School Construction Project
Description: During the November 2006 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, the Chinese Government agreed to provide grant funding to the Government of Benin to support the construction of two primary schools in the rural areas of Kétou and Djougou.  China’s Ministry of Commerce was the funding source._x000D_ _x000D_ Guizhou Provincial Architectural Design Institute, Ningbo Civil Architectural Design Co., Ltd., China Railway Fifth Bureau Overseas Company, and Ningbo Construction Group Co., Ltd. Overseas Company were the contractors responsible for the design and construction of the schools.  China Youfa International Engineering Design Consulting Company was the contractor responsible for project supervision._x000D_ _x000D_ A groundbreaking ceremony for the Kétou School was held at the end of July 2008.  A commissioning ceremony was held for the Djougou School on 19 January, 2009.  The Kétou School was completed in March 2009, according to China’s Ministry of Commerce.

Title: Chinese Government sponsors Chinese language training course for 48 Government of Botswana officials
Description: In July 2015, forty-eight government officials from the Botswana Police Service, Ministry of Trade and Industry, and Ministry of Labor and Home Affairs went to the inaugural Mandarin Chinese language training course in Gaborone. The class was sponsored by the Confucius Institute at the University of Botswana and the Chinese embassy. The class looks to reduce cultural and language barriers between Botswana and Chinese officials. The project is complete.

Title: China's sports technical assistance program provides training for Bolivian athletes in December 2021
Description: In December 2021, the Bolivian national ski team arrived in Heilongjiang Province to attend a training program at the Yabuli Sports Training Base, China's largest ski resort. The training was provided under China's sport technical assistance program by China Sports International Economic and Technical Cooperation Co., Ltd.  The Bolivian national ski team, composed of eight athletes and coaches, underwent a 60-day full-range technical instruction and training. The training included training with specialist professionals, camps, workshops and provided tickets, lodging, food and training equipment. Two of the athletes went on to participate in the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic Games.

Title: Hanban provides grant for the establishment of Confucius Institute at Mongolian State University of Education
Description: On September 1, 2015, a Confucius Institute was founded at the Mongolian State University of Education (Монгол Улсын Боловсролын Их Сургууль), in collaboration with Northeast Normal University of China.

Title: Chinese Government donates audio-visual equipment and more than 1,000 books to DRC’s National Cultural Center
Description: On May 24, 2011, the Chinese Embassy granted audio-visual equipment and more than 1,000 books to the National Cultural Center in Democratic Republic of Congo. This donation was intended to help the Congolese National Cultural Center promote Chinese culture. The value of the donation and the exact equipment donated is unknown. This project is completed.

Title: China Communications Construction Company awards 35 students a scholarship to study in Beijing in 2017 (Linked to Umbrella Project #52535)
Description: In 2015, Chinese president Xi Jinping pledged to grant 1,000 new university scholarships for Kenyan students to study at Chinese universities over the following three years (umbrella project #52535). The first batch of students left for China in 2016. China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) helped follow through with this pledge by implementing a railway studies scholarship program which aims sponsor a total of 100 Kenyan students. Beijing Jiaotong University hosted the students. The value of each scholarship is unknown.  The first batch of 25 students left for China in 2016 (#59732). At the end of February 2017, 35 Kenyan students under the second batch left for China.

Title: Chinese Government provides fifth batch of humanitarian aid worth 40 million RMB to Sudan (Linked to Umbrella #71733)
Description: On 30 April and 3 May 2007, Chinese and Sudanese government officials signed an exchange of letters in which China committed to donating a batch of humanitarian aid materials to Sudan in light of the on-going war in Darfur (see umbrella project #71733). It was divided into six different batches. The fifth batch worth 40 million RMB included vehicles, ambulances, medical instruments, and mobile houses. It shipped out of Tianjin on 24 August 2007. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Financial Tracking Service captures this donation in flow ID #48117.

Title: China donates 5 million RMB for Kazakhstan training of state personnel
Description: In March 2006, China signed an agreement to finance 5 million RMB for projects funding training for state personnel in Kazakstan. The agreement was signed by the chairman of the State Service Agency, Zautbek Turisbekov, and the Chinese Ambassador to the RK Zhang Siyun.

Title: China trains Ethiopian martial arts and acrobats students
Description: On June 12, 2015, a ceremony was held to send off Ethiopian martial arts and acrobatics students to China. According to the Chinese Embassy, the Political Counselor, the president of the Ethiopian Martial Arts Association, Adu, the Secretary-General Salihu, the Secretary-General of the Ethiopian Gymnastics Association, Solomon, and other Ethiopian sports officials, the embassy diplomats and the parents of the students attended the ceremony. It is unclear how many students were sent to China for training.

Title: CNPC AktobeMunaiGas provides $63,700 USD for newspaper and magazine subscriptions for World War II veterans (Linked to Project ID#73474)
Description: On May 9, 2003, Victory Day, CNPC AktobeMunaiGas (CNPC AMG), a Kazakhstan-based subsidiary of China National Petroleum Corporation, set aside $63,700 USD to subscribe Kazakhstani veterans of World War II to newspapers and magazines. CNPC AMG was still spending that amount every year as of 2017. This project captures CNPC's purchase of subscriptions in 2011._x000D_ _x000D_ Linked project ID#73474 is the umbrella project for the newspaper and magazines subscriptions. Below is a list of projects that capture the money set aside for the subscriptions for every year from 2003 to 2017._x000D_ _x000D_ - 2003: Project ID#73487_x000D_ - 2004: Project ID#73488_x000D_ - 2005: Project ID#73489_x000D_ - 2006: Project ID#73490_x000D_ - 2007: Project ID#73491_x000D_ - 2008: Project ID#73492_x000D_ - 2009: Project ID#73493_x000D_ - 2010: Project ID#73494_x000D_ - 2011: Project ID#73495_x000D_ - 2012: Project ID#73496_x000D_ - 2013: Project ID#73497_x000D_ - 2014: Project ID#73498_x000D_ - 2015: Project ID#73499_x000D_ - 2016: Project ID#73500_x000D_ - 2017: Project ID#73501

Title: Chinese Embassy donates 10 million MNT to the Mongolia-China Friendship High School (linked to #73330)
Description: On December 28, 2015, according to China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Development, Chinese Embassy donated 200,000 RMB (captured in linked ProjectID#73330) and 10 million MNT to the Mongolia-China Friendship High School.  At the same time, the Mongolian-Chinese Language Culture and Education Foundation donated 8 million MNT to the Mongolian-Chinese Friendship High School (described in #70300).

Title: Chinese Embassy donates musical instruments worth USD 18,978.65 to the Ilopango city band in El Salvador
Description: On July 31, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to El Salvador attended a ceremony for the donation of musical instruments to Ilopango, El Salvador to create the city's first municipal peace band. According to a press release from the Ilopango Mayor's Office, the instruments were worth USD 18,978.65 and included 18 trumpets, 7 alto trombones, 6 Bb marching tubas, 4 sets of 5 bass drums with charger, 6 multitenor percussion, 5 French horns with 5 marching French horns, and 5 snare drums.   This project is part of the embassy's "Chinese Culture Tour" throughout El Salvador.

Title: Chinese Government trains 40 Laotian students in railway teaching skills as part of the Aid to Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College (Linked to Project ID#63790)
Description: On September 4, 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Laos signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for a feasibility study for the Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College Project. The project sought to construct a full-time vocational and technical college in Vientiane to train railway workers for Laos. Specifically, the project was intended to complement the Chinese Government-financed China-Laos Railway Project, as captured by project ID#85304 and #33726, a key project of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), by providing a reserve workforce for the railway's operation  Then, on April 30, 2019, China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA) approved the Aid to Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College. The Aid to Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College took two separate forms: the aforementioned Chinese Government-provided grant financing for the construction of the Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College (as captured by linked project ID#63790) and educational capacity building and educational technology cooperation (Chinese: 教育能力建设及教育技术合作) by Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical College, as captured by this project.  The educational capacity building and educational technology cooperation sought to provide vocational training in railway skills to 40 future Laotian teachers for the Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College. Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical College would train 40 Laotian students the Chinese language, in railway majors such as railway locomotives, railway vehicles, and railway engineering, and in professional and technical teaching skills to allow them to be professional railway teachers at Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College.   After this two-year training period, Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical College would provide an additional five-year technical cooperation program for Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College by sending 16 experts to Laos in the first three years and eight experts in the last two years to assist the development and educational capacity of the college.   In May 2020, CIDCA assigned the Yunnan Province to organize the implementation of the project (as well as the construction of the Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College). It used the Chinese vocational education model as a framework in its trainings.  In 2020, the 40 Laotian students passed an exam organized by Laos' Ministry of Education and Sports to be trained by Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical Collage and eventually become future teachers at the Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College. However, due to the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Laotian students were unable to enter Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical Collage as scheduled for their two-year learning term (had it not been for the pandemic, the students would have completed their program in 2022).  The first class - an online Chinese language class via the DingTalk virtual teaching platform from teachers at Yunnan Normal University - was on November 29, 2021, marking the official launch of the educational capacity building and educational technology cooperation part of China's Aid to Laos Railway Vocational and Technical College. In December 2021, the 40 students were expected to begin physically studying in Kunming as soon as the end of 2021.  On March 22, 2022, the first batch of 32 Lao students from Lao Railway Vocational and Technical College arrived at Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical College in China to begin the two-years study in China. On the day they arrived at Kunming Railway Vocational and Technical College, the students checked into the  international student dormitory. After the 7-day centralized health monitoring, the college will organize normal education and teaching work according to the established teaching plan.

Title: China donates 611 Laptops and Sports Equipment worth Rs 660,850 to the Mauritius Ministry of Youth and Sports
Description: According to the Treasury of the Mauritius government, on March 26, 2019, China donated 611 Laptops and Sports Equipment to the Mauritius Ministry of Youth and Sports. This donation worths Rs 660,850 has been received.

Title: China Development Bank provides $10.6 million export seller’s credit for acquisition of e-education equipment from Huawei (Linked to Project ID#53952)
Description: In 2011, China Development Bank provided a $10,608,000 export seller's credit loan to Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., in turn, used the proceeds from the seller's credit facility to issue a $10,608,000 supplier credit (loan) to Uzbektelecom JSC  — a state-owned telecommunications company in Uzbekistan — for the purchase of e-education equipment. The loan carried the following terms: a 2.2% interest rate and a 2.5 year maturity.   On December 24th, 2012, China Development Bank provided a $10,608,000 export seller's credit loan to Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. Huawei Technologies Co. The proceeds of the loan were to be used by Uzbektelecom JSC to finance a $12.4 million contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.  and thereby link a network of 200 higher education and vocational education institutions through the creation of a fiber optic network. The e-Education Project commenced in September 2011 and by the end of 2011, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. had installed 132.9 km of fiber optic cable, connecting 80 institutions. This project was ultimately completed, but its precise completion date is unknown.

Title: Chinese Embassy grants the Chinese Ambassador Scholarship to students at the Confucius Institute for a total amount of $6,000 USD
Description: On November 16th, 2018 the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana had presented award-winning students from the Confucius Institute at UCC and its teaching points with scholarship awards to promote further teaching of the Chinese language and culture. The awards were presented at the Chinese Ambassador Scholarship Award Ceremony and the 2018 End of Year Celebration of the Confucius Institute at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), where 1000 people were present including Prof Hu Liangcai, the Chinese Director of the Confucius Institute at UCC, Prof Ishmael Mensah, the Ghanaian Director of the Confucius Institute at UCC, alongside staff and students. According to a 2018 publication of the Confucius Institute at UCC, the scholarship award was made for a total of $6,000 USD given towards deserving students.

Title: Chinese government grants funding for construction of education center in Quito
Description: On May 25 and June 21, 2004, the Chinese ambassador to Ecuador exchanged letters with Ecuador's Foreign Minister on the construction of an education center in Quito. This project appears to be a grant. The center covers a total area of 70,000 square meters and a total building area of 18,600 square meters, including an administrative teaching area, an indoor  sports center, and a stadium. The center will be able to accommodate 3,000 students.

Title: China sends Namibian Students and Teachers to China for Agricultural Training
Description: On November 18th, 2005, Namibia and China signed a cooperation agreement on economy and trade, mainly focusing on the vocational training of young Namibians in their areas of technology. The agreement also focuses on strengthening cooperation in the areas of mining exploration, agriculture, especially irrigation, and the processing of agricultural products such as grapes, and human resource training. It was concluded at the National Planning Commission. At the end of the meeting, the two parties reached a consensus to cooperate and form joint ventures in five areas of economic interest. In the sector of education, the two parties agreed for Namibia to send students and teachers to China for training in agricultural skills on a five-year program. It is unclear if students have been trained.

Title: China pledges training and training centre to Portuguese-speaking countries
Description: In November 2010, Chinese Premier Wen Jiaobao announced during the Forum for Economic and Trade Cooperation that China would help train 1,500 officials and technical personnel in Portuguese speaking countries (Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Portugal and Timor-Leste), give full support to the establishment of a training center affiliated to the Forum in Macao SAR. The status of the project is uncertain.

Title: China donates 120,000 M and crutches to Ithuseng Vocational Rehabilitation Center in Lesotho
Description: On 14 October 2016, the Chinese Ambassador officially donated 120,000 M and crutches to Ithuseng Vocational Rehabilitation Center in Lesotho. The grant will help renovate the facilities and replace old equipment and machinery. _x000D_ _x000D_ The center was established in 1992 with help from the International Labor Organzation (ILO) to teach disabled Basotho with vocational skills such as carpentry, sewing, and metal works.

Title: Chinese Embassy funds Countryside Vehicle Project for delivering library materials to rural regions of Armenia
Description: On December 17, 2018 the Countryside Vehicle Project held its opening ceremony. The project was jointly funded by the Chinese Embassy in Armenia and the Armenians Special Vehicle Manufacturing Plant. The Yahirak State Library in Armenia will deliver library books and audiovisual products to the countryside where libraries are not available. The library will also be in charge of the replenishment and daily maintenance of the library materials.

Title: China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Development Foundation commits 'Future Star' scholarship to Mongolian students in fall 2019 (Linked to Project ID#86933)
Description: In October 2019, on some date following the 4th of the month, the China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Foundation awarded scholarships to Mongolian students. The "Dream Star" and "Future Star" scholarship recipients were presented with 3,000 yuan (approximately $437.32) each. It is unclear how many of the students were "Future Star" scholarship recipients. However, this project captures the money awarded under the "Future Star" program.  The scholarship is organized by the China-Mongolia CESDF and co-organized by the Bank of China Representative Office in Ulaanbaatar and the Confucius Institute of Mongolia State University.  The "Future Star" (“Ирээдүйн од”) scholarship program was organized and funded by the China-Mongolia Culture and Education Foundation in 2014. After the China-Mongolia Culture and Education Foundation merged with the China-Mongolia Social Development Fund in August 2017, the "Future Star" scholarship program was run by the China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Foundation. The "Future Star" scholarship program is co-organized by Bank of China Representative Office in Ulaanbaatar and the Confucius Institute at the National University of Mongolia. Under the program, a up to 30 Mongolian students that score above a certain threshold on the scholarship examination are selected to receive 3,000 yuan each. See project ID #86933 for a full list of scholarships to Mongolian students from the China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Foundation.
Funding_Agencies: China-Mongolia Cultural Education and Social Development Foundation

Title: Chinese government provides scholarships through Sino-Cuban Education Exchange Project
Description: In April 2001, Cuba and China signed the "Agreement on Educational Exchange between the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China and the Ministries of Education and Higher Education of the Republic of Cuba".  According to this agreement, colloquially referred to as the "Sino-Cuban Education Exchange Project," Cuba can send 150 students to China each year on a full scholarship_x000D_ _x000D_ On October 24, 2019, China and Cuba renewed the education exchange agreement until 2022

Title: Chinese Embassy donates teaching supplies to the Sino-Angolan Friendship Primary School (April 2018)
Description: On April 24, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Angola, Cui Aimin provided the Sino-Angolan Friendship Primary School with a donation of teaching supplies, including computers, televisions, mosquito lamps, footballs, basketballs, notebooks and other items for teachers and students. Among the attendees at the event was local Governor Muandumba. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: China provides theater operation and management seminar to 15 African students in 2019
Description: On May 6, 2019, 15 African students completed a Chinese-funded two-week theater management seminar. The Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Management led this seminar. A total of fifteen participants were involved in the two weeks training (April 23-May 4) at the Central Cadre College of Culture and Tourism Administration in Lin-Xiaonan, Daxing District of Beijing. Each country sent three representatives each at the seminar sponsored by the Government of the People's Republic of China. These students came from the countries of Liberia, South Africa, Tanzania, Gambia, and Sierra Leone. The three Liberians were James Enders (Liberia Crusaders for Peace), Tom Fritz Kamara (Ministry of Information, Cultural Affairs, and Tourism), and Abdul Karim Sheriff l (Liberia Movie Union). They completed an intensive training program in theater management and tourism administration in the Peoples Republic of China. They were part of a selected group of artistic and tourism industry practitioners drawn from five African countries at the 2019 Seminar on Theater Management.

Title: China provides 32 scholarships to students in Bangladesh for the 2020-2021 school year
Description: On November 26, 2019, the Government of China committed to continuing to provide 162 scholarships for students in Bangladesh to study in China. As 130 students are already studying in China, 32 scholarships will be awarded to new candidates. This is part of an effort by China to further bilateral relations and cultural exchange with Bangladesh.

Title: Chinese Government provides $7 million grant for E-Education Project
Description: In 2014, the Government of North Macedonia and the Chinese Government signed an agreement for an E-Education Project.
