As of November 2015, Hanban had sent a total of 8 teachers to teach at the Confucius Institute. The Confucius Institute has two classrooms, a library preview room, and three offices. It was established in partnership with Guizhou University of Finance and Economics.

Title: Chinese Government donates 50 schools to the Government of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa
Description: In 2021, the Government of China donated 50 schools to the Government of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The government has also helped rehabilitated 895 schools in the region. This is a response to terrorist attacks in the region that destroyed many schools.   Most of the schools will include six rooms for primary students and 10 for middle schoolers.

Title: Chinese Embassy donates teaching materials to Pilar Buepoyo School in Equatorial Guinea
Description: On April 21, 2011, Chinese Ambassador to Equatorial Guinea Wang Shixiong gave a batch of teaching materials including school bags, textbooks and brushes to the Centro Pilar Buepoyo School in Malabo. The ceremony was attended by the Director-General of Primary Education, Juan Asumu Engonga. The donation consisted of backpacks, notebooks, painting material, pencils, and other study materials.

Title: China to provide training for Caribbean students (linked to project ID #39934)
Description: On June 2, 2013, Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged to send 100 medical staff to the Caribbean region, train 100 part-time post-graduate students, and provide scholarships for 1,000 students from the Caribbean region (#39934). The pledge was made at a luncheon with leaders of Trinidad & Tobago, Suriname, Guyana, Dominica, Barbados, Jamaica, the Bahamas, Grenada, and Antigua & Barbuda._x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese Government provides 15 scholarships to Moroccan Students
Description: On 22 June 2010, China and Morocco signed a three-year agreement to reinforce cultural bilateral cooperation. Under this agreement, China agreed to grant 15 scholarships to Moroccan students. In return, Morocco agreed to grant 10 scholarships to Chinese student who wished to study in Morocco. _x000D_ _x000D_ “我国与突尼斯、摩洛哥分别签署文化合作执行计划” clarifies that this agreement is an “implementation plan” of the formal cultural cooperation agreement which was signed by the two governments in February 1982. The agreement was signed following a meeting between Morocco's Culture Minister Bensalem Himmich and his Chinese counterpart Cai Wu.

Title: 13 Basotho students win 2013/14 Chinese Government Scholarship
Description: On 15 August 2013, the Chinese Ambassador held a send-off reception for the 13 Basotho winners of the 2013/14 Chinese Government Scholarship (2013/14年度中国政府奖学金). This is a fully-paid scholarship sending Basotho students to 13 different universities to partake in bachelors and masters programs related to journalism, economics, geochemistry, management, international trade, international politics, communication, and engineering. The value of each scholarship is unknown.

Title: China funds scholarships for 30 Congolese students
Description: In an official visit to the Congo, Wen Jiabao claimed that China funds scholarships to allow over 30 Congolese students to study abroad in China per year. The commitment year or financial amount for this project is yet unknown.

Title: China constructs a playground for a public school in Rwanda
Description: On February 27, 2014, China handed over the China-aided playground to the Gysoze Comprehensive School in Rwanda. China provided a grant for the project, and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation was responsible for the construction of the playground. During the handover ceremony, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation also donated school supplies to the school. The monetary value of the construction and donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Embassy awards CFA 6 million scholarship to Cote d’Ivoire high school students
Description: On November 7, 2019, Ambassador Van Li and Minister of National Education Kamala of Côte d’Ivoire attended the “Chinese Ambassador Scholarship” award ceremony at Abidjan Yobugun Girls’ High School. Scholarships worth 6 million CFA were awarded to girls from the Abidjan Yobugun Girls’ High School and Ubgun Girls’ High School.  The “China-Cote d’Ivoire Friendship Classroom” was also inaugurated at the ceremony.

Title: Chinese Government donates A/V equipment to Syria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Description: On January 25, 2011, the Chinese Government donated audio-visual (A/V) equipment to the Diplomatic Academy, which is part of Syria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the city of Damascus. This donation of voice and speech equipment was designed to improve the quality of classroom facilities at the Diplomatic Academy.

Title: Chinese government provides economic administration training for Barbadian official
Description: In 2012, the deputy chairman of Barbados' Productivity Council participated in the Seminar on Economic Administration for Latin America, Caribbean and South Pacific Countries, facilitated by the Chinese Embassy in Barbados. The funding organization is not specified. The seminar took place in Beijing.

Title: China Merchants Group provide 'Excellence Scholarships' worth USD $200,000 to fifty Togolese students from the University of Lomé
Description: On February 18, 2019, the China Merchant's Group, through the Lomé Container Terminal (LCT), awarded 50 students at the University of Lomé (UL) scholarships. In total, the scholarships has a value of US $200,000, or approximately XOF $117,000,000. The certification ceremony was chaired by the First Vice-President of UL, Pr. Komlan Batawila. The Second Vice-President, Ms. Kafui Kpégba, also attended, along with the Director General of the LCT and Deans and Directors of UL establishments and central services.   The 50 students were selected from the fourteen establishments of UL to receive financial assistance for two years, including 4 students from the Computer and Computing Center (CIC); 4 students from the National School of Engineers (ENSI); 4 from the Higher School of Agronomy (ESA); 3 students from the Higher School of Administrative Assistants (ESAAd); 4 students from the Higher School of Biological and Food Techniques (ESTBA); 3 students from the Faculty of Economics of Management (FASEG); 3 students from the Faculty of Law (FDD); 5 students from the Faculty of Sciences (FDS); 3 students from the Faculty of Letters, Languages ​​and Arts (FLLA); 3 students from the Faculty of Human and Social Sciences (FSHS); 5 students from the Faculty of Health Sciences (FSS); 3 students from the National Institute of Educational Sciences (INSE); 3 students from the Institute of Information, Communication and Arts Sciences (ISICA); and 3 students from the University Institute of Management Technologies (IUT-GESTION). These scholarships were distributed in monthly installments and were intended to encourage the academic excellence of students over a period of ten years. The recipients were enrolled in a Chinese language course at the Confucius Institute of UL.

Title: The Chinese Embassy in Mexico Grants 70 Chinese Government Scholarships to Mexican Students for 2016-2017 Academic Year
Description: On 17 August 2016, the Chinese Embassy in Mexico held a ceremony to award Chinese government scholarships for the 2016-2017 academic year. Ambassador Qiu Xiaoqi attended and delivered a speech. More than 70 scholarship winners and parents participated. It is unclear which Chinese Government Institution provided the scholarships.

Title: Chinese embassy donates laptops, balls, and school bags to Matapata Middle School
Description: On November 18, 2016, the Chinese embassy donates laptops, footballs, and school bags to Matapata Middle School in Malawi according to the Chinese Embassy in Malawi and MOFCOM. The value of this donation is unknown.

Title: China Hydropower Construction Group donates primary school to Malanje government in Angola (linked to #68377)
Description: On February 14, 2014, China Hydropower Construction Group handed over the "Zhongan Friendship Primary School" (in Chinese "中安友谊小学") to the Malanje government in Angola. The school covers an area of 4,000 square meters and a building area of ​​1,103 square meters. It includes 6 classrooms, 3 offices, 1 secretary room and 1 security room. It can accommodate 540 primary school students to study in divided periods._x000D_ _x000D_ The exact commitment date and start date of this project are unclear, as is the cost of the overall project._x000D_ _x000D_ This project is linked to project #68377, a China Hydropower Construction Group donation of 30,000 sets of clothes for school children at this school.

Title: The Outreach Bureau of the Chinese Ministry of Culture Donates Books and Audiovisual Material to the Library of the Federal College of Micronesia (linked to project #42053)
Description: On 12 January 2007, Ambassador Liu Fei of the People's Republic of China in The Federated States of Micronesia donated over 400 books and 60 DVDs on the history, culture, economy, and social development of China to the Library of the Federal College of Micronesia on behalf of the Outreach Bureau of the Chinese Ministry of Culture. These books and CDs are expected to help students to understand Chinese culture and encourage them to study Chinese. _x000D_ _x000D_ The project is financed by a cultural exchange program (see project #42053). . _x000D_ _x000D_
Funding_Agencies: China Ministry of Culture|Unspecified Chinese Government Institution

Title: Chinese Government funds geological survey to support Phase 2 of Tonga High School Reconstruction Project (Linked to Project ID#39243, #68391)
Description: On October 1, 2000, Tonga’s leading secondary school — Tonga High School — was destroyed in a fire. The school’s 1,060 students and teachers continued classes in the ruins of the school, and in tents before moving in October 2001 to a temporary school built at Old Vaiola, thanks to a $1.2 million grant from the New Zealand, Australian and French governments.   In 2002, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 33 million grant to the Government of Tonga for Phase 1 of the Tonga High School Reconstruction Project (captured via Project ID#39243). The purpose of the project was to reconstruct the Tonga High School complex in the city of Nukuʻalofa. The project involved the construction of six buildings (including one three-story block and five two story blocks), a schoolyard, roads, a fire reservoir (including an underground conservation pool), and water and power supply utilities. Three of the buildings were designed to house 54 classrooms. The project also involved the construction of a separate administration office and reading room, as well as two other blocks for special classrooms for science laboratory and industrial arts. The total floor space of the new school was 7,300 square meters.   Nanjing Architectural Design Institute was responsible for designing the school, while China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation was responsible for the construction of the school. A Chinese team provided a geological survey of the site to ensure favorable conditions for construction. Then, on October 9, 2003, a groundbreaking ceremony took place. Somewhere between 86 and 110 Chinese workers were involved in the construction process. The school was completed and handed over in April 6, 2005. Tonga High School students moved into their permanent facility on July 2, 2005.   Then, on February 6, 2006, the Chinese Government donated $590,000 worth of furniture and equipment to Tonga High School, including 1710 sets of tables & chairs for students, 34 sets of office furniture, 142 sets of bookshelves, and 75 sets of teacher’s tables and experiment tables (as captured via Project ID#39228). China’s Ambassador to Tonga Hu Yeshun and the Education Minister of Tonga Tevita Palefau officiated at the handover ceremony. The Chinese Government also dispatched a Chinese language teacher to Tonga High School from 2003-2005 (as captured via Project ID#39239).  Shortly after Phase 1 was completed, discussions were underway about a possible second phase for the construction of an indoor gymnasium, an outdoor rugby field, four outdoor netball courts, an aquatics center, a lawn bowling field, a tennis court, a hall for the performing arts, and accommodations for teachers (with a total area of 9,180 square meters). In April 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tonga signed an agreement regarding Phase 2 of the Tonga High School Reconstruction Project. A team from Hunan Provincial Institute of Architectural Design conducted an initial set of geological surveys and completed them on or around September 16, 2006 (as recorded in Project ID#62983). They confirmed that the proposed project site was stable and suitable for construction. Then, after several years of inactivity, the Government of Tonga revealed in its 2012 Budget Report that the Chinese Government had provide a TOP 13 million grant for the design of Phase 2 (as recorded in Project ID#65917).   In October 2012, Tonga agreed to host the 2019 Pacific Games and the sports facilities at Tonga High School were intended to be one of the locations for the game's events. In December 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tonga signed an exchange of letters, committing grant funding for Phase 2 of the Tonga High School Reconstruction Project.   Then, in March 2017, a Chinese design team visited Tonga for 27 days to finalize plans for the project. The team was led by a Mr Zi Ling, and met with the Chairman of Tonga 2019 Pacific Games Organizing Committee, Lord Sevele, working out of the Tonga Sports Association and National Olympic Committee (TASNOC). On April 15, 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tonga signed as project implementation agreement, which provided TOP 55 million ($24.8 million USD) of grant funding for Phase 2 (as recorded in Project ID#49242). The grant proceeds were apparently drawn from at least two Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreements (ETCAs) that the two governments signed on November 23, 2015 and December 8, 2017 (as captured in Project ID#49235 and ID#62890).   Only a month later (May 2017), Tonga withdrew its offer to host the 2019 Pacific Games, citing that sports development was no longer of the government's priorities. However, the Chinese Government-financed design plans were finalized in November 2017 and the Chinese Government reaffirmed on December 8, 2017 that it would provide TOP 57.5 million of grant funding for the implementation of Phase 2 (as recorded in Project ID#62890). By the time the Government of Tonga published its 2018-2019 Budget Report, the Tongan authorities had revised their cost estimate of the sporting facilities to $70 million USD, but no additional financial commitments appear to have been made to cover the additional project cost.   As of December 2020, Phase 2 construction activities had not yet begun. Nor is there any record of a Chinese Government grant disbursement for Phase 2 from 2015 onwards.

Title: Members of Kenya's Ministry of Foreign Affairs take Chinese Language Lessons
Description: On November 4, 2016, the opening ceremony for Chinese language classes for Kenyan diplomats in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs was attended by Chinese Ambassador Liu Xianfa and other Chinese and Kenyan officials. The classes were organized by the Chinese Embassy in Kenya and provided by the Confucius Institute at the University of Nairobi. The lessons come as a part of China and Kenya's efforts to enhance diplomatic relations and provide educational opportunities to strengthen government, economic, and cultural ties. The classes are designed to last four months and consist of 96 hours of language lessons, the recipients of which will include 30 diplomats and the director and ambassador of the Kenyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The members who excel and earn good test scores in these classes will be provided the opportunity to study further in China. The project appears to be complete now, although its cost is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government donates desks, chairs, and teaching equipment to Lazaret 4 and Talladjé 5 schools in Niamey (linked to #17839)
Description: On 14 June, 2011, the Chinese Government donated desks, chairs, and teaching equipment worth 9,540,000 XOF to two primary schools in Niamey: Lazaret 4 and Talladjé 5 (or l’Ecole Talladjé V or Ecole de l’Amitié).

Title: China Funds and Renovates Road for Mao Zedong Secondary School in Namibia (Linked to #41119)
Description: In 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Namibia, through the Chamber of Commerce, pledged to finance the paving and stoning of gravel roads outside Mao Zedong Secondary School's (project #41119) main entrance. Chinese enterprises Right-Path Investments and NA Construction were contracted for this project and the official completion ceremony took place on 21 September 2018. The value of this project and construction start date are unknown.

Title: Chinese embassy donates books to Nouakchott University
Description: On May 21, 2011, the Chinese embassy donated books to University of Nouakchott. According to the Chinese Embassy, the donation ceremony was attended by over 30 teachers and students._x000D_ _x000D_ The value of the books is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government grants 10,000 laptops worth RMB 64.3 million through ETCAs (linked to #88180, #88181, and #88182)
Description: On October 11, 2017, the governments of China and Ecuador signed Letters of Exchange, which committed a grant of 10,000 computers worth 64.3 million RMB to be used for the Incorporation of Information Communication Technology in Education project (Incorporación de TICs en la Educación). The grant was to be funded through three Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreements, signed October 25, 2013; December 18, 2013; and January 7, 2015 (see #88180, #88181, and #88182 respectively). The breakdown of funds between these three agreements is unknown.   On June 6, 2018, the handover certificate was signed. The laptops were handed over to the Ecuadorian Minister of Education, which was to subsequently distribute them to public schools across the country. The grant is intended to provide tools for teacher development and is part of the Ministry's Digital Education Agenda.   Several media reports list the value as $10 or $10.7 million. The devices are equipped with Windows 10 PRO, 2TB hard disk, 8 GB RAM, WiFi connection, webcams, and other features.

Title: CNPC Great Wall Drilling Company finances training of 20 Sudanese employees
Description: In 2007, Great Wall Drilling Company of the China National Petroleum Corporation sponsored 150,000 USD to send 20 of its Sudanese employees to China for technical training._x000D_ _x000D_ The commitment, start, and end dates are unknown.

Title: Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Sichuan Province donates books and sporting goods to establish the 'Overseas Huiqiao Panda Bookstore' at the Philippine Chinese Education Center (linked to project ID#96607)
Description: On November 23, 2021, the Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Sichuan Province and the Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Dazhou City made a donation of goods to the Philippine Chinese Education Center. This donation included over 300 books for the establishment of the "Overseas Huiqiao Panda Bookstore," (Chinese:海外惠侨熊猫书屋)  The "Overseas Huiqiao Panda Bookstore" project is sponsored by the Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Sichuan Province to provide Chinese-language materials to overseas Chinese people and spread Chinese language and culture. The donation also included a variety of sporting goods and games, including basketballs, soccer balls, volleyballs, table tennis equipment, badminton equipment, jump ropes, Chinese chess, go, checkers, and military flags. The Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Dazhou City and the Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Sichuan Province both contributed to this donation, although the monetary value and the amount contributed by each party is unknown. See project ID#96607 for the Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Dazhou City's contribution.
Funding_Agencies: Overseas Chinese Affairs Office of Sichuan Province

Title: China sponsors 40 students to study in China in 2014 (Linked to Umbrella Project #62084)
Description: On 30 November 2011, the Chinese State Councilor decided to sponsor 200 Namibian students to study in China from 2012-2016 (40 students per academic year). In 2014, 40 Namibian students traveled to China through this scholarship program for the 2014/15 academic year. The value of each scholarship as well as the start and end dates are unknown.

Title: China gives 11 government scholarships to Bahamians
Description: On August 22, 2018, China granted 11 Government Scholarships to Bahamians for their studies in Chinese universities from the Bachelors to the Doctoral levels. On August 23, 2018, a farewell ceremony was help for the students in the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Commonwealth of the Bahamas. The scholarship covers full tuition, room and board, medical insurance, monthly allowances, and a round trip economy class plane ticket.  The students will study at Peking University, Tsinghua University, University of Science and Technology of China, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, or China University of Petroleum.

Title: Chinese Government provides $1.47 million grant for Ambohidratrimo High School Construction Project
Description: In 2008, the Chinese Government agreed in principle to provide a grant for the Ambohidratrimo High School Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a high school in Ambohidratrimo District with thirteen classrooms, five rooms for administrative staff,  four washrooms, two basketball courts, an athletics track, a playground, and a ping-pong table. Upon completion, the school was expected to accommodate up to 1200 students. This project experienced major delays due to the economic crisis that plagued the county in 2009. Then, on December 20, 2010, the Chinese Government and the Government of Madagascar signed a $1,477,214 grant agreement for the Ambohidratrimo High School Construction Project. The project did not officially commence until May 1, 2014. It was completed on January 13, 2015. Then, on January 16, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Madagascar signed the project handover certificate. The project was officially handed over to the authorities on February 2, 2015.

Title: Chinese citizens living in South Africa donate ZAR 15,000 and over 300 backpacks to Realogile High School
Description: On January 21, 2009, the Chinese Consulate General in Johannesburg, on behalf of the overseas Chinese in South Africa, donated money to a school in Johannesburg.  The donation included a grant of ZAR 15,000 and 300 backpacks to Realogile High School in Alexandra, Gauteng Province, South Africa. The handover ceremony was held at Realogile High School and attended by the Chinese Consul General in Johannesburg Fang Li, South African Overseas Chinese Representative Xu Changbin, local South African officials, and 1,400 teachers and students from Realogile High School.

Title: China Cultural Center in Benin provides training for over 200 students in Chinese language, martial arts, painting, photography, and film.
Description: On July 6th, 2019, the Chinese Cultural Center in Benin held the closing ceremony for the over 200 students of the 2018-19 Training Courses. The Cultural Center hosted trainings in Chinese language, martial arts, photography, painting, and film. Over 100 students passed their exams and received certificates of completion. The closing ceremony served as a performance to showcase what the students had learned in their trainings. It is unclear when the trainings began.

Title: Chinese Government provides 20 scholarships via China–Pacific Islands Forum Scholarship Program in 2019
Description: In 2019, the Chinese Government offered 20 scholarships to nationals of Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) countries under the China–PIF Scholarship Scheme for the 2019-2020 academic year. The value of each scholarship is unknown.

Title: China offered government scholarships to 3 Bahamians for their studies in Chinese universities
Description: In August 2006, China offered government scholarships to 3 Bahamians for their studies in Chinese universities. The awarding ceremony for the scholarships was held on August 25, 2006.

Title: Chinese government awards “China-Africa Friendship” Chinese Government scholarships to four graduates of the Universidade Lusofona from Guinea-Bissau
Description: On July 30, 2019, the Chinese ambassador to Guinea-Bissau, Jin Hongjun, visited Universidade Lusofona and awarded the “China-Africa Friendship” 2019 Chinese Government Scholarships to four outstanding graduates of the school. The "China-Africa Friendship" scholarship is one of the important achievements of the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. President Randi and more than 150 teachers and students attended the award ceremony.

Title: China funds expansion of “Children’s Smile” orphanage in the Democratic Republic of Congo
Description: On January 28, 2018, a handover ceremony of the expanded “Children’s Smile” orphanage, which was funded by the Chinese embassy, Chinese Enterprises Association, and the Federation of Overseas Chinese, was held in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo.  The project included an expansion of the orphanage. The Chinese Enterprises Association also donated daily necessities to the orphanage. The value of the donation and when construction began are unknown.

Title: Chinese Embassy provides 500 handheld electronic smartboards to kindergarten affiliated with the National University of Laos in July 2020
Description: On July 23, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated 500 handheld electronic smartboards to the kindergarten affiliated with the National University of Laos. The smartboards have a "Gift from the Chinese People" label and a LCD screen for eye protection. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony took place for this donation. At the ceremony, Chinese Counselor Qin Chen handed the smartboards over to Gongxi, the Deputy Dean of the School of Education of the National University, and the director of the kindergarten.

Title: Chinese Government grants 20 million RMB to Vietnamese officials for studying socioeconomic development
Description: On May 13, 2002, the Chinese Ambassador and the Vietnamese Deputy Planning and Investment Minister signed 20 million RMB grant agreement. The grant will be used to finance socioeconomic development and fact-finding tours of China by 15 delegations of Vietnamese officials.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Grenada provides education materials to two middle schools in St. David's, Grenada in March 2021
Description: On March 23, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Grenada donated educational materials to support two middle schools in the St. David's constituency of Grenada. The materials included "desks, chairs, bookshelves, books, and other materials." The USD value of the donation is unknown.

Title: China donates pool robot to the Federated States of Micronesia National Olympic Committee
Description: On June 29, 2016, the Chinese Ambassador officially donated a Dolphin Wave 300 pool robot to the Federated States of Micronesia National Olympic Committee (FSMNOC). The pool robot will clean and maintain the bottom floor of the 8 lanes 25-meter outdoor swimming pool. The value of this donation and when it was formally committed are unknown.

Title: China's Economic and Commercial Office in Mexico Hold Foreign Aid Training Class for Mexican Students
Description: On 21 March 2013, the People's Republic of China's Economic and Commercial Office in Mexico convened the Mexican Students' Association to participate in a foreign aid training class. The ambassador to Mexico Zeng Gang attended the meeting and delivered a speech. The business counselor Chen Yuming chaired the meeting.

Title: Chinese Government donates audio equipment and computers to the Diplomatic Academy of Morocco
Description: On January 11, 2010, Morocco’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Taieb Fassi Fehri, and his Chinese counterpart, Yang Jiechi, signed an agreement by which the Chinese Government agreed to make a donation to the Diplomatic Academy of Morocco [L’Académie marocaine des études diplomatiques (AMED)]. The donation included a batch of teaching equipment and materials, including audio equipment and computers. The materials the Chinese Government shipped to Morocco in early 2011 and were installed by technicians.   On April 26, 2011, during an inauguration ceremony at AMED, Secretary-General Amrani thanked the Chinese Government for providing audio equipment and for supporting the construction of the Academy. The mandate of AMED, which is affiliated with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is to train and provide on-the-job education for Moroccan diplomats.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Moldova Donated to the Center for the Placement and Rehabilitation of Young Children of the Republic of Moldova
Description: On December 4, 2019, Zhang Yanjun, wife of the Chinese ambassador to Moldova attended a donation ceremony for the Center for the Placement and Rehabilitation of Young Children of the Republic of Moldova. The center is an orphanage. The nature of the donation is unclear.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Sudan donates uniforms to Rabha Primary School
Description: On October 23, 2017, Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Li Lianhe attended a ceremony at the Rabha Primary School in Khartoum to donate more than 5,600 uniforms to Sudanese primary school students (中国驻苏丹使馆向苏丹小学捐赠校服项目). A total of about 500 people attended the meeting, including Fuzia, the representative of the Olivia District Government of Khartoum State, Sudan, the representative of the Ministry of Education of Sudan, and the vice-chairman of Biltewasu Charity, Batur, the principal of Rabiha Elementary School, and teachers and students.This project was jointly launched by the Chinese Embassy in Sudan and the Al-Birr and Al-Tawasul Organization (BTO, a Sudanese non-governmental organization).

Title: China donated $3000 to the Bahamas Junkanoo Performance Council
Description: On December 7 2006, Chinese Ambassador to the Bahamas Li Yuanming donated $3000 to the Bahamas Junkanoo Performance Council, the recipient of the donation, in order to support the traditional cultural activities in the Bahamas. _x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese Embassy in Cameroon donates computer equipment to the International School of Security Forces
Description: On September 26, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Cameroon donated computer equipment to the International School of Security Forces (EIFORCES) in Yaoundé. The donation was presented by Colonel Major Chao Xiaoliang, military, naval, and air attaché of the Embassy to the Director General of EIFORCES, Andre Patrice Bitote. The donation included computers, printers, surge protectors, and inverters.

Title: Chinese Embassy and Confucius Institute launch Chinese language program for Ethiopian airport employees
Description: In May 2017, Addis Ababa Bole International Airport said it had seen 70 Ethiopian customer service professionals graduate recently from a Chinese language training program aimed at providing better service to Chinese passengers. The Chinese Embassy in Addis Ababa organized the program in partnership with the Confucius Institute. The language training was performed over a 10-week period. According to China Daily, a second round of training was due to start soon after May 2017. It is unclear how much the training cost the Chinese embassy and/or the Confucius Institute.

Title: Hanban and the Chinese government offer a Chinese language programme to the Jamaica Constabulary Force
Description: In 2015, Hanban and the Chinese government introduced the Chinese language programme to the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF). According to the JCF 2016 Annual Report, the JCF and the People's Republic of China collaborated to deliver the first Mandarin course to 65 JCF members in 2016. _x000D_ _x000D_ On 11 August 2017, 50 police officers from Jamaica and two police officers from Suriname were awarded certificates for a Chinese training course at National Police College of Jamaica (NPCJ). On 31 August 2018, 68 police officers from Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, and Suriname were awarded certificates of completion for a Chinese training course at the Jamaica Police Academy. On 2 August 2019, 78 police officers from Jamaica and two police officers from Suriname were awarded certificates of completion for a Chinese training course at the Jamaica Police Academy. These Chinese training courses help Jamaican police understand the Chinese language and culture.
Funding_Agencies: Hanban (Confucius Institute Headquarters)|Unspecified Chinese Government Institution

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 56 million grant for Vocational Training Center Project
Description: On April 21, 2014, Chinese Ambassador to Cambodia Bu Jianguo and Cambodia’s Minister of Finance and Economics Ampang Monila signed a letter of exchange for a 56 million RMB grant from the Chinese Government for the project of assisting the Cambodian Westport Vocational and Technical Training Center in Phnom Penh, known as 西港职业技术培训中心项目 in Chinese ("布建国大使与安蓬莫尼拉部长签署西港职业技术培训中心项目立项换文"). The project and formal grant agreement with Cambodia's Ministry of Labor and Vocational Training were approved on September 2, 2015.  Construction began on December 10, 2015, and was completed on June 10, 2017. This project is located inside the Sihanoukville Special Economic Zone in Preah Sihanouk Province.   The project includes the construction of classrooms, auditoriums, teaching workshops, and offices. After completion, the training center will mainly serve the Sihanoukville Special Economic Zone and the southwestern provinces of Cambodia. It will train a large number of skilled workers for the special zone and the settled enterprises, improve the quality of the local labor force, and improve the employment status of local enterprises ("布建国大使与安蓬莫尼拉部长签署西港职业技术培训中心项目立项换文").

Title: Chinese Embassy renovates an auditorium of the BiH Cinematheque
Description: In December 2016, Chinese Embassy hired a construction company to restore the auditorium of the BiH Cinematheque in Bosnia and Herzegovina.  On December 11, 2017, Ambassador Chen Bo attended the ceremony of opening the renovated cinema hall of the public institution Cinematheque BiH. Director of the Cinematheque BiH Mrs Filipović, President of the Association Bosnian-Chinese Friendship Mr Borić, wife of the director of the movie “Valter Defends Sarajevo” Hajrudin Krvavac, Mrs Ešrefa Krvavac and many other distinguished individuals from culture, art and film industry in BiH attended the event.

Title: Chinese Embassy awards 89 scholarships to students of NUML (Linked to project #43804)
Description: On May 4th, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Pakistan Yao Jing distributed scholarship checks to 89 Pakistani students of the National University of Modern Languages (NUML). 300 students of NUML applied for the scholarship, 103 were called for interview after scrutiny and later by the independent committee recommended 89 students for the scholarship. The scholarships are directly linked to NUML's Confucius Institute, recorded in project #43804.

Title: China grants RMB 650,000 for Samoan archers to train in China (Linked to ETCA #70224)
Description: On January 14, 2010, Chinese and Samoan government officials signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA #70224) granting an unspecified amount to the Government of Samoa. On November 25, 2011, officials signed an exchange of letters allocating RMB 650,000 from this ETCA for the support of Samoan archers to travel to China for training. _x000D_ _x000D_ According to page 32 of the Annual Report of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for the Financial Year July 2011- June 2012, the money covered "international air tickets, expenses of their stay in China on living, transportation, health care and international air tickets of the Chinese coach and interpreter and the expenses of their stay in NZ on living as well as the archery equipment and sports costumes provided by the Chinese Government." Title: China held a series of Uzbekistan and China training sessions to provide advanced techniques from China
Description: On December 20, 2019, the National Project Management Agency under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan hosted the 2019 Uzbekistan-China training course summary meeting. The course had students train in China. Uzbekistan’s Deputy Director Parker, Deputy Director Maksudov, and Uzbek Business Administration Principal Abdulaupo attended the summary meeting, as well as 65 representatives of trainees sent to China shared their learning insights.   The training content focused on bilateral practical cooperation and covered a wide range of fields. Experience, improving vocational skills, and broadening horizons provide were the focus of the training. Over the entire period of cooperation (2018-2019), the Agency with the Office of the Counselor for Trade and Economic Affairs of the Embassy of the PRC, represented by the Ministry of Commerce of the PRC, successfully organized more than 300 seminars and trainings on various topics for public sector employees of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Description: On March 23, 2016, China announced it would provide the opportunity for 400 Nepali to be trained in human resource development, as well as offer more government scholarships to Nepalese as part of an effort to enhance contact between their peoples. Title: Chinese funds 2018 China-Gambian Information Technology and Media Bilateral Training Course
Description: The Chinese Embassy, along with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Higher Education, and the Ministry of Information, created the 2018 Zhonggang Information Technology and Media Bilateral Training Course. On April 13, 2018, Ambassador to the Gambia Zhang Jiming held a farewell reception at the Embassy for the 50 students who will attend this training course. This exchange training will teach about information technology and multi-media development in China. The financing details of this project is unknown, as is its current status. They are also in line with Gambia's National Development Plan.

Title: Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group Co., Ltd., donates school supplies to children's hospital in Senegal
Description: On June 1st, 2019, Jiangsu Provincial Construction Group Co., Ltd., celebrated International Children's Day by holding the "Caring for Children and Dedicating Love" event. Jiangsu Provincial was the implementation unit for the Senegal Children's Hospital technical cooperation project, which has had three batches of technical cooperation teams to protect the normal operation of the children’s hospital facilities and the normal operation of the hospital sent since 2014. Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 5 million grant for Taiz Rural School Construction Project
Description: On June 24, 2008, the Chinese Embassy in Yemen and the Yemeni Government signed letters of exchange, which committed RMB 5 million (or $700,000) grant agreement for the Taiz Rural School Construction Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was the source of funding.   This project involved the construction of a primary school with 15 classrooms in Saber al-Mawadim (صبر الموادم) district within Taiz Governorate. A construction contract was issued to Sinohydro Corporation Ltd. on April 13, 2010 in Sana'a. The project commenced on May 30, 2010 and ended on January 10, 2011. It passed final MOFCOM inspection on January 15, 2012.

Title: China donates 10,000 USD worth of sports equipment to the Uganda Olympic Committee
Description: On December 19, 2003, the Chinese government, through the Beijing Olympic Games Organizers donated 10,000 USD worth of sports equipment to local federations to help them prepare for next year's Summer Olympics in Athens. Chinese ambassador Li Qiangmin handed over the donation that included 96 basketballs, 96 volleyballs, 96 footballs, 100 tunes of badminton shuttles and 50 rackets to Uganda Olympic Committee President Francis Nyangweso.

Title: China Eximbank provides $16.1 million buyer’s credit loan for Luanda and Benguela Secondary School Construction and Equipping Project (Linked to Project ID#42029, #34802, #85457)
Description: On November 28, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Angolan Government signed a framework agreement pertaining to a special economic cooperation arrangement (Agreement name in Chinese: 中华人民共和国商务部与安哥拉共和国财政部关于两国经贸合作特殊安排的框架协议).  Following the signing of the framework agreement, on March 2, 2004, China Eximbank entered into a $2 billion Master Loan Facility Agreement (MLFA) with the Government of Angola. All borrowings under the MLFA, which is an oil prepayment facility,  carried the following estimated borrowing terms: a 21.5 maturity, a 1.5 year grace period, an interest rate of 3-month LIBOR plus a 1.5% margin, a 0.3% management fee, and a 0.3% commitment fee.  The facility was split between a $1.0 billion Phase I facility and a $1.0 billion Phase II facility.  Availability of the Phase II facility was subject to confirmation by the lender on or prior to the date falling five years after satisfaction of the conditions precedent to the MLFA and was made available by China Eximbank during that period.  The MLFA is a framework agreement under which the Government of Angola and China Eximbank may conclude individual buyer’s credit loan agreements (ILAs or subsidiary loan agreements) for the purpose of financing up to 90% of the contract price owing to certain contractors in respect of certain contracts.  The first tranche of the facility was released in December 2004.  The facility was fully drawn down as of December 31, 2017.  Sonangol provided a source of collateral under the MLFA, and repayments were made with the proceeds of oil sales from Sonangol to UNIPEC (China international United Petroleum & Chemicals Co. Ltd, Sinopec group), which were deposited in an Angolan Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) account at China Eximbank.  The volume of oil to be sold to UNIPEC each month for repayment of the loan varied according to market oil prices.  Under the agreement, 70% of works have to be contracted with Chinese companies and the same proportion of construction material, equipment and labour has to be contracted in China.  Loan disbursements were made on a project-by-project basis.  Tendering, management and payments were jointly managed by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the Angolan Ministry of Finance (which coordinated the various Angolan line ministries responsible for supervising the projects).   The Angolan Ministry of Finance submitted the projects for tendering; China Eximbank selected Chinese candidate firms for the projects; and a joint commission made the final firm selections. The process was managed by an office in the Angolan Ministry of Finance -- known as Gabinete de Apoio Técnico (GAT) -- that was specifically created to manage the MLFA with China Eximbank.  In March 2005, China Eximbank and the Government of Angola signed a $16,163,641.55  subsidiary buyer’s credit loan agreement under the 2004 MLFA for the Luanda and Benguela Secondary School Construction and Equipping Project (as captured via Project ID#34775).  The proceeds of the loan were used to partially finance a $17,959,601.79 commercial contract with China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC), which was signed on March 10, 2005.    The purpose of the project was to construct and equip three secondary schools in the Viana [Sapú], Cacuaco and Nova Vida localities within Luanda Province, and construct and equip one secondary school in the Massangarala locality within Benguela Province.  15 Angola workers and 39 Chinese workers were employed through the project.  CMEC was the contractor responsible for project implementation. The implementation of the project commenced on April 17, 2006 and reached completion on June 18, 2007. The project was originally scheduled to commence on March 20, 2006 and various components of the project were originally scheduled for completion on April 30, 2007, July 12, 2007, and October 25, 2007.  China Eximbank and the Government of Angola later signed an additional buyer’s credit loan agreement to support 'complementary actions' related to the Luanda and Benguela Secondary School Construction and Equipping Project (as captured via Project ID#34802).

Title: China commits to provide Chinese government scholarships to Moldovan students in 2016-2017 (Linked to #91327)
Description: In accordance with the provisions of the Cooperation Agreement between the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China and the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Moldova, signed on April 14, 2014, in Beijing, students of the Republic of Moldova are awarded scholarships for the academic year 2016-2017 to the first and second cycle, as well as advanced training courses. The studies are preceded by a preparatory year, during which the Chinese language and terminology specific to the selected specialized profile will be studied.    The educational agreement is recorded in #91327.  Although China commits to provide the scholarship, there is no update on whether students applied.

Title: China donates electric car to Laos National University
Description: On November 30, 2012, the Chinese government donated an electric vehicle to the National University of Laos in Vientiane._x000D_ _x000D_ During the same donation ceremony, Huawei also sponsored the donation of a cloud computing laboratory, which is captured in project #73289._x000D_

Title: Chinese Embassy Donates Teaching Devices to a Primary School in Kenya
Description: On November 15, 2014 Chinese Ambassador Liu Xianfa donated teaching devices to Sisini Primary School.

Title: Chinese Government awards 35 scholarships to STP students in 2018 (linked to project ID#55648)
Description: On August 21st, 2018, a farewell reception was held for the 35 international students from Sao Tome and Principe who received the Chinese Government Scholarship in 2018. 35 students received the Chinese Government Scholarship to study abroad in China and further cooperation between STP and China. Students were expected to use their education to further development in STP after the completion of their studies.

Title: Chinese Government provides 76 scholarships to Algerian students
Description: China has offered 76 Algerian students scholarships to study there in 2008. This was spoken about by Djamel-Eddine Grine, who is the Ambassador of Algeria to China. _x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 30 million grant — via ETCA — for Sino-Egyptian Friendship Model School Construction Project (Linked to ID#72444)
Description: On April 20, 2002, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Egypt’s Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which committed RMB 30 million ($3.75 million) of grant funding for the Sino-Egyptian Friendship Model School Construction Project. This project involved the construction of a school in the 11th district within the 6th of October City (مدينة السادس من أكتوبر) in Giza Governorate. The school has 42 classrooms and a set of laboratories. It occupies an area of 11,268 m^2 and has a floor area of 6,256 m^2. It serves students in kindergarten, primary school, and secondary school.   The ultimate purpose of the project was to promote Chinese language and history education among Egyptian youth. The school also seeks to provide Chinese language instruction so students can compete for jobs as the importance of Chinese language increases within and without Egypt. Additionally, the school seeks to deepen cultural exchanges and trade ties between Egypt and China.   China State Construction Engineering Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction commenced on December 18, 2006. The project was completed and the school was officially inaugurated on September 7, 2008. The school was inaugurated with the signature of a cooperation agreement between Egyptian Minister of Investment and International Cooperation, Fayza Abdul-Naga, and Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce Fu Ziying. At the inauguration ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Egypt Wu Sike, and Egyptian Minister of Education Yosri El-Gamal mentioned that the school was the first to offer Chinese Language instruction in Egypt.   Upon opening, the school accepted an initial class of 87 students from an applicant pool of 1,500. The 87 students were admitted to the school as its first kindergarten class. Tuition ranges between 350 and 1,000 Egyptian Pounds.

Title: Chinese Ambassador pledges grant to support industry in Sierra Leone in February 2018
Description: In late February 2018, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Sierra Leone, Wu Peng, pledged a donation of sewing machines, televisions, other equipment, and financial support from the Chinese Government while addressing a graduation ceremony for a manufacturing training class provided by the E4Impact Foundation in Lunsar. On the same occasion, Wu Peng announced that a team of Chinese experts would travel to Sierra Leone to provide related training to young people in Lunsar. The monetary value of this donation and the status of its delivery are uncertain.

Title: Chinese military sponsors development of shooting range at the Royal Gendarmerie Training Center
Description: On December 17, 2021 the Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister General Tea Banh and Chinese ambassador to Cambodia Wang Wentian presided over the groundbreaking ceremony for a new shooting range at the Royal Gendarmerie Training Center. The Royal Gendarmerie Training Center will built a shooting range on 105 hectares, and the project is supported by the Chinese military. According to General Banh,  the shooting range will serve as the venue for the 2023 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Armies Rifle Meet.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Ukraine provides grant for China-Ukraine Poetry Garden at Taras Shevchenko National University in Kiev
Description: At the end of 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Ukraine provided a donation to build a poetry garden at Taras Shevchenko National University in Kiev. Specifically, the garden was built to accompany the statues by Wu Weishan, a famous Chinese bronze sculptor, donated by the Chinese Embassy to the university in 2017. (captured via Project ID#98734) On October 9, 2019, the opening ceremony for the China-Ukraine poetry garden was held.

Title: Chinese Government hosts the Advanced Seminar on Cultural Industry and Management for Mexican officials (Linked to Project ID#70330)
Description: In 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Mexico, the Chinese Cultural Center in Mexico, and the El Colegio de México, A.C. (Colmex), co-sponsored at the 2018 "Cultural China" Special Training at El Colegio de México. The trainees represented various aspects of Mexican culture, including officials, curators, museum officials, writers, editors, designers, musicians, dancers, artists, cinematographers and others involved in the film and television industry, and Mexican researchers and educators on China. The opening ceremony of the training course was held on August 11, 2018, and the training was set to end on September 8, 2018. For this training, see linked project ID#70330.  After this training, a select number of its participants, as well as 20 other Mexican trainees selected by Mexico's Secretariat of Foreign Affairs, Secretariat of Culture, and other cultural institutions were to visit China from October 11 to October 31, 2018 for the Advanced Seminar on Cultural Industry and Management, a three-week visit and training period to learn about China's cultural policies and practices, trade, and exchanges during visits to Beijing, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen. This seminar is captured by this project.

Title: China Donates Sports Equipment to Myanmar Under Chinese Sports Equipment Assistance Project
Description: On September 27, 2019, the Chinese Embassy held the exchange of letters ceremony regarding the donation of sports equipment to Myanmar. The Chinese Ambassador and the Vice Minister of Health and Sports attended the ceremony. China agreed to donate 8 racing boats and 10 dragon boats to Myanmar.  On July 30, 2020, representatives from the Chinese Embassy signed the contract of implementation and donated the equipment to Burmese officials.

Title: Chinese Embassy Donated Sports Supplies to the Ministry of Youth and Sports of Grenada
Description: On November 26, 2010, the Economic and Commerce Office of the Chinese Embassy in Grenada donated a batch of sports supplies to Grenada's Ministry of Youth and Sports in advance of the Christmas holiday. Chinese First Secretary Zhang Peng handed over the donation on behalf of the embassy and it was received by Ministry Secretary Veda Bruno-Victor.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 10 million grant for Arkra Primary School and Otuam Primary School Construction Project in Ghana
Description: In September 2011, the Chinese Government and the Government of Ghana signed an RMB 10 million grant agreement for the construction of two primary schools. This project involved the construction of Arkra Primary School and Otuam Primary School in Ekumfi District. Each schools included six classrooms, a library, an office to accommodate 12 members of staff, a head teacher’s office, washrooms, a space for recreational activities, and a fence wall. China Geo-Engineering Corporation was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project officially commenced on September 3, 2012 and was completed and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities on September 18, 2013.

Title: China and Sudan sign cooperation agreement on mineral resources
Description: In 2012, Sudan's Ministry of Minerals signed a cooperation agreement with the Ministry of Land Resources of China for a project of geochemical investigation and evaluation of mineral resources in Sudan. The agreement intends to upgrade the level of work and research in geology and mineral resources in Sudan as well as the training of geologists and geochemists in the Chinese Geological Research Corporation. The agreement determined that the project will progress for three years.

Title: All-China Women’s Federation donates electronic equipment to JNCW in 2005
Description: On March 10, 2005, the Jordanian National Commission for Women (JNCW) received a donation of computer and electronic equipment from the All-China Women’s Federation. Throughout the ceremony, the JNCW expressed their gratitude towards the donation as it “fosters cooperation between national mechanisms” and will support the commission’s work. The specific contributions of the donation are unknown.

Title: China donates assorted items to women's groups in Liberia
Description: In December 2012, the Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Zhao Jianhua donated several assorted items, including sewing machines, electronic fans, bags of rice, among other items, to the Sirleaf Market Women Fund, Ever Orphanage Home, Group of 77, Concerned Women for Development and Presbyterian Today Mission School. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chine Embassy donates office furniture to the South Sudan Women's Association
Description: On February 12, 2015, Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Ma Qiang attended a ceremony to handover a set of office tables and chairs to the South Sudanese Women's Association in the outskirts of Juba. The total cost of the supplies donated is unknown.

Title: China donates sewing machine to women's committee in Samoa
Description: On February 14, 2008, the Chinese Ambassador to Samoa visited the Women's Committee of Sapaia Village, and donated a sewing machine. The sewing machine will play a role to improve women's life skills and increase employment opportunities in Samoa.

Title: China Eximbank provides $40.225 million for Luanda Water Supply System Rehabilitation Project (Linked to Project ID#42029)
Description: On November 28, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Angolan Government signed a framework agreement pertaining to a special economic cooperation arrangement (Agreement name in Chinese: 中华人民共和国商务部与安哥拉共和国财政部关于两国经贸合作特殊安排的框架协议). Availability of the Phase II facility was subject to confirmation by the lender on or prior to the date falling five years after satisfaction of the conditions precedent to the MLFA and was made available by China Eximbank during that period.  The MLFA is a framework agreement under which the Government of Angola and China Eximbank may conclude individual buyer’s credit loan agreements (ILAs or subsidiary loan agreements) for the purpose of financing up to 90% of the contract price owing to certain contractors in respect of certain contracts.  The first tranche of the facility was released in December 2004.  The facility was fully drawn down as of December 31, 2017.  Sonangol provided a source of collateral under the MLFA, and repayments were made with the proceeds of oil sales from Sonangol to UNIPEC (China international United Petroleum & Chemicals Co. Ltd, Sinopec group), which were deposited in an Angolan Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) account at China Eximbank.  The volume of oil to be sold to UNIPEC each month for repayment of the loan varied according to market oil prices.  Under the agreement, 70% of works have to be contracted with Chinese companies and the same proportion of construction material, equipment and labour has to be contracted in China.  Loan disbursements were made on a project-by-project basis.  Tendering, management and payments were jointly managed by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the Angolan Ministry of Finance (which coordinated the various Angolan line ministries responsible for supervising the projects).   The Angolan Ministry of Finance submitted the projects for tendering; China Eximbank selected Chinese candidate firms for the projects; and a joint commission made the final firm selections. The process was managed by an office in the Angolan Ministry of Finance -- known as Gabinete de Apoio Técnico (GAT) -- that was specifically created to manage the MLFA with China Eximbank.  In March 2005, China Eximbank and the Government of Angola signed a $40,225,877.10 buyer's credit loan agreement under the MLFA for the Luanda Water Supply System Rehabilitation Project.  The proceeds of this loan were used to partially finance a $44,695,419.00 commercial (EPC) contract with China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC).    The project, which employed 150 Angolan workers and 153 Chinese workers, involved an ETA in Candelabro, a new water catchment in Quifangondo, the addition of intake pipes and the implementation of fountains in the municipalities of Viana and Cacuaco.  CMEC was the EPC contractor responsible for project implementation. The EPC contract supporting the project was originally scheduled to commenced on November 18, 2005 and the project had an originally scheduled handover date of October 2007.  The project was ultimately completed, according to Angola’s Ministry of Finance; however, it is unclear exactly when the project was completed.

Title: China Eximbank provides $381.09 million preferential buyer’s credit for Greater Abuja Water Supply Project
Description: On May 29, 2018, China Eximbank and the Government of Nigeria signed a $381,095,036.84 preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement for the Greater Abuja Water Supply Project. The PBC (loan) carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 7 year grace period, and a 2.5% interest rate. The final maturity date of the loan is March 21, 2038. As of December 31, 2020, Nigeria’s Debt Management Office (DMO) reported that the $381.09 million loan had not yet disbursed and the borrower had not made any interest or principal repayments to the lender.    The proceeds of the PBC are to be used by the borrower to partially finance a commercial contract between the Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA) and CGCOC Group Co., Ltd. (中地海外集团), which was signed on May 2, 2018. The purpose of this project is to provide potable water supply to Garki, Asokoro and the Central Business District. The project will rely upon the Lower Usuma Dam Water Treatment Plant and the Wupa Water Treatment Plant in Abuja to do so. CGCOC Group Co., Ltd. (中地海外集团) is the contractor responsible for implementation. Construction began in July 2021.

Title: China Funds Goudel III Water Treatment Plant Expansion Project in Niger
Description: In 2017, China pledged to finance and build phase III of a water treatment plant in Goudel region, Niamey, Niger. According to the French Development Agency (AFD), this project was co-financed by AFD, International Development Association (IDA), and the West African Development Bank (BOAD)._x000D_ _x000D_ China Geo-Engineering Corporation is the contractor. The main works include: construction of flocculator, mixing weir, sedimentation tank, and supply & installation of matched hydraulic & electric equipment.

Title: China Eximbank provides additional $75.4 million preferential buyer’s credit for Bui Dam Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#183, #30709, #30801, #95483, #95484)
Description: On September 25, 2007, China Eximbank and the Government of Ghana signed a buyer’s credit loan (BCL) agreement worth $293,506,062 for the Bui Dam Construction Project. Then, on September 3, 2008, China Eximbank and the Government of Ghana signed a government concessional loan (GCL) agreement worth RMB 2.1 billion ($330 million). The BCL carried the following borrowing terms: a 17.2 year-maturity (final maturity date: November 21, 2025), a 5-year grace period (first repayment date: September 3, 2013), an interest rate of CIRR plus a margin of 0.75% (6.13%), a 0.3% commitment fee, and a 0.3% management fee. The GCL carried the following borrowing terms: a 2% interest rate, a 20 year maturity (final maturity date: September 3, 2028), a 7 year grace period (first repayment date: September 3, 2015), a 0.3% commitment fee, and a 0.3% management fee. The GCL is captured via Project ID#30801 and the BCL is captured via Project ID#183. The BCL was collateralized with (a) net revenue from a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) between Bui Power Authority — an organization with a mandate to plan, execute and manage the Bui Hydroelectric Power Plant Project — and the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) for the purchase of the energy to be generated from the Bui hydroelectric power plant, and (b) receivables from Ghana Cocoa Board’s sale of up to 30,000 tons of main crop cocoa and 10,000 tons of light crop cocoa per annum to Genertec International Corporation of Beijing under a 20-year, Cocoa Sales Agreement (CSA); and (c) and a mortgage of the land and building and equipment and machinery of the Bui Hydroelectric Power Plant. The cocoa beans were sold at the prevailing market price rather than a fixed price, and the proceeds were to be placed in a Government of Ghana bank account to facilitate loan repayment (and provide a source of security for the BCL). Then, once the dam was operational (and the cocoa agreement came to an end), 85% of the proceeds from sales of energy generated by the Bui hydroelectric power plant were to be placed in an escrow account held by China Eximbank to facilitate loan repayment (and provide a source of security for the BCL). The borrower was expected to maintain a minimum cash balance in the escrow account. The escrow account balance was $27,275,000 in 2018 and $25,582,000 in 2019. The Government of Ghana bank account (for the cash proceeds from COCOBOD’s sale of cocoa to Genertec International Corporation of Beijing) had a balance of $167,816,000 in 2018 and $209,783,000 in 2019. The GCL, by contrast, was not collateralized; it was backed by the full faith and credit of the Government of Ghana. The borrower also purchased a buyer’s credit insurance policy from Sinosure at a cost of $25 million for the BCL (i.e. 8.5% of the face value of the BCL). The GCL and PBC were eventually rescheduled such that repayments would commence on July 15, 2023 and end on July 15, 2037, which implies a maturity extension of 8.8 years and a grace period extension of 7.8 years for the GCL and a maturity extension of 5.2 years and a grace period extension of 6.2 years for the PBC. The 2% interest rate that originally applied to both the GCL and PBC also increased to 2.7% as part of the rescheduling. The GCL rescheduling is captured via Project ID#95483. The PBC rescheduling is captured via Project ID#95484.  The Bui Dam Construction Project had six components: (1) a roller Compacted Concrete (RCC) gravity dam incorporating a 5-bay spillway; (2) three penstocks in the middle of the dam; (3) a powerhouse at the toe of the dam on the left bank; (4) two rock fill saddle dams on the right bank; (5) a switchyard; and (6) 276 km of transmission lines; and a permanent bridge downstream of the dam.   Sinohydro was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Its work was overseen by Bui Power Authority. The dam was designed by the French engineering firm Coyne et Bellier, which also served as the consulting engineers on the project. A groundbreaking ceremony was held on August 24, 2007. However, construction did not begin until December 2, 2008. Then, on May 3, 2013, the first generator was inaugurated. The dam was inaugurated on December 19, 2013. However, the project was not completed and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities until November 28, 2016.   There are many indications that the China Eximbank loans for the Bui Dam Construction Project have financially underperformed vis-a-vis the original expectations of the lender. First, in August 2017, the Ghana Cocoa Board (Cocobod) — a state-owned company whose export receipts provide an important source of revenue for loan repayment to China Eximbank — told the country’s parliament it was in financial distress due to its loan repayment obligations related to the construction of the Bui Dam. Second, at least two of the four loans were rescheduled. Third, in April 2023, Samuel Kofi Dzamesi, the Chief Executive Officer of BPA revealed that the ECG had accumulated $612 million of payment arrears (overdue payments) to BPA. ECG’s payments to BPA for electricity purchases were originally intended to be the main source of revenue for repaying China Eximbank. Fourth, according to the World Bank’s International Development Statistics, the Government of Ghana had accumulated principal and interest arrears to one or more official sector Chinese creditors worth $908,337,346.70) in 2020 ($763,228,526.60 in principal arrears and $145,108,820.10 in interest arrears). Fifth, on December 19, 2022, the Government of Ghana announced a sovereign default, suspending debt service on its Eurobonds, its commercial loans, and most of its bilateral loans.

Title: ICBC and China Eximbank pledges EUR 205 million loan for Linsan-Fomi-Kankan Electricity Transmission Line Project (Linked to Project ID#65113 and Project ID#64352)
Description: In 2017, ICBC and China Eximbank agreed in principle to provide a EUR 205 million loan to the Republic of Guinea for the Lisan-Fomi-Kankan Electricity Transmission Line Project. This loan will be issued as a subsidiary loan agreement under the $20 billion Resource and Loan Cooperation Framework Agreement that the Chinese Government and the Republic of Guinea signed on September 5, 2017 (see Project ID#65113 and Project ID#64352). As such, it will carry the following terms: 15-year maturity, 4 year grace period, and an interest rate of 6-month Euribor plus a 2.5% margin. The 6-month Euribor rate for September 2017 is used to calculate the interest rate (-.273% + 2.5% = 2.227%).  The proceeds of the loan will be used to fund an EPC contract that China International Water and Electrical Corporation (CWE) signed with Guinea’s Ministry of Energy and Water Resources on May 26, 2017. The purpose of this project is to transmit power generated by the China Eximbank-financed Kaleta and Souapiti hydropower plants (see Project ID#53003 and Project ID#187) by constructing 225kV electricity transmission lines between Linsan, Fomi, and Kankan that are 393 kilometers in length. It also involves the construction of four 225kV substations and some rural electrification along the line. Upon completion, the project will connect the proposed Guinea-Mali 225kV transnational transmission and distribution network in eastern Guinea with the planned OMVG, CLSG, and OMVS transmission and distribution network in Western Guinea. The African Development Bank (ADB) financed a feasibility study for this project and CWE is the contractor responsible for its implementation.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 80 million for Nouakchott Stormwater Drainage System Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#53448 and Project ID#56911)
Description: According to the Government of Mauritania’s Development Assistance Database (DAD), the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) on January 1, 2015 which committed an RMB 100 million loan for the Nouakchott Stormwater Drainage System Construction Project. This loan carried the following terms: 20 year maturity, 10 year grace period, and 0% interest rate. _x000D_ _x000D_ The Chinese Government also provided an RMB 100 million grant — through an ETCA that was signed on December 17, 2014 — to support this project. The total cost of the Nouakchott Stormwater Drainage System Construction Project was RMB 280 million and the Chinese Government fully financed the project. However, it is not known if the remaining RMB 80 million was covered through a Chinese Government grant, loan, or some combination of the two. Project ID#53448 captures the RMB 100 million interest-free loan. Project ID#56911 captures the RMB 100 million grant. Project ID#36190 captures the residual RMB 80 million. _x000D_ _x000D_ This project involved the construction of a concrete rainwater collection culvert with a total length of 31.5 kilometers, a reinforced steel rainwater pipeline of 13.6 kilometers, and four rainwater pumps in the low-lying areas of ​​Nouakchott (specifically, Ksar, Tevragh-Zeina, El Mina and Sabkha). Its ultimate purpose was to solve the problems of stagnant water in low-lying areas and waterlogging in the rainy season. China Tiesiju Civil Engineering Group Co., Ltd. (CTCE Group), which is also known as China Railway Fourth Group Co. (CREC4), is the contractor responsible for implementation. Upon completion, it was envisaged that this stormwater drainage system would allow pumping of a total quantity of 225,000 m3 per day, allowing the absorption of precipitation of 50 mm in less than 5 hours. Construction began on November 23, 2015. On November 30, 2018, the completion ceremony was held in Nouakchott. On January 29, 2019, the project was officially handed over to the local authorities in Mauritania.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 14 million grant for Tillabéri and Dosso Borehole Drilling Project
Description: In 2011, the Chinese Government provided an RMB 14 million grant to the Government of Niger for the Tillabéri and Dosso Borehole Drilling Project.  This project involved the drilling of 70 boreholes (water wells) in Tillabéri and Dosso provinces._x000D_ _x000D_ On 2 December, 2011, China Geo-Engineering Corp. International Ltd. signed a contract with the Government of Niger’s Department of Water to implement this project.  The Chinese Ambassador to Niger, Xia Huang, a CGE representative, and Issoufou Issaka, the Nigerien Water Minister signed the contract.  The project was completed and handed over to the local authorities on 30 June, 2012.  It reportedly benefited 20,000 residents of the Dosso and Tillabéri regions.

Title: China Eximbank restructures $84,000,000 loan for Djiri Water Treatment Plant Extension Project (Linked to Project ID#69323, #89048, #89049, #89051, #89054, #89061, #89062, #89063)
Description: On April 29, 2019, the Republic of Congo and China Eximbank signed a debt rescheduling agreement that applied to 8 China Eximbank loans that the Republic of Congo contracted between 2010 and 2014.   The first loan (worth $84,000,000) was contracted in 2010 for the Djiri Water Treatment Plant Extension Project (see Project ID#69323) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 13 to 20 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The second loan (worth $88,000,000) was contracted in 2010 for the Djiri Water Treatment Distribution Network Project (see Project ID#69335) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 13 to 20 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The third loan (worth $1,000,000,000) was contracted in 2013 for the Dolisie-Brazzavile Section of the Pointe-Noire-Brazzaville Road (RN1) Construction Project (see Project ID#369) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 20 years, and a grace period of 5 years.   The fourth loan (worth $96,363,372.65) was contracted in 2011 for the 19.2MW Liouesso Hydroelectric Dam Construction Project (see Project ID#31028) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 19 years, and a grace period of 4 years.   The fifth loan (worth $62,310,857.20) was contracted in 2014 for the Brazzaville Shopping Center Project (see Project ID#58408) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 14 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The sixth loan (worth $54,800,000) was contracted in 2013 for the 264 Mpila Social Housing Units Construction Project (see Project ID#31029) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 13 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The seventh loan (worth $328,100,000) was contracted in 2014 for the Mpila Twin Towers Construction Project (see Project ID#58720) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 13 to 20 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The eighth loan (worth $19,191,458.40) was contracted in 2014 for the Mpila Memorial Construction Project (see Project ID#58721) and it carried the following terms: an interest rate of 0.25%, a maturity of 14 years, and a grace period of 3 to 5 years.   The Republic of Congo’s outstanding debt obligations under these 8 loans amounted to $1,612,330,000 at the point of rescheduling in April 2019. Under the terms of the rescheduling agreement, the Republic of Congo agreed to repay 33% of its outstanding debt obligations under each of these 8 loans ($532,068,900 in total) within 3 years. For the remaining 67% of its outstanding debt obligations under each of these 8 loans, the Republic of Congo agreed to meet its obligations according to extended maturities and higher interest rates.   More specifically, China Eximbank agreed to extend the maturity of each loan by 15 years, reset the interest rate of the loan for the Dolisie-Brazzavile Section of the Pointe-Noire-Brazzaville Road (RN1) Construction Project to 2% and reset the interest rates for the other seven loans to 1.5%. Therefore, the estimated maturities and interest rates of these 8 loans after the April 2019 rescheduling are as follows:   a 31.5-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Djiri Water Treatment Plant Extension Project (captured via Project ID#58340);  a 31.5-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Djiri Water Treatment Distribution Network Project (captured via Project ID#89048);  a 35-year maturity and 2% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Dolisie-Brazzavile Section of the Pointe-Noire-Brazzaville Road (RN1) Construction Project (captured via Project ID#89049);  a 34-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the 19.2MW Liouesso Hydroelectric Dam Construction Project (captured via Project ID#89051);  a 29-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Brazzaville Shopping Center Project (captured via Project ID#89054);  a 35-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the 264 Mpila Social Housing Units Construction Project (captured via Project ID#89061);  a 31.5-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Mpila Twin Towers Construction Project (captured via Project ID#89062);  and a 29-year maturity and 1.5% interest rate for the China Eximbank loan supporting the Mpila Memorial Construction Project (see Project ID#89063).  After restructuring all eight of these loans, the net present value of total repayments to China Eximbank rose from $1.3 billion (before restructuring) to $1.6 billion (after restructuring). This increase represents a 23% increase in net present value terms.

Title: China Gezhouba Group Co (CGGC) funds US$351 million for water and wastewater projects in Zimbabwe (Linked to Project ID#87060, #87066)
Description: On October 7, 2019, Harare City Council approved the signing of US$868 million deals for water and wastewater projects with four Chinese firms, with the Government reportedly going to assist the council in repaying the loans, while the former will cede land as collateral security. The four companies - China Gezhouba Group Co or CGGC, China Geo-Engineering Co (CGEC), Sino-Hydro, and China Machinery and Engineering Co or CMEC - will carry out the works through a loan facility guaranteed by the government of Zimbabwe.  Under the deal, SinoHydro will fund and construct the Lyndhurst sewage treatment plant and expand the Crowborough sewage at a cost of US$237 million (see Project ID#87060). CGGC will fund water distribution network rehabilitation in 11 high-density suburbs for US$351 million.  For US$280 million, CMEC will install pumps at Morton Jaffray and Warren Control, construct new water pumping mains to Alexandra Park reservoirs, Hatcliffe reservoirs, Highlands reservoirs New City, Southern Incorporated areas, and expansion of Adylinn pumping mains while CMEC will implement water and wastewater projects for the Harare Metropolitan Master Plan for Reliable Water Supply Services (see Project ID#87066). The fourth company, CGEC, which will soon sign an agreement with Harare, will upgrade and rehabilitate water distribution networks in the city for US$176.7 million.

Title: China Eximbank agrees in principle to provide $285 million loan — via EPCF arrangement — for Mzima II Pipeline Water Project
Description: On July 17, 2017, the Coast Water Works Development Agency — a government-owned parastatal in Kenya — signed an Engineering, Construction, Procurement, and Financing (EPCF) contract worth $335,340,000 (Kshs 36,756,123,035.42) with M/S Avic International Holding Corporation for the Mzima II Pipeline Water Project. Avic International Holding Corporation, in turn, sought a loan worth approximately $285,039,000 from China Eximbank to finance 85% of the cost of the $335.34 million EPCF contract. The project is designed to draw water from the Mzima springs at the Tsavo River and to supply to the arid parts of Taita Taveta county.
