The proceeds were to be used by finance the expansion of the Lakatabu cement plant located at Ewekoro in Ogun State to increase its capacity by2.2 million metric tons per annum via the construction of a new 5,000 metric-ton-per-day dry production kiln line, additional storage facilities for raw materials, a conveyor belt between the quarry and the new kiln line, coal storage and grinding stations to improve the kiln's reliability, and a 100 MW captive multi-fuel power plant using six Wärtsilä 18V50DF engines. Wärtsilä and CBMI Construction were the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractors and equipment suppliers responsible for project implementation. Construction began in July 2008 and was expected to be completed in 2011. Full operations at the plant began in December 2011.

Title: Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donates 50 bicycles and 3 electric buggies to Sri Lanka Navy (SLN)
Description: On December 10, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donated 50 bicycles and 3 electric buggies to the Sri Lanka Navy (SLN). The purpose of the donation was to support the SLN's "Green and Blue environment" initiative that seeks to protect and conserve the environment  The Deputy Military Naval and Air Attaché of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Sri Lanka, Lieutenant Colonel Chang Qianjin, handed over the bicycles and buggies to Commander of the Navy, Vice Admiral Piyal De Silva during a ceremony on December 10.  The Navy intends to use these bicycles and electric vehicles at the Naval Dockyard in Trincomalee.

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 2 million grant for Parliament Building Maintenance Project
Description: In January 2000, the National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China provided an RMB 2 million grant to the Republic of Congo's Transitional Council for the Parliament Building Maintenance Project. This project involved the maintenance of air-conditioning units and elevators in the Parliament Building (Palais des Congrès) in the capital city of Brazzaville.   This building was constructed with financial support from the Chinese Government in the 1980s. On May 5, 2005, China’s Ambassador to the Republic of Congo and the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and French-speaking Affairs of the Republic of Congo Daniel OWASSA signed the project handover certificate.
Funding_Agencies: National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China

Title: Chinese Government donation of computers, printers, scanners, projection equipment, and pickup trucks to Cambodia
Description: On January 17th, 2018, Chinese Government donated computers, printers, scanners, projection equipment, and pickup trucks to Cambodia (or 援助柬埔寨政府小额物资项目). The handover ceremony of the Chinese government's assistance to the Cambodian government was held in Phnom Penh. Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister, He Nanhong, and Chinese Ambassador to Cambodia, Xiong Bo, attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. This batch of materials is one of the follow-up work of the 2017 China-Cambodia Intergovernmental Coordination Committee meeting and will help the relevant Cambodian government departments to improve office conditions.

Title: Chinese Government provides $500,000 grant for Seikena Tower Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#39307)
Description: In the 2004-2005 period, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided a $500,000 grant to the Government of Niue for the Seikena Tower Construction Project. The purpose of this project was to construct an 80-meter television and radio transmission tower (known as Seikena Tower) in Makefu and install a one-kilowatt transmitter with microwave connections from Kaimiti to Makefu. Its ultimate aim was to provide improved island-wide TV signals and fm radio reception.   Beijing Urban Construction International Co., Ltd. (BUCIO 北京城建国际建设有限公司) was the contractor responsible for implementation. Its work was supervised by China Youfa International Engineering Design Consulting Company. Construction started in October 2004 and ended on or around February 27, 2005.  After the project was completed, General Manager of the Broadcasting Corporation of Niue, Patrick Lino, said that signal tests had been conducted in villages who previously had difficulty getting acceptable TV and radio reception and they now had excellent signals. However, due to faulty materials, the equipment later corroded, necessitating repair. The Chinese Government financed the Seikena Tower Repair Project (as captured via Project ID#39307).

Title: China donates AUD 2,250 to Government of Kiribati for prioritization retreat
Description: In 2021, the Government of China donated AUD 2,250 to Government of Kiribati for a government prioritization retreat. A similar project took place in 2021 (see project ID#97314).

Title: China Eximbank provides $143.9 million preferential buyer’s credit for Second Stage of Phase 1 of the Dushanbe-Dangara Road Reconstruction Project (Linked to Project ID#40063, #40440)
Description: On November 27, 2010, China Eximbank and the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Tajikistan signed a $143,925,000 preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement [China Eximbank PBC NO.2010 (025) Total No. (132)] for the Second Stage of the Phase 1 of the Dushanbe-Dangara Road Reconstruction Project. The loan carried the following borrowing terms: an interest rate of 2%, a maturity of 20 years, and a grace period of 5 years. The total project cost was $151,500,000, including a contribution of $7,575,000 from the Government of Tajikistan.   The project, which was implemented in the design and construction contracting mode, involved road reconstruction, municipal road engineering, tunnels and connecting lines, etc. More specifically, the project supported the reconstruction of a 50.5 km road segment along the 147.64 km Dushanbe-Vahdat-Dangara section of the Dushanbe-Kulma highway (which is also known as the Tajikistan-China highway). It also supported the construction of the 4.43 km Chormagzak Tunnel along the 147.64 km Dushanbe-Dangara section of the Dushanbe-Kulma highway. The road repair project construction period was originally expected to last 24 months, and the tunnel and connection line construction period was originally expected to last 36 months (October 15, 2013).   China Road & Bridge Corporation was awarded the implementation contract.  Construction began on October 15, 2010, and ths project was completed (after passing final inspection) on October 30, 2013.

Title: China sends expert to Eritrea for instruction on demining
Description: From 2001 to 2003, China sent two groups of experts to Eritrea for training and on-site instruction on demining. 60 Eritrean deminers were trained, who cleared at least 103,000 sq meters of minefields and removed at least 587 mines and other unexploded ordnance. See ID# 12946

Title: China Donates 200 Computers to the Tanzania Road Agency
Description: On October 24, 2008, the Chinese government donated 200 computers to the Tanzanian National Roads agency. The donation was handed over by Ambassador Xinsheng Liu. The value for this project is yet unknown.

Title: Chinese Government donated $6,450,000 equipment and supplies for the Third International Conference on Small Islands Developing States (Linked to Project #64876)
Description: In 2014, the Chinese Government donated of equipment and supplies (worth $6,450,000) for the Third International Conference on Small Islands Developing States which was hosted by Samoa. China provided materials of the conference including 15 buses, 20 sedans, communication and information devices, simultaneous interpretation equipment, generators, furniture, office equipment, and water tanks. The handover ceremony was held on May 2nd, 2014 by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade._x000D_ _x000D_ In addition, China sent 16 engineers and technicians to assist with installing these devices (See Project #64876). China National Agricultural Development Group Co., Ltd was the project implementer. This project was located in Apia, Samoa. Later in 2016, the tents and materials provided by the Chinese government for the 2014 SIDS Conference were used as emergency supplies after a fire destroyed the Savalalo Flea Market (See Project #64866).

Title: China donates $1m in office and sports equipment to Afghan government (Linked to Project ID#34515)
Description: On 5 October, 2004, the Chinese government donated office equipment and recreational materials to Afghanistan's transitional government. This included 400 computers, 300 printers, TV sets, digital cameras, footballs, volleyballs and other athletic equipment. This donation was worth $1m.  Chinese Ambassador to Afghanistan Sun Yuxi and Afghan Foreign Minister A. Abdulla signed the notes of exchange. _x000D_ _x000D_ This is the fourth largest donation made by China; in June 2004, China had just donated communication equipment and vehicles to the Afghan government (See Project ID#34515)_x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese government donated two satellite dishes to Samoa
Description: In 2006, the Chinese Government donated two satellite dishes to the Government of Samoa.

Title: China donates Radio Units to Liberia
Description: On November 19, 2008, Chinese Ambassador Zhou Yuxiao donated 500 radio units to Liberia, on behalf of the Chinese government. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD 30,000 to the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs in June 2020
Description: In June 2020, Chinese government provides USD 30,000 to the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs for unspecified purpose.

Title: Chinese Government provides $604,000 grant to support humanitarian activities
Description: On April 23, 2001, as a result of talks between Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko and Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Beijing, the Chinese Government and the Government of Belarus signed an exchange of letters, which committed $604,000 of grant assistance to support unspecified humanitarian activities.

Title: China Ocean Shipping Company donates 10 million RMB to tsunami affected countries
Description: On January 5, 2005, the China Ocean Shipping Company donated 10 million yuan (US$1.2 million) to China Red Cross Society to assist countries affected by the December 26, 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD $2.5 million grant for landmine clearance in Cambodia
Description: On July 20, 2021, the Chinese Government provided a USD $2.5 million grant to the Government of Cambodia for landmine and ERW clearance support in 2022. The clearance project is expected to clear more than 1,700 hectares of land from landmines, and boost education activities to raise mine risk awareness in various Cambodia provinces. Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Stung Treng, Siem Reap and Kampong Thom are the targeted provinces for these clearance activities.  A handover ceremony was held for this grant provision. Heng Ratana, Director General of the Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC), made the donation of the Chinese-funded grant.

Title: Chinese Government provides $1.7 million grant for provision of conservation and wildlife protection equipment to Botswana Wildlife Authority
Description: On July 15, 2015, the Chinese government and Botswana Ministry of Environment, Wildlife and Tourism jointly announced a donation of $1.7 million worth of goods from the Chinese government for wildlife protection._x000D_ _x000D_ On January 27, 2016, Zheng Zhuqiang, the Chinese Ambassador to Botswana, officially gave the Botswana Ministry of Environment, Wildlife, and Tourism $1.7 million USD worth of wildlife protection equipment including generators, solar panels, sleeping bags, GPS computers, and uniforms on behalf of the Chinese government. The equipment donation serves as help for the wildlife ministry due to its limited financial capacity and difficulty implementing anti-poaching projects. Tshekedi Khama, the Minister of Wildlife, Environment and Tourism thanked China for the donations. The donation appears to have been completed.

Title: China provides 5 million RMB grant to Mongolian provinces because of severe winter
Description: On February 26, 2003, Ambassador Huang Jiakui of China met the chairman of the State Emergency Commission, Defense Minister J. Gurragchaa, and informed him that China decided to grant 5 million Yuan of aid to the Bulgan, Hovsgol, Tov and Selenge provinces suffering from the severe winter.

Title: China provides $21 million in disaster relief materials to Nepalese army
Description: Around October 12, 2019, China signed an agreement to provide the Nepal army with about $21 million in unspecified disaster relief materials over the next three years, as Beijing strengthens its ties with Kathmandu. The agreement on disaster relief was signed by Nepali defense minister Ishwar Pokharel and his counterpart Wei Fenghe, as a part of Xi Jinping's visit to Nepal.

Title: Chinese embassy grants 1 million kwacha to Bingu Seniors Foundation
Description: On January 11, 2010, the Chinese embassy granted 1 million kwacha to the Bingu Seniors Foundation in Malawi. The exact use of the funding is unknown.

Title: China gives 163,000 NZD in Aid to Niue After 2004 Tropical Cyclone Heta
Description: Following the 2004 Cyclone Heta, China contributed 163,000 NZD in relief aid.

Title: China donates $50,000 for flood relief in the Philippines after typhoons Violeta and Unding
Description: On November 26 2004, the Chinese Government donated $50,000 USD to the Philippines after Typhoon Violeta and Typhoon Unding triggered floods in the northern parts of the country.

Title: China provides 50 million RMB interest-free loan to Kenya for resettlement of refugees (linked to #19014)
Description: On May 15, 2008, the Chinese Government offered Kenya an interest-free loan of 50 million yuan to help resettle hundreds of thousands of villagers uprooted by political turmoil following Kenyan elections. The project is linked to a 200 million shillings grant of the same nature (Project #19014).

Title: Chinese Embassy in Pakistan donates PKR 1 million for IDPs
Description: The staff of Chinese Embassy in Pakistan donated three-day salaries equivalent to one million rupees to the internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the shape of relief items. This was stated by a three-member delegation, headed by Chinese Ambassador Luo Zhaohui, in a meeting with Minister of States and Frontiers Regions (SAFRON) Najamuddin Khan._x000D_ _x000D_

Title: Chinese Embassy in Uganda donates 13 million Ugandan Shillings worth of relief items to victims of landslides in Eastern District of Bududa in 2018
Description: On October 15, 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Uganda donated cash and emergency relief items to the victims of landslides that struck the eastern district of Bududa. The donations were said to be worth about 13 million Ugandan shillings.   The landslides that left at least 46 people dead and 700 others affected occurred on Oct. 11 in Bukalasi and Buwali sub-counties. Hillary Onek, Minister of Relief, Disaster Preparedness and Refugees received the donation. The Chamber of Chinese Enterprises in Uganda donates 100 million Ugandan shillings worth of relief items and the Embassy also donated equipment as well.

Title: Chinese Government pledges RMB 15 million grant for Syrian refugees living in Jordan
Description: On August 23, 2012, the Government of China made a commitment to grant the Government of Jordan CN¥15,000,000 for refugee relief. The aid was intended to respond to civil unrest in Syria and provide emergency humanitarian aid to Syrian refugees in Jordan and Lebanon. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) reported that China's contribution remains in the commitment phase. This project is captured by UNOCHA flow #97525._x000D_ _x000D_ The 15 million RMB donation to Lebanon is captured in project ID #41523.

Title: Chinese Government provides USD 50,000 for specially designated contributions to United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs in July 2020
Description: In July 2020, Chinese government provides USD 50,000 as specially designated contributions to United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

Title: Chinese Embassy provides emergency grant assistance to the Druze Church
Description: On February 3, 2016, the Chinese Embassy in Syria signed a handover certificate for the donation of emergency aid to the Druze Church in the state of Jabal al-Druze. The aid included quilts, blankets, and other materials.   The Druze community of Syria is believed to constitute an estimated 3.2 percent of the Syria population (as of 2010), or approximately 700,000 persons including the Golan Heights. The Druze are concentrated in the rural, mountainous areas east and south of Damascus in the area known officially as Jabal al-Druze. Druze Church has played an important role in local refugee resettlement and humanitarian relief activities.

Title: Chinese Embassy contributes to donation of $64,094 to terrorist attack survivors at Moi University
Description: In April 2015, the Chinese Embassy handed over a donation of $64,094 (6 million Kenyan shillings) to survivors of a terrorist attack at Moi University's Garissa campus in Kenya. According to the announcement, the donation was from multiple organizations, including the Kenya China Economic and Trade Association, the Kenya Chinese and Overseas Chinese Association, the East Africa China Chamber of Commerce, the Chinese Embassy in Kenya, and Ambassador Liu Xianfa.

Title: China Trust Fund provides $400,000 USD grant for the Support for the Revision of National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans in Central Asian Countries Project
Description: On 14 December 2012, China’s Ministry of Environmental Protection (China MEP) and the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) signed a framework agreement on strategic cooperation. This agreement involved China MEP committing $2 million annually to the China Trust Fund which focuses on environmental protection in African, ASEAN, and Central Asian countries.  According to a 2017 Final Report from UNEP, $300,000 USD from China Trust Fund was allocated towards the Support for the Revision of National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans in Central Asian Countries Project (T2-P5) (p. 4). The project was completed in May 2016.
Funding_Agencies: China Ministry of Ecology and Environment

Title: China grants a batch of arborvitae seeds to Tirana
Description: On November 29, 2009, Tirana municipal government of Beijing city government donated a batch of arborvitae trees planted to hold the ceremony, Ambassador Wang Junling and Tirana Mayor Rama attended the ceremony and personally planted an arborvitae. In order to express its friendship with the people of Tirana and celebrate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, Beijing this year presented these arborvitae to Tirana._x000D_

Title: Chinese Government provides RMB 25 million grant for provision of mobile scanning devices to combat drug and arms trafficking
Description: On February 5, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Uzbekistan signed letters of exchange for on a grant of RMB 25 million (3.7 million USD) for the provision of mobile x-ray (customs inspection) equipment to prevent smuggling and boost trade. The RMB 25 million grant was drawn from the proceeds of an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) that was signed on August 23, 2006. The grant agreement was finalized and signed by both parties on April 2, 2009. The purpose of the grant was to equip customs posts (border checkpoints) with mobile scanning equipment to combat smuggling, drug trafficking, and arms trafficking. No additional implementation details are available.

Title: China donates 20 million yuan of supplies to Sri Lanka
Description: In 2014, after the flood, China donated supplies that worth 20 million yuan to Sri Lanka.

Title: China grants Myanmar 40 million yuan for Mekong River Security Cooperation Project
Description: In 2012, China committed 40 million yuan for the Security Cooperation Project for the Mekong River. The two countries signed an agreement under the Economic and Technical Cooperation. Start and end dates are as claimed by original source.

Title: Chinese government donates office supplies to government of Central African Republic
Description: On November 24 and December 3, 2008, the Chargé d’affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Central Africa, Gu Zhengyou, and the Chinese-African Minister of Planning, Economics, and International Cooperation Malico signed exchange letters to provide material assistance to the Conference of Heads of State of the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (CEMAC) held in 2009. On September 4, 2009, the Chinese government donated office supplies to the Central African Republic Ministry of Planning, Economy, and International Cooperation. The donation consisted of 480 chairs, 12 splits, 4 computers with accessories, 3 leather lounges, a presidential office, and flags in the colors of CEMAC states, and was valued at 180 million CFA Francs.

Title: Chinese Government grants$74,000 for the provision of office supplies to Uganda's ruling political party
Description: On September 1, 2009, the Chinese Government gave a $74,000 grant to the Government of Uganda for the provision of office supplies to the country's ruling party - the National Resistance Movement (NRM).

Title: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides RMB 20 million grant for police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers
Description: In 2013, the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China provided a grant worth RMB 20 million to the Government of Tajikistan for the provision of police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers to Tajikistan’s Ministry of the Interior, Narcotics Administration and National Security Commission. The police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers were officially delivered to the local authorities on or around November 21, 2013.

Title: China will Send 4 Youth Volunteers to Cambodia
Description: On March 19 2007, China signed an agreement with Cambodia to send 4 youth volunteers to Cambodia to help improve the government's computer and agricultural technology services. They will provide services for computers and agricultural technology as well as mentor students of advanced technology. Their service period is one year from the arrival date._x000D_ _x000D_ The agreement aims to enhance the mutual understanding and friendship between the youths of China and Cambodia and promote exchange in all fields between the two sides. Such an exchange is reported to speed up economic and social development in Cambodia and improve living standards.

Title: Chinese Government donates 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service
Description: On August 21, 2019, Chinese ambassador Song Yumin formally presented a gift of 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) at the Policy Academy in St. James, Port of Spain. The donation was originally announced on May 14, 2019. The motorcycles are equipped with GPS and camera technology, and the Prime Minister hopes that they will reduce the response time of the TTPS and give citizens a greater sense of security.

Title: China donates 370 computers worth 456 million CFA Franc to Guinea-Bissau
Description: China offered the Guinea Bissau government 370 computers worth 456 million CFA Francs (about $800,000), a statement from the Chinese Embassy in Bissau said on Feb 3. The donation was handed to Guinea Bissau's Prime Minister Domingos Simoes Pereira by China's Ambassador Wang Hua. The official said, the aid will help improve the operational capacity of Guinea Bissau's public institutions.

Title: Cameroon Parliament receives 70 million CFA of Equipment from China
Description: The President of the National Assembly of Cameroon traveled to China December 10th-16th of 2009 and received 70 million FCFA of equipment from China for the Parliament of Cameroon. The donation was completed in 2009.

Title: China donates computers and printers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
Description: On October 22, 2013 Chinese Ambassador Zhao Jianhua handed over 20 computers and 20 printers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia computer lab on behalf of the Chinese government. Ambassador Zhao presented the electronics to Foreign Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan at the Chinese Embassy in Congo Town. The computers were donated in the hopes that it will make the Ministry more efficient in conducting business and will increase the computer skills of the Ministry workers.

Title: Chinese government sends 18th peacekeeping mission to DRC
Description: On December 16 2014, the peacekeepers in the 18th Peacekeeping mission arrived in the DRC. The 218 peacekeepers in total came from the engineering unit and medical unit. The peacekeeping mission is likely supporting the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo or MONUSCO. The mission will reportedly last for 8 months.

Title: China deploys 14th team of peacekeeping police in Timor-Leste
Description: China's 14th peacekeeping squad to Timor Leste arrived in 2009. The 21-person squad was sent to work with the UN mission in East Timor for one year, setting the end date to be in February 2010. Seven out of the 21 members had previously participated in UN peacekeeping missions. The squad, which includes staff from the criminal investigation, public security, traffic and entry and exit sections in the southeastern Jiangxi Province, all passed strict exams in the regional situation, world affairs, international law, driving, first aid, and English.

Title: Chinese Government provides $10,000 grant for retrieval and saving of Grenadian historical documents
Description: According to internal records that the Government of Grenada shared with AidData in June 2018, the Chinese Government provided a $10,000 grant to the Government of Grenada in 2014 for the retrieval and saving of Grenadian historical documents.

Title: Chinese Government provides $5 million loan to strengthen the falling value of PNG’s local currency (Linked to Project ID#43082)
Description: On March 20 2000, in a meeting with Chinese Ambassador to PNG, Zhao Zhenyu, PNG Prime Minister Sir Mekere Morauta thanked the Chinese Government for providing a $5 million loan (captured in this project) and a $5 million grant (captured via Project ID#43082) to strengthen the falling value of PNG’s local currency (the kina).

Title: China sends 15th peacekeeping team to Sudan
Description: On December 11, 2018, a group of 100 Chinese Peacekeepers left for Darfur, Sudan for a year-long peacekeeping mission. This is the first group of the 225-member peace-keeping force team, with the second group leaving on December 18 for Darfur. Together, the 225-member team is the 15th batch of peacekeepers that China has sent to the Darfur region. The team will be tasked with maintaining supplies, engineering projects, renovating buildings, and constructing/repairing homes, roads, and airports.  On December 4, 2019, the United Nations Peacekeeping Strategic Partnership Office evaluated the 15th Chinese peacekeeping team, and the team passed the evaluation with high standards.  On August 13, 2020, a group of 115 members from the 15th peacekeeping team successfully completed their 20-month mission and returned to China. During their mission, the peacekeeping team has successively completed the infrastructure construction of the Gloria Temporary Operation Base of UNIFIL, the clearing and remediation and transfer of 10 camps, the upgrade of the El Fasher super camp, etc. All 225 members were awarded the United Nations "Peace Medal of Honor" in July 2020.

Title: Chinese government announces 301 million RMB grant to the Government of Malawi (linked to #58442 and #58443)
Description: On December 12, 2017, at the 10 year celebration of diplomatic relations between China and Malawi, the Chinese Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Chen Xiadong announced a 301 million RMB grant to the Government of Malawi.  1 million RMB was specifically earmarked for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (project #58443). It is unclear whether the funds were actually disbursed.

Title: Chinese Government donates equipment worth $4.78 million for Public Security Video Surveillance System Project
Description: In July 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Uruguay began negotiations on a possible donation of video surveillance equipment. Then, in April 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Uruguay’s Ministry of Interior signed an exchange of notes regarding a donation of video surveillance equipment in support of the Public Security Video Surveillance System Project.   The monetary value of the donation from China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) was $4,780,000. The donation of 4000 pieces of equipment included 1,900 fixed video surveillance cameras and 200 dome (PTZ) units with aimable cameras (built by Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.), ethernet switches, video wall controllers, video management servers, and network equipment. The equipment was intended for use by the Government of Uruguay to more effectively monitor and control its borders between Argentina and Brazil.   The equipment was earmarked for installation in 374 sites across the Rivera, Artigas, Cerro Largo and Rocha departments. Each department has its own Monitoring Center and the video surveillance system enables real-time monitoring of imagery from a Unified Command Center in Montevideo. The donated equipment arrived in Uruguay in January 2019 and an equipment handover ceremony was held on February 28, 2019. Equipment installation activities began in December 2018 and they were originally expected to reach completion in September 2019.

Title: China grants $100,000 to the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) for unspecified purposes
Description: On November 27, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti, Fu Huaqiang, handed over a a $100,000 donation to the Executive Secretary of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), Mahboub Maalim. According to the Ambassador, the donation is for IGAD "allocate and use these funds on the basis of its priority needs."

Title: $150,000 Demarcation of Ethiopia-Sudan border
Description: In 2005, the Chinese ambassador to Ethiopia Lin Lin presented Konjit Senegiorgis, director general of African affairs with Ethiopia's Foreign Ministry, with a check of $150,000 for the demarcation of the Ethiopia-Sudan border. By May 4, 2010, 80% of the border demarcation had been completed, according to the Sudanese foreign minister, Deng Alor.The final status of the project is uncertain.

Title: China donates 50 Saloon cars to Sudanese president's office
Description: On December 26, 2011, and January 5, 2012, Chinese and Sudanese officials signed an exchange of letters announcing China's intention to donate 50 cars to the government of Sudan, according to the Chinese Ministry of Commerce. BBC reported that on April 1st, 2012, a contract for donating 50 saloon (sedan) vehicles by China to Sudan's Presidency of the Republic was officially signed. The signing ceremony was attended by the minister at the Presidency of the Republic, Gen Bakri Hasan Salih, the minister at the Ministry of Cooperation, Ishraqah Mahmud, the undersecretary of the Ministry of Finance and the ambassador of China to Sudan._x000D_ _x000D_ The value of the cars is unknown.

Title: Chinese Government agrees to send a team to train the Ugandan police in December 2017
Description: On December 20, 2017, during a meeting between the Inspector General of Police, Kale Kayihura, and a delegation of the China Public Security, the Chinese Government agreed to send a team to Uganda to train the Uganda police in areas of criminal investigations, crime intelligence, and cybercrime. The decision was made after two Chinese nationals were murdered in Uganda.

Title: China donates 153 computers to the National Directorate of Public Defenders
Description: In September 2009, China donated 153 computers to the National Directorate of Public Defenders (Dirección Nacional de Defensorías Públicas), which is the institution that offers judicial assistance to citizens. According an August 2010 articles from China's Economic and Commercial Counsellor's Office in Uruguay, the computers had all been put to use._x000D_

Title: Chinese Embassy donates cash to the Seychelles National Youth Assembly (SNYA)
Description: In September 2018, the Chinese Embassy in Seychelles made a monetary donation to the Seychelles National Youth Assembly (SNYA). Further details are unknown.

Title: China Eximbank provides RMB 246.1 million government concessional loan for MOI acquisition of cars, patrol boats, police vehicles and helicopters (Linked to Project ID#98029, 96221)
Description: On March 11, 2015, the Parliament of Myanmar approved a government proposal to accept a RMB 246,149,000 ($39 million) government concessional loan (GCL) from China Eximbank for the Ministry of Interior to purchase 985 cars, patrol boats, vehicles, and helicopters for the country's police force. The GCL agreement, which was signed by China Eximbank and the Government of Myanmar on August 28, 2015, carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 5 year grace period, a 4.5% interest rate, a 0.4% commitment fee, and a 0.4% management fee. China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation (CATIC) is the contractor responsible for implementation. The Ministry of Interior (Home Affairs) had received 8 vehicles from CATIC by December 2015. This equipment acquisition project is part of a larger police force upgrading project (警察部队升级项目) and it was designed to address an equipment shortage causing problems in the police force.  There are some indications that the China Eximbank loan for the acquisition of 985 cars, patrol boats, vehicles, and helicopters for the country's police forcea may have financially underperformed vis-a-vis the original expectations of the lender. In 2020, China Eximbank and the Government of Myanmar signed a debt suspension agreement as part of the G-20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI). Under the terms of the agreement, the lender agreed to suspend principal and interest payments due between May 1, 2020 and December 31, 2020 under 3 buyer’s credit loan (BCL) agreements, 6 government concessional loan (GCL) agreements, and 27 preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreements (as captured via Project ID#98029).  Debt service payments under many of these loan agreements were again deferred in 2021 (as captured via Project ID#96221).

Title: Chinese Ministry of National Defense donates humanitarian equipment worth $7.5 million USD to Uruguay's Ministry of National Defense
Description: On October 24, 2016, China's Ministry of National Defense signed an agreement with the Ministry of National Defense of Uruguay in which the Chinese side committed to the provision of equipment worth about $7.5 million USD to Uruguay. Under these agreements, Uruguay was to receive $2.5 million USD of equipment in mid-January 2017, and another $5 million USD by the end of 2017.  On February 2, 2017, the Chinese Ministry of National Defense provided equipment worth $2.5 million USD. The equipment consisted of 10 winter tents for 12 people, 400 summer tents for 20 people, 2,000 field cots, seven field kitchens, 14 electric power generators, seven water trailers, and four command posts/mobile housing vehicles that could serve as ambulance. The equipment was to be delivered to each of the 4 National Army divisions. The equipment was expected to help in emergencies ("Donación de la República Popular China al MDN").  The remaining $5 million USD of equipment was handed over in a ceremony on March 23, 2018. The equipment includes 10 off-road ambulances, six 42-seat buses, three motor graders, 10 loaders, four bulldozers, and one-year's worth of spare parts. The equipment was destined for use as prison guard transportation and road work equipment by the National Army of Uruguay.

Title: Chinese Government cancels RMB 50 million of the Government of Angola’s outstanding obligations (linked to #73825)
Description: On 27 December 2007, the Chinese Government and the Government of Angola signed a debt exemption protocol cancelling RMB 50 million (approximately $7 million) of outstanding debt for the Government of Angola owed to the Chinese Government. The Chinese Ambassador to Angola, Zhang Beisan, and the Angolan Minister of Exterior Relations, Manuel Gomes dos Santos, represented their respective governments at the signing ceremony for the agreement.  In January 2009, China’s Minister of Commerce Chen Yuan announced that the Chinese Government had cumulatively cancelled RMB 67.38 million of the Government of Angola’s outstanding debt obligations, so the remaining debt forgiveness equal to RMB 17.38 million is captured in linked Project #73825.

Title: China donates $15 million to Guinea-Bissau in 2016
Description: In 2016, China donated $15 million to Guinea-Bissau for unspecified projects. The funds were given to Guinea-Bissau on the basis of solidarity and an act of China's efforts to strengthen ties with Portuguese-speaking African nations.

Title: China grants Eritrea 2 million USD
Description: On May 6, 2003, Eritrean Economic Advisor Dr. Woldai Futur and Chinese Ambassador to Eritrea Chen Zhanfu signed a $2 million aid agreement. Further details are unknown.

Title: Chinese Government provides $3.6 million USD interest-free loan to Sudan in July 2005
Description: On 20 July 2005, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sudan signed a $3.6 million USD loan agreement for unspecified purposes. The loan carried a 0% interest rate, a 10-year maturity, and no grace period.  The Chinese Government institution that provided the loan is unknown, but it was likely China’s Ministry of Commerce. It is unclear whether these funds were ever disbursed.

Title: Chinese Government cancels GBP 27 million of the Government of Myanmar’s outstanding obligations (Linked to Project ID#67509)
Description: On January 14, 2003, the Chinese Government and the Government of Myanmar signed a partial debt exemption protocol, which cancelled the Government of Myanmar’s outstanding obligations under two interest-free loans that it previously contracted: an interest-free loan worth RMB 100 million that the two governments signed on June 12, 1979 (as captured via Project ID#67509) and a loan worth GBP 27 million that the two governments signed on January 9, 1961 (as captured via Project ID#67508).

Title: Chinese Government cancels RMB 32 million of the Government of Mauritius’ outstanding debt obligations (Linked to Project ID#67620)
Description: In March 2021, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritius signed a debt forgiveness agreement (‘partial debt remittance protocol’). China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) agreed to agreed to cancel RMB 32 million of the Government of Mauritius’ outstanding debt obligations. These obligations resulted from an RMB 40 million interest-free loan that the Government of Mauritius had contracted in late 2008 or early 2009 for the New Operation Theaters and Ward Blocks at Victoria Hospital Project (as captured via Project ID#67620). As of December 31, 2020, the Government of Mauritius had made an RMB 8 million repayment on the RMB 40 million loan (with a final maturity date of December 31, 2028). Therefore, MOFCOM waived the Government of Mauritius’ obligation to repay the loan’s outstanding amount (RMB 32 million).

Title: Chinese Government cancels VUV 407 million of the Government of Vanuatu’s outstanding obligations
Description: In 2005, the Chinese Government cancelled VUV 407 million of the Government of Vanuatu’s outstanding debt obligations related to one or more loans that it had previously contracted.

Title: Chinese Government cancels $13 million of the Government of CAR’s outstanding debt obligations in 2021
Description: On January 22, 2021, the Chinese Government and the Government of the Central African Republic (CAR) signed a debt forgiveness agreement. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) agreed to agreed to cancel $13 million of the Government of CAR’s’ outstanding debt obligations. These obligations resulted from one or more interest-free loans that the Government of CAR previously contracted, which were scheduled to mature before December 31, 2020.
